News.title: Manchester United hounded off pitch by own fans
News.content:
The joke goes that Michael Carrick has already bettered Ruben Amorim’s efforts by reaching the third round of the League Cup, but Manchester United will need to find a way past free-flowing Brighton if they are to go any further.

United were eliminated in the second round by League Two Grimsby Town last season, but start the competition a stage later because they are one of nine Premier League clubs playing in European competition.

Brighton knocked United out of the FA Cup in the third round, with Danny Welbeck scoring at Old Trafford, meaning the club played just 40 matches in 2025-26.

Carrick will want to make a better fist of the cup competitions, but he could really use a win of any kind after taking just four points from United’s first four league games of the new season.

The no-show at Hull and derby defeat by City’s 10 men were especially dispiriting, and the relationship between the club and supporters is becoming increasingly strained.

There were no flags on the Stretford End for the game against City, as fans voiced their opposition to what they view as a heavy-handed ticketing policy. The club says the measures are to stop ticket-touting but critics believe many innocent season-ticket holders are being caught in the crossfire and having their tickets revoked.

Discontent is never too far away given the continued presence of the Glazer family, and confidence is fragile regarding the club’s sporting direction under Sir Jim Ratcliffe and Ineos.

The news that 15-year-old JJ Gabriel, possibly the country’s outstanding academy player in his year group, wants out (broken by Matt Law in a Telegraph Sport exclusive) nagged at some of those fears.



Gabriel could have been in contention for a place on the bench this evening, but that is now surely out of the question even if United say they have not given up hope of persuading him to stay.



Full team news on the way shortly.

News.title: Spurs finally score... but still lose
News.content:
“But that is why we cannot say it does not work for anyone. There are players who play every three days with no issues. They are very robust, their performances do not change too much. There are other players where the risk is bigger and the performances are different. I have to learn who is ready to play games every three days and who needs a rest so their performance level is not affected. I thought I had it quite clear in my mind with some, but with others, it is new, even for them, because they have not played as many games. We are learning.”

Liverpool were knocked out in the fourth round of this competition last season, losing 3-0 at home against Crystal Palace. Joe Gomez returns to the squad for the hosts tonight after an injury early in pre-season but Giovanni Leoni, Hugo Ekitike, Conor Bradley and Federico Chiesa remain out.

Tottenham are still without a league win or goal this season. Their 0-0 draw at home against Everton Saturday means they sit just above the relegation zone. Tottenham overcame Charlton in the second round, convincingly winning 5-1 at the Tottenham Hotspur Stadium last month.

“I think we are working well,” Tottenham boss Roberto De Zerbi said. “We played 30 minutes, 25 minutes very well [against Everton]. In that moment we could score two goals. Then we lost maybe the confidence because we did not score. For sure we have to improve. For sure I have big confidence in my players, they are very good players.

“We have to improve, yes. We can say the coach has responsibility if we do not score, yes, I accept, no problem. We did not win any game so far, yes. We are disappointed, sorry for that. But we have other positive things, like I said we did not [concede goals] in the last two games and the things we have to improve, we start our work. Nothing changed in my project and my idea.”

News.title: England cruise to victory led by ‘absolute freak’ Brook
News.content:
Whatever his returns, there has been an extra focus to Brook’s approach this summer, possibly because he has learnt from a grievous indiscretion in Wellington last winter. While others chase the Indian Premier League, he is totally committed to England, taking his break while that tournament is on and playing every match in all formats for his country.

Brook had come to the crease at the fall of the first wicket and, while it is early days, England appear to have added another arrow to their quiver. They handed a debut to opener Aneurin Donald, with his cap presented in the pre-match huddle by Pietersen, the new “specialist mentor”.

Donald has been selected as an “intent merchant”, charged with going extremely hard from the first over, aping Phil Salt, who is missing with a quad injury. He did what he was asked to do, smearing his first ball for two, then pulling six to leg and hammering four through the offside before the first over was out. Another big shot, off Wellalage, in the second saw him well caught in the deep, but 12 off five had kickstarted the innings.

News.title: Max Dowman-mania could make League Cup hottest ticket in town
News.content:
At this rate, Arsenal supporters will be looking forward to Carabao Cup matches as eagerly as any Premier League or Champions League game, simply because it will be a chance to watch Dowman again. The forward’s age and inexperience means he is still used sparingly in those high-priority competitions. The League Cup, by contrast, may prove to be his domain over the coming months.

Dowman’s double at Portman Road made him just the second 16-year-old to score two goals in a game for a Premier League side. The first was Wayne Rooney, for Everton against Wrexham in 2002.

The two goals underlined why there is so much excitement around Dowman. The first was a demonstration of his prodigious dribbling ability, as he weaved through Ipswich’s defence and buried his shot with the weaker right foot. The second showed his composure: a slotted finish, rolled in with ease.

News.title: UK borrowing costs hit 19-year high as global bond rout intensifies
News.content:
The cost of UK government borrowing hit its highest level since 2007 in a fresh global debt sell-off.

The yield on 10-year gilts, a benchmark for what the Treasury pays to borrow money, rose from 5.37pc to a fresh 19-year high of 5.41pc on Tuesday as rising oil prices risk reigniting inflation.

Mortgage experts have warned that residential and buy-to-let mortgage rates are set to climb towards 5pc, as market turmoil threatens to filter through to household finances.

Short-term debt costs have also jumped, with the yield on two-year UK bonds surpassing 4.9pc for the first time in three years.

The bond chaos came as Andy Haldane, a former Bank of England chief economist, warned that Labour risked becoming “just a traditional tax and spend socialist government with better TikTok videos”.

He told LBC that John Healey’s original plan for a “low drama budget” had been “torpedoed” by higher borrowing costs and “events over the last couple of weeks”.

He said: “I think that [the bond market turmoil] will mean some hard choices next month at the Budget.”

“Few hard choices so far, but one is looming on the horizon, how any hole to the budget headroom is made good on. Is that a question of tax rises, or is it a question of taking the knife to public spending.”

Mr Haldane has been advising Labour since Andy Burnham took power.

It comes as the US Federal Reserve and the Bank of England face pressure to raise interest rates this week to combat rising prices.

Anthony Brinkman, a portfolio manager at Principal Asset Management, said: “The recent gilt market movements seem to be intent on showing central banks they are out of time – the market is expecting action.”

Borrowing costs around the world are rising after a 20pc surge in oil prices so far this month.

Brent crude tipped above $109 a barrel this week after Houthi rebels in Yemen, considered a proxy for Iran’s forces, seized control of a key port in the Red Sea, threatening shipping.

The US Federal Reserve is expected to raise interest rates on Wednesday in the face of the inflation threat.

As a result, the yield on 10-year US Treasury bonds has surged above 5pc for the first time since 2007.

News.title: AI could transform global inequalities or ‘widen the gap’, warns Bill Gates
News.content:
“AI could be a great equaliser, or [it could] widen the gap”, says Mr Gates. “This is not a long-range prediction. It’s a present-tense choice”.

“We can harness AI for good. But it won’t happen by accident. After all, the market is an extraordinary engine of innovation, but a terrible guarantor of equal opportunity.

“With AI, the gap could grow even faster … That is what makes this moment so urgent. Things are changing rapidly, and the window to shape who benefits from AI, and how soon, is short”.

The key issue holding back the deployment of AI in the developing world revolves around the availability of local data and, in turn, the ability for the technology to scale in environments very different from where it is currently being created.

An app that is trained on billions of hours of American English, will struggle at first with British English (see your spell check) but is next to useless if your local language is Swahili or Chichewa.

More profoundly, an AI tool that allows a farmer in Hampshire to control his combine harvester remotely, will offer little to a smallholder in South Sudan who works the land by hand and faces a completely different array of pests, weather conditions and costs.

The same is true for health. “A community health worker in Rwanda examining a baby with a fever faces different questions than a clinician in a well-resourced hospital - and the AI supporting her needs to reflect that”, says Mr Gates.

He adds: “Most of the world is invisible to today’s AI models. These AI systems were trained primarily on what exists on the internet – and the internet reflects a deeply unequal world. More than 90 percent of the data used to train early, large language models came from English-language sources. The communities that stand the most to gain from AI are largely absent from the knowledge base these tools are built on. They are not just underserved. They are not in the picture at all”.

The new investment aims to help correct that. Mark Suzman, CEO of the Gates Foundation, says investments are already being made with companies including Microsoft and Google to build databases of a much wider range of languages, for instance.

Africa alone has more than 2,000 languages, and for AI’s to be effective there they have to understand what and how people actually speak - “their dialects, accents, and slang, too”.

The investments, he says, are being made on the condition that the intelligence and knowledge they accumulate are made freely available for others to use.

Languages for AI “are true public goods, almost definitional public goods. They need to be freely available to everybody. Once they’re created, they are public goods that can be uploaded onto any AI,” said Mr Suzman.

News.title: Reynolds refuses four times to rule out tax raid on state pensioners
News.content:
The Business Secretary refused four times to rule out retirees paying tax on the state pension from next year.

Jonathan Reynolds declined to reassure pensioners that they would not pay income tax on the benefit for the first time, saying it was a question for the Chancellor.

The comments on Tuesday raised concern for millions of retired people expecting to see their state pension surpass £13,000 from April, forcing them to pay income tax.

However, pensions minister Torsten Bell later insisted Labour would not put up taxes on people who rely on the state pension.

It is still unclear how this will be implemented given the complexity of separating the tax arrangements of different groups of pensioners.

The rise under the triple lock guarantee would drag many pensioners into paying income tax for the first time because their state income would surpass the personal allowance of £12,570.

Rachel Reeves, the former chancellor, said last year that people solely reliant on the state pension would not have to pay the tax.

However, Mr Reynolds was repeatedly asked on BBC Breakfast whether Labour would honour this commitment after the next increase in the state pension in April. He declined to answer four times.

He said: “I’m sorry, that is for the Chancellor and for a Budget.

“The majority of pensioners in this country don’t just rely on the state pensions. Some do, I accept that, but the majority don’t.

“Sometimes when this is looked at, we’re focusing just on the state pension side of this. You’ve got to consider the full range of income retired people in the UK have.”

However Mr Bell, the pensions minister, walked back from Mr Reynolds comments.

He said: “In line with the commitment made at Budget 2025, pensioners who only just exceed the personal allowance will not have the administrative burden of paying small amounts of tax in this Parliament.

“The Chancellor will set out further details on how that commitment will be delivered at the Budget.”

Former pensions minister Sir Steve Webb said only one in 16 pensioners would benefit from this policy.

He said: “Those on the new state pension can expect to see an increase of nearly £500 per year next April.

“But the sting in the tail is that this will take the standard rate of the new state pension above the tax threshold.”

The comments came after official figures on Tuesday indicated the triple lock will rise by 3.9pc from April.

Under the triple lock, the state pension rises each April in line with inflation, average wages or 2.5pc, whichever is highest.

Total pay, including bonuses, rose by 3.9pc in the three months to July, down from 4.2pc in the three months to June.

Pensioners may yet receive a bigger increase if September’s inflation figure is higher than 3.9pc. That will be revealed next month but a higher figure is thought to be unlikely.

Sports.title: Kai Havertz named in Germany squad for HALF the international break as Jurgen Klopp adopts bizarre new approach
Sports.content:
Next

KAI HAVERTZ will feature in just HALF of Germany’s games during the international break in a boost to Mikel Arteta.

Arteta has lost players to injury while on international duty in recent seasons and will be buoyed to learn that the risk of that happening to Havertz is now halved.



New Germany boss Jurgen Klopp has adopted an unusual strategy for his first four games as national boss, choosing two different squads to split the load.

The first group will be available for the fixtures against the Netherlands in Amsterdam on September 24 and at home to Greece three days later in Augsburg.



The second group will be available for Germany’s matches against Serbia in Munich on October 1 and Greece in Thessaloniki on October 4.

Havertz, 27, has been chosen as part of the first group and should return to North London following Germany’s home fixture against Greece.



Arteta has heavily relied on Havertz to lead the line for Arsenal this season, with the former Chelsea ace starting every Premier League game so far.

He has notched goals against Chelsea and Coventry already and his reduced involvement during the international break should allow him an extended break ahead of Arsenal’s first game back against Leeds.

Klopp, who took the Germany job in the summer following Julian Nagelsmann‘s resignation, has named 44 different players in his squads as a result of his new techniques.

And the mammoth group means there is space for a first senior call-up for 16 players.

FREE agent Mauro Icardi could be set for a move to Tottenham as he continues the search for a Premier League goal.

The former Inter and Paris Saint-Germain striker left Galatasaray after a four-year stint with the Turkish giants.



And, according to Cronache di Spogliatoio, Roberto De Zerbi‘s Spurs are pondering a move for the 33-year-old after failing to score in their first FOUR Premier League games.

Spurs have conceded eight goals in the league this season, recording two losses and two draws as they lie 17th in the table.



Their Carabao Cup campaign kicked off with a promising 5-1 victory over Championship side Charlton, but they were knocked out in the third round by Liverpool on Tuesday.

The struggling side splashed out this summer, stacking up on the likes of £100million Sandro Tonali and £85m Mateus Fernandes.



And they even secured Manchester City’s Omar Marmoush on loan with a £60m obligation to buy – with the fee split into a £50m guaranteed payment, plus £10m in add-ons.

The Egypt international started in their goalless draw with Liverpool and provided more quality than recent games, still missing the needed class to finish.

He also made the starting XI against Newcastle and Nottingham Forest.



Dominic Solanke – who started against Charlton and Everton this season – has also not scored in his five appearances.

And an exiled Richarlison has not played since Spurs’ opening 3-0 defeat in late August.

The Brazilian will be stuck on the sidelines in N17 until at least January after his disastrous fall out with the Premier League side.

And De Zerbi will be hoping for reinforcements to drag his squad back to fighting form – even if a move to Icardi is unlikely.

Sports.title: What is Clearlake Capital and do they have full control over Chelsea after Todd Boehly sold ownership stake?
Sports.content:
Next

CHELSEA are going through a major change off the pitch involving owners Clearlake Capital.

SunSport can reveal exactly who this private firm is and what is going on behind the scenes.

What is Clearlake Capital?

Clearlake Capital Group is a major American private equity firm founded in 2006.



The firm was set up by billionaires Behdad Eghbali and Jose E Feliciano



It is headquartered in Santa Monica, California, and manages more than $185billion in assets.



Clearlake typically invests in technology, industrial and consumer sectors.

The firm is known for securing some of the private equity industry’s best financial returns 5.

In May 2022, Clearlake entered the sports world by leading a consortium to buy Chelsea from Russian billionaire Roman Abramovich.



The takeover deal was worth a whopping £2.3billion.



Clearlake took a 61.5% majority stake in Chelsea, while partners Todd Boehly, Mark Walter and Hansjorg Wyss split the remaining shares.

The investment firm has been the driving force behind Chelsea’s massive spending on players.



Under the joint ownership, the club committed more than £1.5billion to new signings.

Do Clearlake Capital have full ownership over Chelsea?

On Wednesday September 16, Chelsea announced that Clearlake is taking full control of the club.

The private equity firm has agreed to buy out the minority stakes held by co-owners Todd Boehly and Mark Walter.

Hansjorg Wyss will remain as a minority stakeholder and partner in the ownership group.

As part of the transition, Boehly will step down from his role as Chelsea chairman.



What has Todd Boehly said?

In Wednesday’s statement, the American said: “It has been an honour to serve as Chairman of Chelsea Football Club.

“I would like to thank the many who helped secure a bright future for the Club, including the English Premier League, the coaches and players, the talented leadership and staff at Chelsea, and the legions of dedicated fans.

“I have valued my partnership with Clearlake and the wider ownership group, and the collective decisions and investment we have made to support the immediate and long-term success of the Club.

“I am confident that Chelsea is well positioned for continued success under Clearlake’s leadership.”

What have the co-founders of Clearlake Capital said?

Eghbali and Feliciano, co-founders of Clearlake Capital, said: “Todd has been an important partner throughout our ownership of Chelsea, and we thank him for his time and contribution as Chairman.



“He will always be a part of the Chelsea story and family.”

They added their focus will be on “investing” in the club and “delivering long-term success for Chelsea and the Club’s supporters”.

Sports.title: Chelsea owners break silence on Todd Boehly exit as Blues embark on ‘next chapter’ with very clear plan
Sports.content:
Next

CHELSEA have promised fans there is a “clear direction” for their future after chairman Todd Boehly left the club.

The American was one of the leading faces of Clearlake Capital’s takeover from Roman Abramovich in 2022.



But he has now sold his stake in a £1billion deal, with majority owners Clearlake taking full control.

The club released a statement on Thursday assuring fans they had “confidence” in the club’s direction despite Boehly’s exit.



It read: “Yesterday marked an important milestone and the beginning of the next chapter for Chelsea. We thank our departing partners and are grateful for their contributions to the Club.

“We move forward with a shared sense of purpose, clear direction and confidence in what comes next.



“Our ambition is clear: to compete at the highest level, to win major trophies, and to build sustained success.

“Chelsea FC supporters are the heart of this Club and have been its true custodians for over 120 years.

“While we have the responsibility of ownership, this will always be your Club. We are committed to listening, and building a Chelsea you can be proud of, on and off the pitch.

“Success on the pitch will always be our first priority. That means competing to win the Premier League and other major trophies and strengthening the Club commercially so that we can invest consistently in the team.



BEST ONLINE CASINOS – TOP SITES IN THE UK

“We will also maintain our focus on Chelsea’s future infrastructure – investing thoughtfully and pursuing the right long-term solutions for generations to come.

“We are ambitious about what Chelsea can achieve, and equally conscious of the responsibility that comes with leading this great Club.

“We will keep working to move Chelsea forward – together. Chelsea Ownership.”



Boehly and Mark Walters have both flogged their 12.8 per cent shares for a small profit.

The club will now be led by Behdad Eghbali and business partner Jose E Feliciano, who have increased their stake to 99.9 per cent.

Boehly was a divisive figure among fans during his time in charge, with some angered over his transfer strategy and managerial changes.

Fans protested against his leadership on a number of occasions, most recently in April when hundreds of fans marched at Stamford Bridge with banners reading: “BlueCo Out”.

Boehly discussed his exit from Chelsea on Wednesday and said it had been an “honour” to lead the club.



He said: ““I would like to thank the many who helped secure a bright future for the Club, including the English Premier League, the coaches and players, the talented leadership and staff at Chelsea, and the legions of dedicated fans.

Sports.title: McManamon to fight Yu on undercard of heavyweight world title fight
Sports.content:
Britain’s Marie McManamon will meet Hong Kong Muay Thai star Yu Yau Pui in an atomweight clash on ONE Fight Night 48, live on Sky Sports on October 3.

McManamon is one of the UK's premier female Muay Thai athletes. A force in the ring, she has used her relentless cardio and whipping kicks to earn both Victory League and Roar Fighting Championship Titles.

Coming off a loss to Selina Flores, McManamon, a former ONE world title challenger, is going straight back into another top-level contest.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Paul Elliott beats Regan Upshaw with a head kick after just six seconds of their ONE Championship heavyweight bout

A dangerous striker who can end a contest at any given moment, Yu Yau Pui began competing in the weekly ONE Friday Fights series in 2023 and after four knockout wins in five fights, the Chinese striker won a lucrative $100,000 contract to ONE Championship.

Image: Marie McManamon challenges Allycia Hellen Rodrigues for the world Muay Thai championship

ONE Fight Night 48, live on Sky Sports in the early hours of Saturday October 3, will be headlined by Middlesbrough's Paul Elliott in a ONE Championship heavyweight world title bout against Shamil Erdogan.

The card also features America's Luke Lessei versus England's Charlie Guest in an important Muay Thai match which will see the winner push for a crack at Nico Carrillo's featherweight title.

Sports.title: 'More risk earlier!' - Norris braces for 'tougher' Monaco with shock Sprint
Sports.content:
World champion Lando Norris believes Formula 1 drivers will face a greater challenge at next year's Monaco Grand Prix than normal due to the addition of the Sprint format.

The 24-round 2027 calendar, published on Wednesday, includes 10 Sprint weekends - four more than this season - with Monaco's street circuit to host the alternative format for the first time.

The Principaliy's narrow track is not known for overtaking, where the Sprint format has hitherto tended to be used, but is considered arguably the greatest challenge in the sport for an F1 driver when it comes to qualifying.

Reacting to the news when speaking with Sky Sports F1's Natalie Pinkham alongside golfer Justin Rose during an appearance at the BMW PGA Championship Pro-Am at Wentworth on Wednesday, McLaren's Norris said: "Interesting.

"I guess the main thing is that means you've got FP1, [Sprint] qualifying on Friday - which is the challenge.

"Obviously not a lot happens in a race on Sunday or in the Sprint, but the challenge is just one practice session straight in, which has probably never happened before in Monaco."

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Craig Slater takes a look at the big talking points from the 2027 F1 season calendar

Drivers normally have three one-hour practice sessions to build up a rhythm and momentum around the twisty wall-lined track, on which mistakes are usually heavily punished. Set-up and on-track preparation work will now all have to be squeezed into just 60 minutes.

On the new challenge that the Sprint schedule presents, Norris said: "That's more [about] relying on data from this year.

Image: Norris watches on during the Pro-Am at Wentworth

"Obviously tougher for us as drivers.

"You don't have as much time to build up to things so you're going to you're probably going have to try and risk a little bit more earlier which is normally when you can see a bit more of a difference between people who can get comfy, try things and be at 99 per cent and not go to 103 and 104 [per cent] because in Monaco when you go to that limit, game over.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Craig Slater explains why Monaco has been chosen as a Sprint venue for the 2027 F1 season

"It's more exciting for the fans and the people watching."

Norris won the Monaco Grand Prix from pole position in 2025 during his title-winning year.
