Sports.title: Todd Boehly and Mark Walter cut all ties with Chelsea as Clearlake acquire shares in club in £950m deal
Sports.content:
Todd Boehly and Mark Walter cut all ties with Chelsea as Clearlake acquire shares in club in £950m deal

Clearlake Capital will acquire Todd Boehly and Mark Walter's shares in Chelsea Football Club, it has been announced.

Boehly and Walter own close to 26 per cent of the club having first purchased stakes in Chelsea in May 2022.

3 Boehly will also vacate his role as Chelsea chairman Credit: PA

It means Clearlake Capital, founded by Behdad Eghbali and Jose Feliciano, have 'full control' of the Premier League club.

talkSPORT understands the sale of the 26 per cent share is worth £950million with a total valuation of near £5billion, including the debt.

Meanwhile, stakeholder Hansjorg Wyss is understood to have increased his 12.8 per cent stake by joining Clearlake in acquiring part of Boehly's ownership interest.

With his stake being acquired, Boehly will no longer be the chairman of Chelsea.

However, the club insist that day-to-day operations will not change.

Xabi Alonso and the sporting leadership will also retain the full support of the ownership group.

Boehly statement

"It has been an honour to serve as chairman of Chelsea Football Club," Boehly, co-owner of MLB franchise LA Dodgers said.

"I would like to thank the many who helped secure a bright future for the club, including the English Premier League, the coaches and players, the talented leadership and staff at Chelsea, and the legions of dedicated fans.

"I have valued my partnership with Clearlake and the wider ownership group, and the collective decisions and investment we have made to support the immediate and long-term success of the Club.

"I am confident that Chelsea is well positioned for continued success under Clearlake’s leadership."

Eghbali and Feliciano statement

"Todd has been an important partner throughout our ownership of Chelsea, and we thank him for his time and contribution as chairman," Eghbali and Feliciano said.

3 There were plenty of reports of infighting between Boehly and Eghbali Credit: Getty

"He will always be a part of the Chelsea story and family. Clearlake has served as Chelsea’s majority owner since 2022, and as we move to full control our focus is to continue investing in the club’s infrastructure, sporting performance, player development and delivering long-term success for Chelsea and the club’s supporters."

Boehly was the face of the Chelsea ownership ever since their 2022 acquisition was completed.

The American joined the club alongside Clearlake Capital in a period of uncertainty amid sanctions on predecessor Roman Abramovich following Russia's invasion of Ukraine.

A 12th-place finish in the Premier League signalled a dreadful first season for Chelsea's new custodians, and Boehly was a focal point for criticism from fans and those outside the club.

However, despite continuous managerial upheaval and a questionable transfer policy, the Blues eventually won more silverware in 2025 with Conference League and Club World Cup glory.

Boehly also oversaw some successful signings as chairman, with Cole Palmer being the most notable having hit 58 goals and 34 assists in 137 appearances since signing from Manchester City three years ago.

3 Boehly was on hand to help deliver trophy success as Chelsea chairman Credit: Getty

Moises Caicedo and Joao Pedro are among the other hits as well as Estevao Willian, who chose Chelsea over European titans Barcelona and Real Madrid.

Morgan Rogers, who became the club's record signing in a £117m move from Aston Villa in the summer, has already been a success in the Chelsea attack.

Boehly was also present at numerous matches, both at Stamford Bridge and other venues, during his time as chairman.

Chelsea have ongoing plans to either redevelop Stamford Bridge or move to a new stadium which are said to have created tensions between Boehly's camp and Clearlake.

However, given that he and Clearlake Capital were at loggerheads just two years into their joint-ownership, the latest structural change should allow for a more streamlined plan of action going forward.

Sports.title: Man United player accused of ‘hiding’ as they suffer 50-year low with damning Carabao Cup collapse
Sports.content:
Man United player accused of ‘hiding’ as they suffer 50-year low with damning Carabao Cup collapse

Diogo Dalot has been accused of 'hiding' during Manchester United's Carabao Cup collapse against Brighton in an 'awful' team display.

The Red Devils' difficult start to the season went from bad to worse on Wednesday night as they suffered an embarrassing League Cup exit by squandering a two-goal lead to lose 3-2 at Old Trafford.



4 Man United were rocked by Brighton despite taking a commanding early lead Credit: Getty

After a demoralising defeat in Sunday's Manchester derby against a ten-man Manchester City, Michael Carrick's side were in need of a morale-boosting win.

And they made the perfect start as Shea Lacey and Mason Mount put them 2-0 up in the first 10 minutes.

But United were unable to build on their early dominance, and Charalampos Kostoulas took advantage of a Karl Darlow error to pull one back just before the break.



The game turned on its head in the second half, as goals from Pascal Grosz and Maxim De Cuyper saw Brighton take a 3-2 lead.

Unable to find an equaliser in the final 20 minutes, this condemned United to a third-round cup exit as they slumped to a 50-year low.



The capitulation was the first time since 1976 that a Red Devils team has lost a game at Old Trafford after going 2-0 up.

It piles even more pressure on manager Carrick, whose side have lost three of their first six games of the season, as well as suffering defeat in their opening domestic cup game for the third time in a row.



Dalot bears the brunt

After Man United's dismal cup exit saw their players booed off the pitch at full-time, former England defender Micky Gray singled out the performance of right-back Dalot for criticism.

Reacting to the result live on talkSPORT, Gray said: “Diogo Dalot tonight, I really felt for him.

“At times it just didn't happen for him. You could see him starting to hide. He was shirking away from just taking hold of the ball, maybe grabbing the game by the scruff of the neck.

4 Dalot was caught out on numerous occasions against Brighton Credit: Getty



“But nobody wanted it tonight at all, you could just see it. There were shrinking violets. It was awful to watch."

Dalot looked a weak link in the Brighton clash, as he struggled to contain the pace of Malick Yalcouye.

The Seagulls' attacker regularly managed to run in behind the Portuguese full-back, who has endured a difficult few days after also being far from his best against Man City.

His performance in Sunday's derby also came in for criticism, with United legend Wayne Rooney questioning his ability.



Discussing the defeat on the 'Stick to United' podcast, he said: "Full-backs in the modern game have to be and have to have energy.

"And I think Dalot is fit enough but lacks the quality."

4 Diogo Dalot kept his place in the starting XI against Brighton despite a poor Manchester derby display Credit: Getty

Dalot moved to Old Trafford from Porto in 2018, and has gone on to became a mainstay in the starting XI, making 251 appearances for the club.

He has featured in five of Man United's first six games of the season, starting in their 5-2 victory over Ipswich as well as a 2-2 draw against Everton and their latest two defeats to Man City and Brighton.



Carrick: We have to be better

With the pressure piling on Michael Carrick following United's crushing Carabao Cup exit, he admitted his side must respond quickly.

In his first full season as permanent boss, the Englishman has overseen just two wins so far - against Sabah in the Champions League and Ipswich - in a shock turn of events after securing a third-place league finish last season.

Carrick to Sky on the game: “The start of the game and the end of the game was completely different. It didn’t feel like the same game and certainly not the same emotions at all.

“We had the game exactly where we wanted it but we let it get away from us in a big way. That’s the story of the game.



4 Michael Carrick has so far struggled to replicate his heroics from last season at Old Trafford Credit: Getty

“There’s a number of things that we’ll look and dissect and I know quite a bit of where it went wrong.

“We can’t accept that and I take responsibility for it. The performance towards the end of the second half is on me.

“We’ll all be better. We all have to get better for a big game we have on Sunday that we need to prepare for.



“We’re out of this competition and we need to get back to winning football matches because it doesn’t feel good, let me tell you. But if we’re to get back to winning football matches we need to do a lot of things better.”

Sports.title: Daughter of F1 legend Juan Pablo Montoya lands Formula 2 driver and BROTHER a fine after breaking obscure rule by wearing revealing dress at the Spanish Grand Prix
Sports.content:
Daughter of F1 legend Juan Pablo Montoya lands Formula 2 driver and BROTHER a fine after breaking obscure rule by wearing revealing dress at the Spanish Grand Prix

See more Daily Mail on Google - save us as a Preferred Source

The daughter of Formula One legend Juan Pablo Montoya has landed an F2 driver in trouble after her dress broke pit lane regulations.

Paulina Montoya, an influencer with more than 40,000 Instagram followers, was a guest for F2 team Prema in Madrid over the weekend.

But the 20-year-old, who was supporting her driver-brother Sebastian, has landed her sibling a fine of £428 due to her attire on the Friday.

Montoya was wearing a white dress, but regulations stipulate that team and technical staff must wear long trousers in the pit lane.

Prema raced off to the commissioners, arguing that the social media star was a guest of the team and therefore exempt from the rules.

But the governors hit back by citing the FIA's International Sporting Code, which defines all guests as 'participants', and so the fine stood.

Paulina Montoya - daughter of F1 legend Juan Pablo - got in trouble for wearing this dress in the F2 pit lane

The regulations say that she had to wear long trousers in the pit lane - the dress does not count

Father Juan Pblo raced in F1 between 2001 and 2006, winning seven Grands Prix

Young Montoya took the slap on the wrist with good cheer, switching to white trousers the next day and writing on Instagram: 'Appropriate attire.'

On Sunday, the floor-length dress was back, but she did not get so close to any of the cars.

An FIA statement read: 'The Stewards summoned (Document 19) and heard the team representative. They examined video evidence. The team representative explained that the woman wearing shorts was a guest of the team and not an operational team personnel member.

'The Race Director reminded the following to all the Competitors in Competition Notes in Madrid (art 11.1). Teams are reminded that guests are included in the category as defined in Article 20 of the ISC. Additionally, Article 9.15 of the ISC states that the competitor is responsible for all acts or omissions on the part of any person to whom the competitor has allowed access to the reserved area.

'Furthermore, 'Article 22.15 of the Sporting Regulations states all team and technical personnel must wear long trousers in the pit lane during all practice sessions and the races. Having considered the matter extensively, the Stewards determined that a team member of Car 11 near the car was not wearing long trousers during the session and therefore decided to fine the team.'

Montoya Sr raced for Williams and then McLaren in F1 between 2001 and 2006, winning seven races and finishing as high as third in the Drivers' Championship on two occasions.

He has also raced in IndyCar and the NASCAR Cup Series.

His son, Sebastian, 21, is in his second season competing for Prema in F2 and currently sits 16th in the standings.

Sports.title: Jamie Carragher insists youngsters with 'nightmare' parents 'do not fulfil their potential' in warning shot to JJ Gabriel with Man United wonderkid's father pushing for exit
Sports.content:
Young stars do not reach their potential if they have a nightmare parent behind the scenes, Jamie Carragher has warned. The pushy parents issue has been in the spotlight after Man United's prodigiously talented 15-year-old, JJ Gabriel, stunned the club by informing them that he wants out – a play orchestrated by his father Joe O'Cearuill. Daily Mail Sport on Wednesday lifted the lid on O'Cearuill's behaviour being a nightmare for the club, riling up families and making a number of outlandish demands. Clubs having to manage the parents of their top starlets, who have become increasingly valuable from an even younger age, is an issue Carragher is well aware of. The former Liverpool centre-back's son, James, is a professional with Wigan in League One. Speaking on the latest Stick to Football podcast, Carragher said: 'In my experience when I was a kid... and watching James [Carragher] come through, in the main when there are situations like this the players never really fulfil their potential. JJ Gabriel wants out of Man United and Jamie Carragher has warned about the careers of starlets with pushy parents going awry 'When you've got an entourage, maybe it's the parents... we all know growing up, even at our age, some parents were a nightmare with their kids and were onto coaches about not getting enough minutes. 'You always look back, 20 years later, and I just think "that didn't help your son". And those players... I'd say 70, 80 per cent of situations where the entourage or the parents are a nightmare to deal with, they never end up doing what they should do because of situations like this.' Michael Carrick was asked about the Gabriel furore in the wake of Man United's 3-2 defeat by Brighton in the Carabao Cup on Wednesday night. He said: ‘We have to be a little bit careful on that one. He's a 15-year-old boy. It's more about the welfare, the care and the attention of JJ as a child really.’ It was another unwanted distraction and has clearly caused a stir within the club, with 19-year-old Shea Lacey scoring against the Seagulls having posted a photo of himself walking into Old Trafford along with a heart emoji before the game. That was interpreted as a pointed message to Gabriel, who has been dubbed 'kid Messi', with the teen wanting to depart before signing his first professional contract away from the club that nurtured him. Gabriel's social media conduct has not endeared him to supporters after he wiped all reference to the club from his Instagram account. It should be stressed that Gabriel is not fully accountable for his decision and image – his father and team behind him are hugely influential. Carragher said some parents can be a 'nightmare' behind the scenes at clubs Daily Mail Sport's Oliver Holt has pinned the blame for his would-be exit on the club, asking why English football's hottest youth property would entrust his future to an institution in decline with controversial owners. Less than a week ago, Gabriel scored a hat-trick on his UEFA League debut against FK Sabah, becoming the youngest player in United history to do so. Last summer, when Gabriel flirted with an exit, director of football Jason Wilcox intervened. Along with head of negotiations Matt Hargreaves, he convinced Gabriel of his route to becoming the youngest-ever first-team player. This season, Gabriel has been playing six years up and is thriving with the under-21s. United sources believe there is still the possibility that the situation can be rectified given that despite the player’s request, he cannot be de-registered from the squad and his current contract runs until the end of the season. Sources close to the player were quick to play down talk of discontent but it has now transpired that an explosive episode has been brewing behind the scenes, with Barcelona having spent years pursuing him, given he can leave the UK at 16 due to holding an Irish passport, allowing him to play in Europe. Joe O'Cearuill, the father of Gabriel, is a former Ireland international footballer and is seen as an ambitious and unpredictable character Only days ago after scoring the European hat-trick Gabriel’s boss at youth level Adam Lawrence, who leads the Under-19s and the Under-21s, spoke about coaching a player like Gabriel. ‘I think the first thing in my job is not to ruin him,’ Lawrence said. ‘So when you have a talented player like JJ and the other lads of course, you obviously don't want to stifle their freedom and their creativity. And I think essentially what you try and do is to set the team up to allow the talent to function and to play free at the right moments. ‘Of course, it can't always be free and off the cuff in terms of some of the off-the-ball responsibilities that he's working on and some of the pressing things that he's thinking about. But again, in terms of how he plays properly and how he connects with other team-mates at the top end of the pitch, he's just in a real good space. ‘With JJ, he's surrounded by people that really believe in him,’ Lawrence added. But those steering Gabriel's career from the background may be well advised to listen to Carragher's warning before taking the crucial next step.

Sports.title: Saudi club slapped with two-match stadium ban after Cristiano Ronaldo demanded lifetime bans for fans who targeted Ruben Neves with disgraceful Diogo Jota chants
Sports.content:
Saudi club slapped with two-match stadium ban after Cristiano Ronaldo demanded lifetime bans for fans who targeted Ruben Neves with disgraceful Diogo Jota chants

See more Daily Mail on Google - save us as a Preferred Source

Saudi Pro League Al-Taawoun have been handed a two-match stadium ban after a group of their fans shamefully taunted Ruben Neves with chants about his late friend Diogo Jota.

The club will play their next two home fixtures behind closed doors and they have also been ordered to pay a fine of 100,000 Saudi Riyals (£20,000).

The ban comes after footage shared on social media showed Al-Taawoun supporters repeatedly chanting Jota's name in the direction of Neves, during their 6-0 defeat to Al-Hilal.

Neves, who was a close friend and former team-mate of Jota at Wolves and for Portugal, appeared to signal to the fans that 'God is watching' in response.

He pointed first to the sky, then to his eyes and finally in their direction. The Portuguese star could be seen repeating the gesture before returning to the game.

Cristiano Ronaldo furiously called for the spectators who mocked Jota's passing to be handed a lifetime ban.

Ruben Neves was targeted by groups of Al-Taawoun supporters who chanted the name of his late team-mate Diogo Jota during a Saudi Pro League match on Saturday

Neves appeared to signal to the fans that 'God is watching', as he pointed first to the sky, then to his eyes and finally in their direction

Portugal captain Ronaldo posted on Instagram on Sunday: 'The league must take action and punish this kind of fan behavior.

'This is no longer football, and there have to be limits. People who behave like this should never be allowed to enter a stadium again.'

Neves briefly referenced the incident after Al-Hilal recorded a 6-0 victory over Al-Taawoun, as he quickly walked through the mixed zone post-match.

'I hope they don't go to prayer later,' Neves told reporters, appearing to contrast the behaviour of the fans with religious teachings.

Jota and his brother Andre Silva died in a car crash in northern Spain in July 2025. The former Liverpool forward was just 28 years old.

Neves had been Jota’s best friend after the days playing together at Wolves and with the national team. The midfielder was one of the pallbearers at his funeral.

Join the discussion How should football leagues handle fans who cross the line with deeply personal taunts?

Jota tragically died at the age of 28 in July last year following a car crash in Spain

Neves and Jota were close friends and played alongside each other on 164 occasions

Cristiano Ronaldo furiously called for the chanting spectators to be handed lifetime bans

The 29-year-old revealed last year that he had a new leg tattoo of him hugging his late team-mate in an emotional tribute, while Portugal decided Neves should wear Jota's No21 shirt, which he also dons for Al-Hilal.

Neves has also been a constant figure of support for Jota's widow, Rute Cardoso, who had married the star just 11 days before the tragic car accident.

Saudi Arabian international Saleh Abu Al-Shamat, who plays for Al-Ahli, also labelled the chants as 'wrong and unacceptable' in a social media post.

'I wanted to draw attention to something we all witnessed today. I felt it was my duty - as a Muslim - to share this and raise awareness,' Abu Al-Shamat wrote on Instagram.

'No one is perfect, of course, but regarding the actions of some Al-Taawoun fans during the match against Al-Hilal: this isn't just about our club; it concerns our great religion, Islam.

'No matter how intense the rivalry or the situation, we should never stoop to gloating over the dead, engaging in slander, or attacking people's families or the deceased.

'We live in an Islamic country, and it is our duty to show the world what Islam truly represents—a religion of love, tolerance, and respect. I hope we can leverage the massive attention our league is receiving to project the best possible image of Islam.

'By doing so, we might foster goodwill and help others learn about our faith. That is the message I wanted to convey; I felt a personal obligation, as a Muslim living in this great Islamic nation, to speak out against what is happening—because it is wrong and unacceptable.'

Sports.title: Max Verstappen WINS chaotic go karting race against 100 influencers: Formula One star sees off content creators in just 14 LAPS after starting from the back of the grid at Silverstone
Sports.content:
Max Verstappen blasted past 100 influencers in just 14 laps to win a chaotic exhibition go-kart race at Silverstone on Wednesday.

The Red Bull star started at the back of the field and was tasked with putting the social media stars in their place live on Disney+.

Within a single lap he had climbed to 37th and had unfortunately picked off Daily Mail Sport presenter Henry Williams, who had qualified 73rd.

Somewhat controversially, as absolute carnage broke loose, the Dutchman left the track at the second corner to overtake this publication's representative.

Verstappen was up to fourth by lap 10, with any driver he had overtaken having to retire.

And on lap 14, the four-time world champion finally got past Dutch journalist Jacky Martens to seal victory.

COMEÇOU: MAX VERSTAPPEN VS 100 KARTS



LOUCURA TOTAL!!!!! pic.twitter.com/GmpCs6JpZW — Blog Fórmula 1 (@blog_formula1) September 16, 2026

Max Verstappen beat 100 influencers in a race at Silverstone - after starting at the back of the grid

The Red Bull star had climbed to 37th after the first lap, eliminating most of the competition

Daily Mail sports presenter Henry Williams was controversially overtaken as the Dutchman left the track

'When I went to the grid and I saw where I had to start, with 100 karts in front of me, I was a little bit worried,' said Verstappen.

'After my first lap with all the carnage, I did think "OK, we have got this under control". From there on, I could really have a lot of fun trying to hunt them all down.

'Once I started getting into a rhythm and was able to overtake them one by one and saw the gap closing, that was really exciting.

'It was great to just be back in a go-kart again and go back to basics, it reminded me of racing back in the day.

'It's a really beautiful track and well designed. I had a great day and it was good to come out with the win.'

Daily Mail Sport star Williams said: 'It was really fun to be part of. Verstappen was a good sport.'

This race was a case of rolling back the years for Verstappen, 28, who started out in karting before building his illustrious F1 career.

Sports.title: Three Man City kids who can light up the Carabao Cup: The one-on-one dribbler who has blown Enzo Maresca away, the defender who took up boxing to toughen up and the 6ft midfield goal-machine with an unlikely first-team buddy
Sports.content:
During his first weeks in the job at Manchester City, Enzo Maresca revealed three academy kids had impressed him sufficiently to earn a permanent residence in first-team training this season.

Ryan McAidoo, Kaden Braithwaite and Floyd Samba were the trio who stood out more than the rest on the pre-season tour of Asia, with Maresca’s staff devising plans to divide the players’ time between the senior group and getting minutes for the Under 21s.

Both McAidoo and Braithwaite have already featured in the Premier League, with Samba on the hunt for a senior debut when City face Norwich City in the Carabao Cup tonight.

‘When we started pre-season we had many young players, and then at the end we decided to keep these three because we think they can improve training with us and then they can get some minutes,’ Maresca said.

Daily Mail Sport looks at the journey all three have taken so far at the Etihad Stadium.

RYAN McAIDOO

Age: 18, Position: Right winger

Maresca was blown away by McAidoo’s ability one-on-one during his first few sessions in Asia, with the winger stealing the show in a friendly against Inter.

A shoulder injury curtailed the start of his season but the 18-year-old is set for minutes having come off the bench in the Premier League against Crystal Palace and Coventry City.

Ryan McAidoo of Manchester City in action against Coventry City this season. The 18-year-old right winger is a wonderful dribbler and superb in one-on-one situations

McAidoo, who joined City from Chelsea two years ago, is considered the jewel of those breaking through at the Etihad

Considered the jewel of those breaking through at City, McAidoo joined from Chelsea two years ago – and scored on his senior debut in January, a 10-1 win over Exeter City in the FA Cup.

He was the first transfer between City and Chelsea at academy level since an informal pact between former director Jason Wilcox and his counterpart Neil Bath down at Cobham, struck so neither club would target the other’s teenage talents.

McAidoo’s journey at City has so far been stable, scoring 10 goals in 19 Under-18 league games in his opening year. Asked by Daily Mail Sport if the year had surprised him, he said: ‘No, not really. I’d planned it to go well but not this well.’

So there is a quiet confidence about a youngster whose progress England’s Under 21s are tracking and who has benefited from individual one-to-one coaching at club level.

His first training session with Pep Guardiola came at 16. Coaches were keen to work on his decision-making during the private work away from the group. They worked on timing when to cross rather than relying on dribbling past markers – even if McAidoo is devastating at that, still the clear elite facet of his game.

His coach, Oliver Reiss, even set targets of how many crosses to attempt in certain games as City attempted to challenge somebody who could find matches too easy.

McAidoo scored a 19-minute hat-trick off the bench in the UEFA Youth League against Feyenoord as a central striker while barely having completed his GCSEs and then stepped up to the higher age group last year, combining that with more consistent first-team training call-ups.

Notably the number of assists went up, which indicates McAidoo has taken on board the advice around decisions in the box. Sources say the next part to target is his movement and knowing when to attack the back post.

‘One of the surprises has been Ryan McAidoo, which nobody expected,’ Maresca said recently. ‘He was very good. I really like players who are aggressive in wide areas.

‘For him the best thing is to learn. Try to be intelligent, try to learn from Antoine (Semenyo) and Jeremy (Doku). When I say try to learn, it’s not in terms of how to dribble – it’s about working hard because it can be difficult with young players, they can stop working because they feel they are ready when they are not.’

Enzo Maresca is full of praise for McAidoo. 'I really like players who are aggressive in wide areas,' the manager said recently of the 18-year-old

McAidoo in action on his senior debut in January, a 10-1 win over Exeter City in the FA Cup in which he scored

KADEN BRAITHWAITE

Age: 18, Position: Central defender

Captain of the FA Youth Cup-winning team last season, Braithwaite officially joined City at the age of eight and is in a long line of academy products who have gone right through the ranks.

Braithwaite was part of the backline that kept JJ Gabriel quiet in that final against Manchester United in May and had already made his first-team bow by that point.

It was in the Carabao Cup third round two years ago when Braithwaite became the third-youngest player in the club’s history, starting the 2-1 victory over Watford. Only Glyn Pardoe and Paul Simpson made debuts younger than the then-16-year-old.

Interestingly, there were staff at the time who felt that Stephen Mfuni – now on loan at Coventry City for the season – was ahead of Braithwaite in the pecking order. The pair are the same age, born four days apart in February 2008, but Braithwaite’s first session with Guardiola’s squad two days out from that tie convinced the Catalan to throw him in at the deep end.

As with McAidoo, Braithwaite is set individual targets by coaches. At 16, it was to win more duels.

The Bolton-born teenager then took up boxing in a bid to toughen up – claiming that he had previously been too nice – and has caught the eye of Maresca with his composure and additional strength, making his Premier League debut against Palace last month.

Kaden Braithwaite was captain of the FA Youth Cup-winning Manchester City team last season and part of the backline that kept Manchester United's JJ Gabriel quiet

In the Carabao Cup third round two years ago, Braithwaite became the third-youngest player in Manchester City's history, starting the 2-1 victory over Watford

FLOYD SAMBA

Age: 17, Position: Central midfielder

Scorer of a sublime 25-yard curling free-kick in the FA Youth Cup final last season and has an eye for goal when breaking into the box from midfield.

He has netted a goal a game in the league for the Under 21s and Under 18s over the past year and at 6ft, already looks a commanding presence. In all, he contributed 24 goals and 10 assists in 38 appearances last season.

Samba’s brother Tyrone (18) regularly plays in the same team, while their younger brother Emerson is also a promising central defender within City’s academy.

Floyd Samba has been in Manchester City’s youth set-up throughout his childhood and has consistently excelled through the age groups

Samba scored a sublime free-kick in last season's FA Youth Cup final against Manchester United

The surname might feel familiar, with Samba the son of former Blackburn Rovers and Queens Park Rangers defender Chris.

Like Braithwaite, Samba has also been in City’s youth set-up throughout his childhood. Long-serving scout Mike Hayes spotted him at the Wilmslow Football Academy, a place specialising in summer soccer camps, and he has since consistently excelled through the age groups.

Fast forward to today, and Samba has taken on a surprising mentor within the first-team building.

Despite not yet mastering English and coming across as almost painfully shy, Uzbek Abdukodir Khusanov has been the one (alongside Gianluigi Donnarumma) who is helping Samba settle.

Sports.title: Kylian Mbappe insists Real Madrid stars 'HAD' to wear t-shirts supporting Ceuta and reveals why he defied orders amid migrant crisis in Spanish enclave
Sports.content:
Kylian Mbappe insists Real Madrid stars 'HAD' to wear t-shirts supporting Ceuta and reveals why he defied orders amid migrant crisis in Spanish enclave

See more Daily Mail on Google - save us as a Preferred Source

Kylian Mbappe has broken his silence on the decision to defy Real Madrid by covering up a t-shirt bearing a message of solidarity with the people of Ceuta.

Mbappe, Vinicius Jr and Ibrahima Konate were the only three players to roll up the pre-game shirts, which were designed to show support for residents of the territory which is facing an unprecedented migrant crisis.

Their small act of protest was an embarrassing look for Real, and it hinted at division in the ranks as the rest of the squad were happy to participate.

Now Mbappe has spoken for the first time about his thinking and expanded on his position on the Ceuta crisis.

He told AS: 'I want to explain this clearly so people understand. It was the club's decision to include the jersey, to have us wear it. We players had to wear it. The first thing I want to say is that I stand in full solidarity with Ceuta and with all the victims.

'Because before I’m a player, I’m a human being. But I also wanted to make a gesture and spare a thought for all the immigrants who have lost their lives and who are also living in harsh conditions.

Kylian Mbappe rolled up his t-shirt, partially obscuring the message of support for Ceuta

Ibrahima Konate, Vinicius Jr and Mbappe were the only three players to roll up their shirts

'It wasn’t an easy position to take, it was difficult because in the end, people might think I’m against the people of Ceuta, but no, absolutely not.

'I have nothing against them, and I support them 100% in my thoughts. But I also wanted to spare a thought for all the people who are suffering, because at the end of the day, I’m human, and I don’t want to prioritize one form of suffering over another.

'There are people who are suffering, and it breaks my heart to see that happening in the world. I’m a young man who wants the best for the world we live in.

'I aim to send a message of positivity and peace, and I hope this situation is resolved quickly.'

The t-shirts the players wore onto the field read 'We are all Caballas' (the nickname given to the people of Ceuta).

Mbappe, Vinicius Jr and Konate concealed that message prior to their 3-2 win over Elche on Tuesday night, causing a stir in Spain.

Earlier this summer, a state of emergency was declared when Spain faced a serious border crisis, with 80,000 migrants, mostly young Moroccan men, arriving on July 30 and 31. At least 57 people died trying to make the journey and Morocco has disputed Spanish sovereignty of the territory since independence in 1956.

The Ceuta president has said 13,000 of those migrants remain and it is still a red-hot political issue, which Real Madrid and other clubs have now waded in on.

The three Real stars who opted to defy the club have angered plenty of supporters.

Vinicius Jr (left) and Mbappe (right) showed their opposition to the message of Ceuta solidarity displayed on Real Madrid's t-shirts

One wrote: 'I hope they boo them until the day they leave Real Madrid, utter disgust.'

Another posted: 'I hope Florentino fines them with 3 months' suspension without a job or pay. That way, the nonsense would end quickly. They're way too full of themselves.'

While a third gave his damning verdict: 'Shame that @realmadrid allows this contempt toward our compatriots from Ceuta by these millionaires who live in luxurious gated communities with private security.'

A Moroccan player for Real Betis in Seville, Ez Abde, also wore the t-shirt before his side's game against Villarreal and received a barrage of abuse online from his countrymen.

After the criticism of the three Real stars, the club came out and defended them, with an official saying they'd accepted Elche's request to show such support in solidarity and wear the shirts.

Pictured: People play football at a settlement in Benitez Beach, created after the mass crossing of migrants from Morocco, in Ceuta, Spain, September 13, 2026

But the club added they respected differing opinions and gave each player the freedom to decide whether to wear it.

Barcelona opted not to wear the t-shirts for their LaLiga fixture.

The issue is a hugely sensitive one and Ceuta's crisis has been front and centre of the political agenda in Spain since July.

Spain is preparing accommodation for up to 10,000 migrants in Ceuta and the Spanish prime minister, Pedro Sanchez, has insisted the situation was not mishandled. 'What happened is that we couldn't cope with the influx,' he said this week.

He added that authorities had taken in the migrants before returning the majority to Morocco, adding that nine in ten had gone back.

Sánchez said accommodation for 6,000 people would be available by the end of the week, with capacity eventually rising to 10,000.

He said the government hoped to have the situation under control by the end of the year and appealed for patience from residents of Ceuta, which has a population of around 84,000.

Sports.title: Dejected Michael Carrick hits out at 'unacceptable' Man United performance after dismal Carabao Cup defeat by Brighton as he breaks silence on JJ Gabriel, 15, after wonderkid's quit threat
Sports.content:
Michael Carrick insists he is not feeling the pressure as Manchester United manager after an 'unacceptable' Carabao Cup exit at the hands of Brighton.

Carrick and his plays were booed off with chants of 'what the f***ing hell was that?' from the displeased supporters in the Stretford End after United blew a 2-0 lead to lose 3-2.

'We can't accept that as a group. I take responsibility for it,' Carrick said.

'The performance towards the end of the second half, that's on me.

'We'll all be better. We have to be better. We have a big game on Sunday that we have to prepare for. We're out of this competition and we have to go back to winning football matches. It doesn't feel good at the moment.'

Director of football Jason Wilcox looked shellshocked at the final whistle and after throwing away victory in the final seconds at Everton, losing in abject fashion at Old Trafford to Manchester City and now getting out-worked at home by Brighton to go out of the cup, the boos of discontent are growing ever louder.

Michael Carrick says it's not acceptable to see his Man United side tumble out the Carabao Cup

Carrick saw his United side blow a 2-0 lead to lose 3-2 at Old Trafford against Brighton

'We all know it's there,' Carrick, who has been slashed from 15/2 into 10/3 to be the first manager to leave the Premier League this season by Betfair, said of the boos.

'We know it's there whether it's good or whether it's not good. I think it's pretty obvious.

'We've all got feelings, we've all got emotions to a point, but it's how you deal with that that is the important thing. Being here toughens you up over a period of time, so it depends how you deal with it.

'You've got to deal with it in a way where you can cope with it and you can bring out the best in yourself, and whatever, however you do that, with your motivation and the confidence deep within yourself, as a whole group I'm talking about here, that we know we can win football matches and that's what we are here for is to win.'

Asked if this miserable start to the season, which also saw United lose at newly-promoted Hull City on the opening weekend, has him sweating over his job, Carrick was defiant in response.

'No, I don't feel under pressure,' he said.

'Either way, that doesn't bother me one bit. It generally doesn't bother me one bit.

'I understand what goes on outside and how the world works, but it generally doesn't bother me.

'What bothers me is winning games and having a good feeling around the place, and a good feeling around the group to know we're moving in a good direction. That's ultimately what bothers me.

'When we're on a good run, the biggest thing I'm worried about or thinking about is keeping the good run going and keeping everything on an even level really, to keep pushing that it's not enough.

'And if we're not on a good run, then we've got to get back to being on a good run. So, that's as simple as it gets.

'We've got to win football matches and we can do; I fully believe we will do. But obviously we've got to do it pretty quick and Sunday is a starting point.'

Shea Lacey scored the opening goal – a 'great moment' that Carrick conceded will get lost in light of this cup exit – and Mason Mount added a second before United unravelled badly.

But it was another academy player, 15-year-old JJ Gabriel, that dominated the lead-up to this match after the youngster, along with his family, requested contract termination as he shocked everyone at the club by asking to leave.

Join the discussion What does Man United need more right now: stronger leadership or better support for young talent?

Manchester United's teenage prodigy JJ Gabriel, 15, announced on Tuesday that he wants out

Gabriel's entourage have been left displeased by his lack of first team opportunities and while the original plan was to include him in the matchday squad for the Brighton game, that had to be shelved following the termination request and the fact Gabriel has not trained this week as he now appears to be effectively on strike.

'I just think we've got to be really careful of the whole situation,' Carrick said of Gabriel's situation.

'He's a young boy, he's 15, and for me, definitely, and from a club point of view, is about looking after our younger players, their welfare, their well-being, their exposure, and I think we've got to be really, all of us, I think we've got to be really conscious of that in this situation,' Carrick added.

Asked if he is involved in ongoing conversations given United still feel this situation with their brightest attacking player is rectifiable, Carrick confirmed it's a team effort.

'As a club for sure, we're all involved in those conversations,' he concluded. 'I just think we've got to be very careful of that.'

Brighton never lost belief and that was the key ingredient that they had against United to come from 2-0 down to win 3-2, according to their boss Fabian Hurzeler.

'I definitely believed and belief was a big word in the preparation for us,' he explained.

'When you go to a place like here you need to have belief and then to show it when you are 2-0 down shows real character.

'That shows the players have a real social bond.

'The foundation was that togetherness, this connection, the relationships they build on the pitch. The longer the game went on the more we had control.'

Sports.title: These are desperate days for Man United: After derby defeat and academy star JJ Gabriel's public snub, it gets even worse for Michael Carrick as Brighton fight back to knock them out of the Carabao Cup
Sports.content:
These are desperate days for Man United: After derby defeat and academy star JJ Gabriel's public snub, it gets even worse for Michael Carrick as Brighton fight back to knock them out of the Carabao Cup

See more Daily Mail on Google - save us as a Preferred Source

What desperate days these are for Manchester United. Beaten here in the Old Trafford derby on Sunday, at odds with supporters and in danger of losing the crown jewel of their academy, they crashed out of the Carabao Cup at the first attempt for the second year in a row. At least Brighton aren’t Grimsby.

The night had started so positively as well. Leading 2-0 inside 10 minutes, United looked to be cruising into the fourth round. Better still, the scorer of the first goal on his first start was teenager Shea Lacey who couldn’t have timed it more perfectly following the bombshell news on Tuesday that his Under-21s teammate JJ Gabriel wants to quit the club.

But it has been a poor start to the new season for Michael Carrick’s side, and it was about to get even worse as Brighton fought back to stun Old Trafford with their fifth win here in six visits.

It was also the first time in 50 years and 146 games that United have lost at home after being two goals ahead, going back to a 3-2 defeat to Tottenham in September, and the first after leading at half-time since Ipswich won here in 1984.

After a tame defeat in the derby to Manchester City on Sunday that could not be hidden behind the VAR controversy over Erling Haaland’s winning goal, this was a second defeat in four days at Old Trafford.

The boos at full-time told their own story. Carrick takes his team to Fulham on Sunday knowing that another one will put him under close early-season scrutiny going into the long international break.

Maxim De Cuyper wheels away in celebration after scoring Brighton's winner vs Man United

Michael Carrick saw his United side lose a 2-0 lead to get knocked out of the Carabao Cup

It's been a tumultuous few days for the Red Devils on and off the field and this only adds to it

‘We can't accept that as a group,’ said the United boss. ‘I take responsibility for it. It's on me ultimately. I’ll take the praise, I’ll take the criticism and the upset.

‘The pressure doesn’t bother me one bit. I understand how the world works. The feeling at the start of the game to the feeling at the end couldn’t be further apart. It’s happened so quickly over two or three weeks, there’s a lot of disappointment.

‘Of course we can turn it around. We have to be better. It doesn't feel good at the moment. We have a big game on Sunday that we have to go back to winning football matches.’

On the furore over Gabriel, Carrick added: ‘We have to be a little bit careful on that one. He's a 15-year-old boy. It's more about the welfare, the care and the attention of JJ as a child really.’

The news about Gabriel could hardly have come at a worse time. Lacey appeared to react to it on Tuesday night by posting a photo of himself walking into Old Trafford along with a heart emoji, and he made another point inside eight minutes when he fired United ahead.

It was a particularly sweet moment for the 19-year-old given that he was sent off against Brighton on his home debut as a substitute in January.

There was something inevitable about his goal last night. Youri Tielemans picked out Lacey on the right side of the box and he cut inside Jaouen Hadjam before whipping a shot inside Jason Steele’s near post.

Old Trafford rose to salute the first teenager to score on his United debut since Marcus Rashford against Midtjylland here a decade ago.

The fans had only just settled down when Mason Mount had them off their seats again in the 10 minute. Rashford picked Costinha’s pocket and breezed past Luka Vuskovic. Steele kept out his effort but the ball ran to Mount who got there just ahead of Lacey to score the second.

Shea Lacey kisses the Manchester United badge after opening the scoring in the match

United doubled their lead on 10 minutes when Mason Mount scored with this right-footed shot

Charalampos Kostoulas started the Brighton comeback with this shot just before half-time

Pascal Gross (second right) levelled the scoreline for the Seagulls with this left-footed finish

At that stage, who could have foreseen the pain that was about to follow?

United were enjoying themselves and the crowd loved it when Rashford, who had Costinha on the run down the left, nutmegged Chema Andres.

But there was a vulnerability to them that was perhaps epitomised by the young centre-back partnership of Ayden Heaven and Leny Yoro after Carrick made eight changes from the derby and waited too long to change back again as the tide of the game turned dramatically against his team.

‘The performance towards the end of the first half is on me,’ he admitted after Brighton took control of the game and threatened on a number of occasions before Charalampos Kostoulas pulled a goal back in added time at end of the half.

United were unhappy that referee Farai Hallam didn’t give Benjamin Sesko a free kick when he was floored by a tag team of Malick Yalcouye and Olivier Boscagli, but they switched off as Hadjam’s long diagonal pass picked out Kostoulas who got in between Heaven and Darlow to score.

The equaliser arrived in the 64th minute when Diogo Dalot hooked a clearance towards halfway where Sesko was under pressure by Pascal Struijk and succeeded only in heading the ball 30 yards back towards his own goal. Pascal Gross was waiting to receive it on the edge of the box and sold Yoro a dummy before sliding a shot past Darlow.

The momentum was with Brighton and Kostoulas got away from Mazraoui in the 69th minute and crossed for substitute Maxim De Cuyper to complete an incredible comeback.

‘I definitely believed and belief was a big word in the preparation for us,’ said head coach Fabian Hurzeler. ‘When you go to a place like this you need to have belief and then to show it when you are two goals down shows real character.’

Sports.title: Man Utd are back in an all-too familiar position - where do they go next?
Sports.content:
The new season may only be six games old, but it feels as though Manchester United fans have already lived through it a thousand times.

A run of underwhelming results - yielding just two wins - and performances means the goodwill and momentum built up by Michael Carrick during the second half of the 2025-26 campaign has already waned significantly. And while questions will inevitably be asked of United's former interim coach during the upcoming, prolonged international break if the Red Devils cannot sign off with a win at Fulham on Sunday, scrutiny should also be directed to those above Carrick in the hierarchy.

United's disappointing week went from bad to worse on Wednesday as they were dumped out of the Carabao Cup. While there was a sense of injustice over the Manchester derby defeat last Sunday given the offside controversy shrouding Erling Haaland's decisive goal, United were bang to rights against Brighton.

They crumbled after surging into a two-goal lead with Carrick becoming the first Manchester United manager to oversee a home defeat after leading 2-0 at half-time since Tommy Docherty in 1976.

‌



Carrick and his team left the field to a chorus of boos from supporters, whose early season optimism has already taken a pummelling.

JOIN US ON FACEBOOK! Latest news, analysis and much more on Mirror Football's Facebook page

Get YOUR Mirror Football Newsletter Get our comprehensive football coverage, with news, updates, opinions, analysis and everything that matters to you, straight to your inbox. To get it, it's a quick and easy one-two: 1. Head THIS WAY 2. Enter your email and hit Subscribe

And that has become a common trend for those taking their seats on the Stretford End. Just 12 months ago, United backed Ruben Amorim heavily in the transfer market, helping him rebuild their attacking options. But hopes of a second-season surge under the Portuguese were quickly extinguished, with his demise coming in January of this year.

‌



Go back another year and it was Erik ten Hag - fresh off after another summer of investment - who was clinging onto a job he would ultimately lose by the middle of October.

This represents a first crisis period for Carrick, who was handed the reins on a permanent basis after providing the perfect tonic to Amorim's torturous tenure by overseeing 11 wins and three draws from 16 competitive games.

View 3 Images Carrick had United purring last season, but he is now in the midst of his first really difficult patch (Image: Justin Setterfield/Getty Images)

There were, understandably, parallels drawn between his impact in an interim capacity and that previously of Ole Gunnar Solksjaer. Crucially, though, Carrick has already proven he can navigate choppy waters; few would have envisaged a third-place finish for United given the condition they were in at the time of Amorim's implosion nine months ago.

‌



Since then, United have spent around £150million on a midfield overhaul designed to give Carrick the tools to continue the club's rehabilitation as they seek a seat back at the Premier League's top table.

But not only did the new partnership of Andrey Santos and Youri Tielemans get outfoxed by Brighton, there are already glaring holes elsewhere in the squad.

View 3 Images Man Utd crashed out of the Carabao Cup at the hands of Brighton

Luke Shaw's absence again highlighted United's failure to bring in adequate cover in that area during the transfer window for the here and now. And while it has already been suggested that the club will look to level up their defence next summer, choosing to rely so heavily on Shaw and Harry Maguire given their previous arcs - and where they are in their careers - for another year feels like a big call. Leny Yoro, signed for a significant transfer fee, has also yet to hit the desired levels in defence.

‌



In Benjamin Sesko, still yet to start a Premier League game this season, United have invested significantly. But the Slovenia international did not make the most of an opportunity to impress leading the line against Brighton. Bryan Mbeumo and Matheus Cunha have Premier League pedigree and been rare transfer wins for United, but the fact Sesko was replaced by Joshua Zirkzee punctuates up a real dearth of quality depth in that No 9 area.

Strategic shortcomings like that cannot be attributed to Carrick, rather those above United's manager hierarchy. And solving them will not be cheap, nor will they be straightforward, even though United have managed to successfully move away from inflated figures in the transfer market.

Teething problems after a transfer window are not uncommon and perhaps United's business will age like wine rather than milk. After nailing their colours to Carrick's, he must, at least, be given the opportunity to steer United back on course. After all, a rinse and repeat would do nobody any favours.

‌



In two years the club will celebrate it's 150th anniversary; an event which Omar Berrada, United's chief executive, targeted back in 2024 as an occasion for United to mark by winning both men's and women's league titles.

Right now that feels fanciful. And while it will ultimately be down to Carrick to achieve the results which will ensure he gets the chance to see 'Project 150' through, others will be just as culpable if he is unable to do.

Sports.title: Roy Keane points finger after JJ Gabriel quit bombshell with reminder about Man United starlet
Sports.content:
Roy Keane points finger after JJ Gabriel quit bombshell with reminder about Man United starlet

Former Manchester United midfielder Roy Keane has delivered his verdict on JJ Gabriel's transfer bombshell with the teenage talent asking to leave Old Trafford

View 2 Images JJ Gabriel told Manchester United he wants to leave (Image: Manchester United/Manchester United via Getty Images)

Roy Keane has pointed the blame at JJ Gabriel's representatives after it was leaked that the 15-year-old has requested to quit Manchester United.

‌



Earlier this week, The Telegraph first reported that Gabriel had sent formal notice that he wishes to cancel his registration at the club with immediate effect to become a free agent.

‌



United were left stunned by Gabriel's decision and he was due to be involved in the Carabao Cup squad to face Brighton & Hove Albion on Wednesday. If he had featured, he would have become the club's youngest-ever player, eclipsing David Gaskell, who was 16 years and 19 days old when he debuted back in 1956.

‌



Jamie Redknapp tears into two Man Utd players after embarrassing Brighton collapse READ MORE :

Man Utd next manager odds with three clear favourites as pressure mounts on Michael Carrick READ MORE :

Despite this, United believe the situation can still be resolved with Gabriel still having time left on his contract. He cannot be de‑registered unless all parties agree, but he is going to be able to negotiate a move abroad once he turns 16 next month, helped by the fact he has an Irish passport.

Speaking on The Overlap, Gary Neville claimed that Gabriel has been let down by his representatives and said that his camp should not have leaked the information to the media. The young sensation has since become one of the biggest football stories this week, due to his talent and potential at his disposal.

Responding to Neville, Keane said: "If his agents have leaked this, to be fair, that's not on United is it?"

‌



View 2 Images JJ Gabriel has asked to leave Manchester United (Image: Manchester United via Getty Images)

Neville then added: "I would say from a point of view of duty of care for a 15-year-old, is that a 15-year-old is the back page story of every newspaper in the country, How are you looking after that kid?

"I don't care whether you think he should be playing or not; if you think he should be playing, great - I think lots of parents think their kid should be playing. However, his representatives: why would you want that leaking out to the newspapers?"

‌



While defending United on the Gabriel situation, Keane did stress that the Reds need to start winning matches to ease the pressure on the club and manager Michael Carrick, who has come under scrutiny this week.

"Carrick's under pressure. Obviously, [Sir Alex] Ferguson, we go back and sometimes you’d throw lads into the first team, but United they need wins," Keane continued.

"I don't think United are in the position to go 'We can write off a cup game tonight and play a couple of young lads'. No, we need to get some wins, we need to get some momentum into the season and if some 15-year-old is spitting his dummy out, we'll deal with that."

Sports.title: Roy Keane tells Man Utd exactly what to do after JJ Gabriel exit threat
Sports.content:
Roy Keane tells Man Utd exactly what to do after JJ Gabriel exit threat

JJ Gabriel has submitted a transfer request to leave Manchester United, with Roy Keane delivering a blunt response to the 15-year-old's exit request

View Image JJ Gabriel has requested to leave Man United (Image: Manchester United via Getty Images)

Roy Keane says Manchester United cannot afford to focus on an unhappy 15-year-old who has 'spat his dummy out' while Michael Carrick faces mounting pressure and desperately needs results. United were shocked when JJ Gabriel made his exit request this week.

‌



Club officials were taken aback by the development, especially given plans had been in place to include Gabriel in the matchday squad for Wednesday night's clash with Brighton and Hove Albion, with a potential debut on the cards. Had he taken to the pitch in the 3-2 home defeat, a match United had led 2-0, he would have set a new record as the youngest player ever to represent the club.

‌



Nevertheless, United remain confident the matter can be sorted, with time still remaining on his deal. Gabriel cannot be de-registered, though he will be free to explore opportunities overseas once he reaches 16 next month, aided by his possession of an Irish passport.

‌



Jamie Redknapp tears into two Man Utd players after embarrassing Brighton collapse READ MORE :

Man Utd next manager odds with three clear favourites as pressure mounts on Michael Carrick READ MORE :

Speaking on The Overlap, Keane weighed in on the saga but emphasised that United's priority must be securing victories, having suffered a less-than-ideal start to the season. "Carrick's under pressure. Obviously, [Sir Alex] Ferguson, we go back and sometimes you'd throw lads into the first team, but United they need wins," he said.

"I don't think United are in the position to go 'We can write off a cup game tonight and play a couple of young lads'. No, we need to get some wins, we need to get some momentum into the season and if some 15-year-old is spitting his dummy out, we'll deal with that."

Carrick also addressed the matter publicly following the defeat to Brighton. "I just think we've got to be really careful of the whole situation, you know," he admitted.

‌



"He's a young boy, he's 15, and for me, definitely, and from a club point of view, is looking after our younger players, their welfare, their well-being, their exposure, and I think we've got to be really, all of us, I think we've got to be really conscious of that, really, in this situation."

Carrick emphasised that the circumstances surrounding Gabriel required careful handling when speaking to Sky Sports. "It's more about the welfare, the care and the attention of JJ as a child, really," he said.

‌



FOLLOW OUR MAN UTD FB PAGE! Latest United news and more on our dedicated Facebook page

"He's certainly a young man. The situation is what it is, but we have to be careful about the exposure on that one."

The 15-year-old wonderkid is yet to make his official first-team debut, though he did turn out for Carrick's side during pre-season. Gabriel has been training regularly with the senior squad following his remarkable campaign for United's Under-18s last season, netting 26 goals in 29 matches.

‌



However, Gabriel's future now hangs in the balance after he lodged a request to cancel his registration, though United are yet to approve it. The club remain convinced the matter can be sorted, but their prospects of retaining their academy jewel could become more complicated as the striker nears his 16th birthday next month.

He has no shortage of suitors, with Real Madrid, Barcelona, Paris Saint‐Germain and Bayern Munich amongst the clubs pursuing the teenager. Madrid are understood to have watched Gabriel and were left impressed by his recent display against Sabah, where he grabbed a hat-trick in the UEFA Youth League.

As he qualifies for an Irish passport, Gabriel could feasibly transfer to clubs across the continent without facing the same restrictions applied to British youngsters.

Sports.title: Todd Boehly’s Chelsea era ends after disastrous transfers and more managers than trophies
Sports.content:
It has been thoroughly entertaining for everyone but Chelsea fans. In truth, it is something of an achievement to take a team who finished in the top four for 16 out of 19 seasons, and then presided over one top-four finish in four years.

History is unlikely to look fondly on Todd Boehly's legacy as his spell as one of the most recognisable figures attached to the Blues comes to an end.

On Wednesday night, it was confirmed that Clearlake Capital had purchased the shares owned by Boehly and fellow minority co-owner Mark Walter.

The American, also heavily involved in MLB franchise the Los Angeles Dodgers, was a driving force behind the purchase of Chelsea and, from the outside, it has long looked as if he was calling the shots, but that wasn't always the case. Nevertheless he has still been part of a regime that has hired more managers than trophies its won.

‌



Get YOUR Mirror Football Newsletter Get our comprehensive football coverage, with news, updates, opinions, analysis and everything that matters to you, straight to your inbox. To get it, it's a quick and easy one-two: 1. Head THIS WAY 2. Enter your email and hit Subscribe

JOIN US ON FACEBOOK! Latest news, analysis and much more on Mirror Football's Facebook page

Roman Abramovich, who remains adored by the bulk of the Chelsea faithful, showed that hiring and firing managers was by no means a barrier to success. The Russian was trigger happy, but his methods resulted in trophies, in part because the individuals he hired were competent and given high-calibre squads.

Boehly, and those he worked with, seemed determined to rip up conventional wisdom and do it their way, some of their ideas seemed to stem from what works in US Sports. This was ultimately a man who ramped up the idea of an All Stars Game, talking about the revenue streams, but ignoring the fact player welfare is an ongoing issue.

‌



Boehly ultimately sacked the best manager he's had within months of arriving. Chelsea haven't come close to hiring a man who sits in the same league as Thomas Tuchel.

View 5 Images Behdad Eghbali and Clearlake will take overall charge of the club (Image: PA)

Not only has he done that, but he's also spent astronomical sums on players, the majority of whom have underdelivered. Again, look at Abramovich, the oligarch came in and threw his wealth around, but when he did it he was signing Didier Drogba, Petr Cech and Ricardo Carvalho - men who would be pillars of their success.

When Boehly and co rocked up, the American was initially serving as an interim sporting director, replacing the widely respected Marina Granovskaia. His tenure had arguably left the Blues chasing their tails ever since.

‌



Their initial summer of recruitment saw them spend big. Really big. A net outlay of £485million - a figure that dwarfs anything the league has seen.

They went for the likes of Wesley Fofana, Marc Cucurella, Kalidou Koulibaly and Raheem Sterling. Only one of those remains, that being Fofana, and he's spent huge periods on the sidelines.

Chelsea have managed to sign Noni Madueke, decide he's not for them, sell him to rivals Arsenal, and watch him win the Premier League title in his first season. Even more damning was the decision to let Kai Havertz walk the Chelsea to Arsenal path. A player who the Blues couldn't get the most out of, was deemed surplus to requirements to the extent they were happy to hand him off to a rival. He's now thriving as the false 9 for the country's dominant team.

He eventually stepped down after just six months, but the damage had arguably already been done. If you get recruitment and retention wrong to that degree, you'll find it hard to be a success.

‌



View 5 Images Raheem Sterling and Pierre-Emerick Aubameyang were two signings who ultimately flopped

The fact so many players have come and gone inside the four years of the Boehly regime speaks volumes for the lack of continuity they've enjoyed. This summer Nicolas Jackson and Liam Delap, two men signed as strikers but ultimately underwhelmed, have both been sold to fellow Premier League clubs.

Chelsea on the pitch haven't passed the eye test, you don't need to be a footballing-watching veteran to see that it hasn't worked. And the numbers don't act as any type of solace.

Sticking with the striker theme, the Blues have brought in Pierre-Emerick Aubameyang, Christoper Nkunku and Delap and have seen a return of 24 goals. They've all now found new homes.

‌



It's not to say some signings haven't worked. Cole Palmer for £40m has been a hit. Moises Caicedo and Enzo Fernandez, both signed for British-record fees, have impressed, but then you'd expect them to given their £100m plus price tags. The Chelsea project and revolving door of managers was so utterly convincing that Fernandez pushed and pushed for the exit door before eventually joining Enzo Maresca at Manchester City.

View 5 Images Enzo Fernandez had been pushing for the exit door for months (Image: 2026 Getty Images)

Maresca remains the only manager to leave Chelsea, in part, off his own back whilst Boehly has been in the building. Graham Potter, Mauricio Pochettino and Liam Rosenior were hired and quickly fired - with the Argentine's dismissal reportedly behind the tension between Boehly and Clearlake.

Questions were asked at the time as to whether Potter and Rosenior's CVs were worthy of them landing the Chelsea job. The club's fanbase had been accustomed to the hierarchy going for a Jose Mourinho, a Carlo Ancelotti or an Antonio Conte. That type of ambition has certainly been lacking.

‌



It seems remarkable that Chelsea are only the fourth highest net spenders in England since Boehly and co took the reigns. That said, if outlay and investment should somewhat correlate to league position, then finishing 12th, 6th, 4th and 10th is a poor show.

Winning the Europa Conference League just over a year ago was seen as something to celebrate, which is maybe a sign of the change in expectations, as it meant the Blues had won all three of the European trophies on offer. No one seemed to realise that a Real Madrid or a Bayern Munich probably can't pull off that feat given they never finish low enough to qualify for the newly created Conference League.

View 5 Images Chelsea won the Club World Cup in 2025 (Image: Darren Walsh/Chelsea FC via Getty Images)

They were crowned the inaugural FIFA Club World Cup champions in the summer of 2025, but the dust had barely settled on that trophy, before Maresca was gone.

‌



Boehly has ultimately been the face of one of the biggest demises of a European giant in modern time. Chelsea insist the day-to-day operation at the club will not be impacted, a sign of just how much power Boehly has ceded in recent times.

With Xabi Alonso in the dugout, and the boardroom uncertainty resolved, Chelsea fans will hope a new era can finally bring some stability to a club now all-too accustomed with upheaval and chaos.

Sports.title: Inside the Spanish Grand Prix and why F1 needs to drastically change the Madring
Sports.content:
Inside the Spanish Grand Prix and why F1 needs to drastically change the Madring

Formula 1 returned to Madrid last weekend following a 45-year absence, and Mirror Sport was taken behind the scenes at the new £71million circuit to watch one of this season's most anticipated races

View 4 Images The Spanish Grand Prix won't look the same in 2027 (Image: Hoch Zwei Photography/Allwyn)

I didn't dare to blink. As the red lights flashed and engines whirred, history was about to be made.

‌



Not since 1981 had the travelling roadshow that is Formula 1 made a stop at Madrid, but Sunday's Spanish Grand Prix put an end to that wait. Once the who's who of celebrities - including the King of Spain and practically the entire Real Madrid squad - had been shepherded away from the grid, it was time to race.

‌



Lando Norris knew what was at stake, as the world champion made an aggressive start from pole position to cut off Kimi Antonelli. In normal circumstances, Norris would've gone on to convert his excellent qualifying session on Saturday into a third victory in four weekends - and in doing so closed the gap on Antonelli, this year's champion elect.

‌



But this was no normal Grand Prix. This was the Madring, a brand-new circuit purpose built for £71million that proved to be the scene of Norris' frustration. The timing of a virtual safety car on lap 15 worked against the McLaren star and right into Antonelli's hands, ultimately giving Mercedes' wonderkid the win.

JOIN US ON FACEBOOK! All the best sports news and much more on our dedicated Facebook page

‌



I can't think of another instance in 2026 when there's been so much chatter about the track layout. A recent Formula 3 test had resulted in a whopping 19 red flags over two days, prompting Williams team principal James Vowles to label the Madring a 'car killer'.

From leaving home to arriving in the Spanish capital, I couldn't help but ask myself questions. Will the race be ravaged by red flags? Is overtaking even going to be possible on such a narrow track? How will the sloping, swerving 'La Monumental' go down? And is this where local heroes Carlos Sainz and Fernando Alonso finally kickstart their seasons?

I spent the weekend with Allwyn, the multi-national lottery and gaming company who understands the thrill of anticipation better than anyone. That's why Allwyn is the lead parter of the formation lap.

‌



It's during those tantalising seconds when you feel the level of anticipation hit fever pitch. As they take their positions and wait on the grid, every driver must feel as if they have a lottery ticket in their hands, hoping that fortune is on their side.

After jostling for a clear view above the end of the pit lane, I couldn't take my eyes off the action for a split second, with the short dash to turn 1 promising all-out racing warfare. That pulsating start - including a battle between Lewis Hamilton and Max Verstappen, plus contact between Sainz and Yuki Tsuonoda, was the highlight of the Grand Prix.

View 4 Images Lando Norris maintained the lead by getting off to a fast start (Image: Hoch Zwei Photography/Allwyn)

‌



But as I discovered, there's so much more to a weekend at the F1. Before travelling to Madrid, I didn't appreciate the level of anticipation that exists in the days, hours and minutes leading up to Sunday's race.

During Friday and Saturday's practice sessions, you could feel the excitement radiating from fans who filled the sweltering grandstands or indulged in the swanky hospitality. Even in the city centre, the buzz was palpable.

The Paddock Club was packed with special guests - so much so I that having football legend Roberto Carlos brush past me didn't come as a shock. Yet the lavishness of the setting - and insatiable food and drink - didn't distract from what we were all here for.

‌



It's not only the drivers who have a chance to win at a Grand Prix either. The Allwyn League lets F1 fans predict the results, key moments and specific scenarios ahead of qualifying. It's always fun to play and you can find it here - just sign up and be in with a chance of winning prizes.

View 4 Images 'La Monumental' is the Madring's signature corner (Image: Hoch Zwei Photography/Allwyn)

My predictions proved to be 60 per cent accurate after a drama-sapped race. Once Ferrari admitted defeat in their hope of a late red flag that would've give race leader Charles Leclerc a free pit stop, Antonelli cruised to a victory which he acknowledged really belonged to Norris.

‌



Then came the backlash. A visibly frustrated Norris didn't mince his words in the post-race press conference, bemoaning: "There are some obvious changes they should make.

"They should get rid of (turns) 18 and 19. Useless! Just have more of a straight into a hairpin. I don't know how someone looks at this design [in planning] and goes, 'mint'."

Williams driver Alex Albon also labelled the race 'pretty boring' while Audi's Gabriel Bortoleto joked that he 'almost fell asleep'. Those comments are exactly why organisers of the Spanish Grand Prix plan to make changes in time for the second edition which will take place between September 10 and 12 next year, with F1's 2027 calendar having finally been confirmed on Wednesday.

‌



View 4 Images The Madring is set for changes next year (Image: Hoch Zwei Photography/Allwyn)

Mirror Sport understands that various sections of the track will be tweaked in an effort to encourage more wheel-to-wheel racing and increase the amount of overtaking opportunities, giving fans the drama they deserve. People came from around the world to witness F1's return to Madrid, with the weekend attendance recorded at 353,000.

The Argentine flag was flown in various grandstands, as Alpine's Franco Colapinto delighted them with a P7 finish. Those supporting Sainz and Alonso didn't have much to cheer about, nor did Hamilton's fans following his early retirement due to a brake problem.

‌



Two hours before the race, I was treated to the same view as the drivers thanks to a guided track tour. While some grandstands offered fantastic views and welcome shade, other areas left fans short-changed.

Those who'd purchased general admission tickets and watched the action from the Madring's north fan zone had to sit on planks of wood on a sandy hill, sizzling in the baking heat. If that wasn't disappointing enough, their views of the track were partially obstructed by vehicles and temporary toilet blocks.

As for the wider facilities at the Madring - built around the Ifema exhibition centre near Madrid's international airport - the teams were impressed. Ferrari boss Fred Vasseur described the event as 'mega' while Mercedes counterpart Toto Wolff hailed: "For a first [race], it's probably one of the best, or maybe the best, that I've seen so far."

Article continues below

If the F1 hierarchy can listen to its drivers and paying fans, we might be in for a vastly improved Madring experience next time around. Don't let them down.

Sports.title: Man Utd boss Michael Carrick makes it clear where he stands on JJ Gabriel exit talks
Sports.content:
Man Utd boss Michael Carrick makes it clear where he stands on JJ Gabriel exit talks

Manchester United are at risk of losing their most promising academy star after JJ Gabriel lodged a request for the club to de-register him prior to their loss against Brighton

View 2 Images JJ Gabriel wants out of Manchester United (Image: Manchester United/Manchester United via Getty Images)

Michael Carrick has stressed that people need to be mindful of JJ Gabriel's age following reports the Manchester United prodigy has asked to leave the club.

‌



Gabriel, 15, has been billed as the next big thing at Old Trafford after making a seismic impression among the academy ranks. It has even been suggested that the teenager was in line to make his senior debut in Wednesday night's Carabao Cup defeat against Brighton prior to Gabriel expressing a desire to quit the club.

‌



United are understood to have been taken aback by Gabriel's request, with the bombshell news quickly making headlines given the youngster's significant potential.

‌



Carrick gave little away about the situation after the Brighton loss and outlined why Gabriel's age means things must be handled delicately.

‌



"We have to be a little bit careful on that one. He's a 15-year-old boy," said the United manager. "It's more about the welfare, the care and the attention of JJ as a child really.

“He's certainly a young man. The situation is what it is, but we have to be careful about the exposure and how much we jump on that."

When he was asked if he was involved in the discussions around Gabriel's future, Carrick added: "As a club, for sure, we're all involved in those conversations. I just think we've got to be very careful of that."

‌



Barcelona and Real Madrid are two of the juggernauts understood to be keeping a close eye on developments with Gabriel, who is eligible to sign scholarship forms following his 16th birthday on October 6.

View 2 Images Gabriel is already being linked with a host of big clubs (Image: Manchester United via Getty Imag)

The attacker, who scored a hat-trick on his debut for the Under-19s in the UEFA Youth League just last week, has an Irish passport which would allow him to move overseas.

‌



Despite Gabriel's request to be de-registered immediately, Manchester United are said to harbour some hope that the situation can be resolved amicably without the talented teenager's departure.

Gabriel was named Under-18 Premier League player of the year last season despite being just 14 when the campaign started and would have become United's youngest ever player had he made his senior bow on Wednesday night.
