World.title: South Africa’s 10-year driving licence takes another step forward
World.content:
Motorists in South Africa could soon have one less piece of admin to worry about when it comes to renewing their driving licence cards.

A long-discussed change to the country’s driving licence system has now reached another important stage, bringing the proposed new rules closer to becoming reality.

Another step towards longer driving licence validity

Transport Minister Barbara Creecy published the proposed changes in the Government Gazette on 17 August 2026, opening a 30-day public comment period.



That period has now closed, meaning the Department of Transport can move on to considering the submissions before the regulations are finalised and implemented.

Civil action group OUTA has previously said that, provided there are no political or logistical delays, the changes could potentially be in place within months.

However, there is currently no confirmed implementation date.

So, what’s changing?

Under the proposed regulations, driving licence cards for Codes A, A1, B and EB would be valid for 10 years from the date they are ordered from the Card Production Facility.

These codes cover motorcycles and light motor vehicles.

The validity period for C1, C, EC1 and EC licences would remain at five years. These codes cover heavier vehicles.



The proposal also forms part of a broader change under which the driving licence itself would no longer expire, unless it is suspended or cancelled. The physical card would still need to be renewed at the applicable intervals.

Motorists should also continue renewing their cards as normal while waiting for the new 10-year driving licence to come into effect.

World.title: 8 million South Africans forced to live on R34 a day or risk starving
World.content:
The Social Relief of Distress (SRD) keeps millions of South Africans in abject poverty.

This is according to the government’s own definition and limits.

But the grant’s eligibility criteria prevent 8.2 million South Africans from earning more.



8 million South Africans living in poverty

To get the R370 SRD grant, a beneficiary cannot earn more than R670 in 30 days.

The South African Social Security Agency (SASSA) strictly enforces these rules.

Beneficiaries are approved for three-month periods and agree to have their bank accounts reviewed during this time.

Going over R670 means they lose the grant.

But R670 a month means the beneficiary is starving.

According to Statistics South Africa (Stats SA), the 2026 food poverty line is R868.



An adult in South Africa needs to spend at least that amount on food only to avoid starving.

The R670 limit puts beneficiaries nearly R200 below that.

In fact, the last time the food poverty line was below R670 was April 2021.

Realities of Living on R1040 a Month

If a beneficiary remains in these limits, the most they’ll get in a month is R1 040 a month.

With this, they can get food, but not much else.

To buy some food and non-food items, an adult needs at least R1 457 a month, according to Stats SA.

Stats SA assumes that those spending R1 457 on a mix of food and non-food basics like transport are going hungry.

To avoid hunger and have enough money to spend on basic non-food items, what Stats SA calls the Upper-bound Poverty Line (UBPL), an adult must earn at least R2 962 a month.

That’s R2 252 less than minimum wage, for someone working 40 hours a week.

Unfortunately, for the 8.2 million getting this grant, finding a job won’t be easy.

Rather than employment increasing, unemployment is rising.

One-third of working-age South Africans are unemployed.

What’s Next for the SRD Grant?

National Treasury has suggested making the SRD grant permanent.

But the 2026 Budget shows plans to remove millions of beneficiaries.

Treasury budgets R1.72 billion for the grant in 2027.

In 2026, Treasury budgeted R36.88 billion.

That’s a 95.33% decrease, which could mean 7.8 million people won’t get the grant after February 2027.

World.title: Kempton Park killings: Rachel John speaks out on GBV in SA
World.content:
Rachel John, the 25-year-old influencer rumoured to be dating Springbok captain Siya Kolisi, has taken to Instagram to share her thoughts on the killings that have taken place in Kempton Park, South Africa. She addressed the killings via an Instagram Story on Wednesday 15 September.

NINE BODIES FOUND DEAD IN KEMPTON PARK

A total of nine dead bodies have been found in Ekurhuleni over the past two months. The latest victim, which was another woman, was found half-naked and wrapped in a sheet on the side of the road on Thursday morning (17 September), in Dawn Park, Ekurhuleni.

Investigators are working on finding her identity as well as the circumstances surrounding her death. Between 15 July and 15 September 2026, Gauteng police discovered five bodies of mostly half-naked women in the Kempton Park area.



The first case was a 37-year-old woman found half-naked and dead in an open veld near the R21 highway, with a suspect arrested two days later and remaining in custody since.

One victim has been formally identified: 38-year-old Elizabeth “Tsontso” Moselakgomo, a runner from Rhodesfield, Kempton Park. A second victim has been identifed as 32-year-old Itumeleng Kekana. A third victim has also been identified as 38-year-old Dineo Evelyn Motapane.

RACHEL JOHN SPEAKS OUT AGAINST GENDER-BASED VIOLENCE

Rachel John, the woman who has been rumoured to be dating Springboks captain Siya Kolisi, took to social media to speak out on the killings and the issue of Gender-Based Violence in South Africa. The 25-year-old influencer lives in Amsterdam, Netherlands but frequently visits South Africa, often staying in Jefrrey’s Bay in the Eastern Cape.

“For those of you who don’t live in South Africa, let me update you on a serious problem happening here. South Africa is facing a major crisis of gender-based violence and femicide. Over the past two months, the bodies of eight women have been found in the Ekurhuleni area, east of Johannesburg. Several were found with signs of violence. One of the women 38 year old Elizabeth Tsontso Moselakgomo, went missing after leaving home for a run. Her body was found days later,” she wrote.

“What really breaks my heart is that this is part of a much bigger problem. Women shouldn’t have to live in fear of being the next victim. Women should be able to live their lives freely and feel safe 🤍,” she continued.

Take a look…

World.title: Big Blow: Kaizer Chiefs lose another striker to injury
World.content:
Wandile Duba is the latest of the forward players to be sidelined with injury.

The club announced on Wednesday that both Duba and captain Brandon Petersen were unavailable for selection ahead of Amakhosi’s league game against Golden Arrows.

Duba, who has scored three goals this season, is out for two weeks after picking up a hip and grown injury.



“He has a minor defect in the affected area, and the medical team will monitor his progress closely over the coming week before determining the next course of action,” Kaizer Chiefs said on their website.

“Both players have played key roles in Kaizer Chiefs’ strong start to the campaign, and their absence will be felt. The Club extends its best wishes to Petersen and Duba for a speedy recovery and looks forward to welcoming them back to action soon.”

With Duba out of action for two weeks, he joins the likes of Khanyisa Mayo, Flavio Silva and Langelihle Phili on the sidelines.



Amakhosi might have a crisis in the coming games, with Etiosa Ighodaro as the only striker available. The Nigerian forward has played a handful of games this season but is yet to find a goal for the Glamour Boys.

If Kaizer Chiefs are to get three points against Arrows, they will heavily rely on their wingers and midfield to get them over the line. The postivie thing is that they only play one game before the FIFA break which will give their injured players enough time to recover.

Why are many Chiefs players getting injured?

World.title: Report: Kaizer Chiefs boss Jessica Motaung to step down
World.content:
The report comes from veteran journalist Robert Marawa. He claims Jessica Motaung could leave her day to day commercial duties.

However, she is reportedly expected to remain on the Kaizer Chiefs Board of Directors.

JESSICA MOTAUNG SET FOR NEW ROLE?

The development would represent a major change at Naturena. Motaung has been one of the club’s most important commercial figures for decades.



“Kaizer Chiefs are reportedly set for a change in their commercial structure, with Jessica Motaung expected to step down as Marketing Director,” Marawa reported.

“However, she is reportedly set to remain on the Amakhosi board. The move comes months after Bheki Shongwe was appointed Group CEO, raising questions about a possible restructuring at Naturena.

The timing is also significant. Kaizer Chiefs appointed Bheki Shongwe as Group Chief Executive Officer in May 2026. Shongwe returned to the club in a senior leadership role. He previously served as Managing Director between 2009 and 2012.

His appointment was part of a wider effort to strengthen the club’s corporate and commercial operations. If confirmed, Motaung’s reported change in role would add another major development to the restructuring at Naturena.

HOW LONG HAS MOTAUNG BEEN AT KAIZER CHIEFS?

Motaung has been part of Kaizer Chiefs for more than two decades. Her journey with the club began in 1998. She joined after building a career in modelling and media.

She was appointed Marketing Manager in 2003. Four years later, she became Marketing and Commercial Director. Motaung has held the position for many years. She has played a major role in developing the Kaizer Chiefs brand.



Her work has covered several areas of the club’s commercial operation. These include marketing, digital platforms and commercial partnerships.

She has also been involved in expanding the club’s retail and licensing activities.

WHAT HAS MOTAUNG DONE OUTSIDE THE CLUB?

Motaung’s influence has extended beyond Kaizer Chiefs. Her work at club level helped open doors in African and global football administration.

She joined the CAF Organising Committee for Women’s Football in 2022. In 2023, she was elected Deputy Chairperson of the African Clubs Association.

Her biggest international appointment came in 2025. Motaung was named to the FIFA Men’s Football Stakeholders Committee. Her term runs for four years until 2029.

World.title: Ekurhuleni killings: What we know about 9 women found dead
World.content:
From left, Itumeleng Kekana, Elizabeth “Tsontso” Moselakgomo and Dineo Evelyn Motapane are the three women publicly identified in the widening Ekurhuleni murder investigation. Six women are yet to be identified. Images: SAPS

Police are now investigating the deaths of nine women across Ekurhuleni after officers found another woman’s body in Dawn Park on Thursday morning.

The cases stretch from July to September and include bodies found in Kempton Park, Pomona, Clayville, Olifantsfontein, KwaThema and Dawn Park.

Three victims have now been publicly named: Itumeleng Kekana, Elizabeth “Tsontso” Moselakgomo and Dineo Evelyn Motapane.



Police have not established that one person or group killed all nine women. Detectives continue to compare the cases and test possible links.

Here is what we know about the nine women whose deaths form part of the widening Ekurhuleni investigation.

1. 15 JULY: WOMAN FOUND BOUND NEAR R21

Police found a 37-year-old woman naked and restrained with cable ties in an open field near the R21 in Kempton Park on 15 July.



Officers arrested a suspect two days later in connection with her murder. He remains in custody.

Police have not linked that suspect to any of the other deaths. Authorities have not publicly released the woman’s name.

2. 3 AUGUST: ITUMELENG KEKANA FOUND IN POMONA

Itumeleng Kekana, 32, disappeared from Kempton Park on 17 July.



Police found her body near Great North Road in Pomona on 3 August after her family spent more than two weeks searching for her.

Her family later formally identified her.

Police have included Kekana’s death in the wider Ekurhuleni investigation.



3. 24 AUGUST: WOMAN FOUND NEAR R21

Police found a 32-year-old woman dead near the R21 in Kempton Park on 24 August.

She was partially clothed.

Authorities have not publicly released her identity and continue to investigate the circumstances surrounding her death.



4. 7 SEPTEMBER: WOMAN FOUND IN CLAYVILLE RIVER

Police recovered the body of a woman believed to be in her late 20s from a river in Clayville near the Mall of Thembisa on 7 September.

She was wearing only underwear.

Police initially investigated the case separately before adding it to the wider probe into the women’s deaths across Ekurhuleni.



Her identity remains unknown publicly.

5. 10 SEPTEMBER: DECOMPOSED BODY FOUND IN KEMPTON PARK

Police found another unidentified woman near the R21 and Voortrekker Road in Kempton Park on 10 September.

Her body was naked and in an advanced state of decomposition.



Investigators turned to forensic processes to establish her identity.

6. 12 SEPTEMBER: ELIZABETH ‘TSONTSO’ MOSELAKGOMO

Police found Elizabeth “Tsontso” Moselakgomo, 38, in Rhodesfield on 12 September, three days after she disappeared while out running.

Her disappearance triggered a search involving relatives, residents and members of the running community.



Police found her body behind a hotel near the R21. Her family formally identified her at the Germiston mortuary on 14 September.

Moselakgomo’s death sparked widespread outrage, vigils and memorial runs in Kempton Park.

7. 14 SEPTEMBER: WOMAN FOUND IN OLIFANTSFONTEIN

A passer-by alerted police after finding another woman on the side of a road in Olifantsfontein on 14 September.



Police found the woman partially naked with bruising on her body.

Investigators are examining whether someone killed her elsewhere before dumping her at the scene.

Authorities have not publicly identified her.

8. 15 SEPTEMBER: DINEO EVELYN MOTAPANE

Police found Dineo Evelyn Motapane, 38, on the side of a road in KwaThema, Springs, on Tuesday, 15 September.



Her family last saw her alive on Sunday and had not yet reported her missing when police discovered her body.

Relatives positively identified Motapane at the Springs Mortuary on Wednesday afternoon.

Motapane became the third publicly named victim in the investigation.



She leaves behind a two-year-old daughter.

9. 17 SEPTEMBER: WOMAN FOUND DUMPED IN DAWN PARK

Police confirmed the discovery of a ninth woman’s body in Dawn Park on Thursday morning.

The woman was found partially naked on the side of the road. Police said preliminary information indicated that someone had dumped her body at the scene. Another report said officers found her wrapped in a sheet.



Police have not yet released her name or age.

Her discovery pushed the number of women’s deaths under investigation across Ekurhuleni to nine.

WHO HAS BEEN IDENTIFIED IN THE EKURHULENI KILLINGS?

Three women have so far been publicly named in connection with the wider investigation: Itumeleng Kekana, 32; Elizabeth “Tsontso” Moselakgomo, 38; and Dineo Evelyn Motapane, 38.



Police continue to work on identifying the six remaining women and have urged families with missing relatives to come forward.

R900 000 NOW ON OFFER

The rewards linked to the Ekurhuleni killings now total R900 000.

SAPS has offered R400 000 for information that helps investigators identify and arrest those responsible for the women’s deaths.



The DA has added a R500 000 reward for information that leads to a successful criminal prosecution. The party said tip-offs must first be formally submitted to SAPS, with proof of the police report provided before it will consider paying the reward.

DA Ekurhuleni mayoral candidate Khathutshelo Rasilingwane announced the reward as police intensified their investigation into the killings. SAPS has not confirmed that one offender committed all nine deaths and continues to investigate possible links between the cases.

World.title: Ma’a Nonu named in massive Sharks URC squad
World.content:
Ma'a Nonu could have a key role with the Sharks this season. Image: Sharks website

Sharks coach JP Pietersen has named a 67-man squad for the 2026/27 United Rugby Championship season, ahead of the tournament’s commencement next weekend.

Pieter has named an expansive squad, with the Sharks stating: “Following a productive pre-season, the Sharks enter the new campaign with a squad that has been carefully assembled to meet the demands of what promises to be an intensive and highly competitive nine-month season. Preparation has focused on building fitness, developing combinations and creating the depth and resilience required to compete across multiple competitions.”

The squad includes 31 backs and 36 forwards, aiming to strike a balance between youth and experience.



Amongst those named are Springboks Thomas du Toit, Andre Esterhuizen, Eben Etzebeth, Ethan Hooker, Ox Nche and Edwill van der Merwe, alongside a group of emerging players who have featured in the World Rugby Junior Championship and Currie Cup.

The squad also includes a wealth of URC and international experience, with the likes of the Hendrikse and Tshituka brothers, Phepsi Buthelezi, Vincent Koch and Makazole Mapimpi bringing significant experience to the group.

Meanwhile, veteran All Black Ma’a Nonu will also play an important mentorship role with the young backs in the squad.



Sharks 2026/27 URC Squad

Forwards: Bongi Mbonambi, Cameron Dawson, Coetzee le Roux, Corne’ Rahl, Darrien Landsberg, Deon Slabbert, Dian Heunis, Eben Etzebeth, Eduan Swart, Emile van Heerden, Emmanuel (Manu) Tshituka, Esethu Mnebelele, Ethan Bester, Fezokuhle (Fez) Mbatha, Hanro Jacobs, Hendre’ Stassen, Jannes Potgieter, Jason Jenkins, Johan Momsen, Lee-Marvin Mazibuko, Liam van Wyk, Matt Romao, Nemo Roelofse, Nicholas (Nick) Hatton, Phatu Ganyane, Phendulani (Phepsi) Buthelezi, Phiwayinkosi (Rambo) Kubheka, Retshegofaditswe (Ox) Nche, Simphiwe Matanzima, Simphiwe Ngobese, Stephan Lewies, Thomas du Toit, Thomas Dyer, Tinotenda (Tino) Mavesere, Trevor Nyakane, Vincent Koch, Vincent Tshituka,

Backs: Albertus (Albie) Bester, Andre Esterhuizen, Bradley Davids, Ceano Everson, Donavan Don, Edwill van der Merwe, Ethan Hooker, Gianni Lombard, Ivan van Zyl, Jaco Williams, Jaden Hendrikse, Janco Purchase, Jordan Hendrikse, Juan Loots, Jurenzo Julius, Khuthadzo (Khuthi) Rasivhaga, Litelihle (Lili) Bester, Luan Giliomee, Lyle Matthews, Ma’a Nonu, Makazole Mapimpi, Matthew Fortuin, Murray Koster, Phikolomzi (PK) Sobahle, Ross Braude, Siya Masuku, Suleiman Hartzenberg, Vusi Moyo, Yaw Penxe, Zekhethelo Siyaya

Ready for battle

The Sharks’ campaign gets underway on 26 September at Kings Park against the Ospreys, before welcoming Leinster to Durban in the following round.



Two challenging fixtures on home soil provide the perfect opportunity for the Sharks – who recently underwent a club rebrand – to establish their intent from the outset.

“The objective is to build a team that is resilient, competitive and capable of responding to the challenges of a demanding season,” the Sharks stated.

World.title: Police yet to confirm nationality of suspect in Ekurhuleni woman's murder
World.content:
JOHANNESBURG - Police have yet to confirm the nationality of a man arrested in connection with the murder of one of several women whose bodies were discovered in Ekurhuleni.

The suspect was arrested after the body of a woman was found on 15 July in an open field near the R21 in Kempton Park.

The woman was found naked and had been restrained with cable ties.

The suspect appeared in court on Wednesday, where the matter was postponed to a later date. He remains in custody at the Modderbee Correctional Facility in Benoni.

Deputy National Police Commissioner for Policing, Lieutenant-General Tebello Mosikili, says investigators are working to establish the suspect’s nationality using his fingerprints.

“We want to get the fingerprints from police and the prison so that we can confirm the nationality. At the moment, we cannot say, yes, he’s a non-South African, but we have been informed that he’s a non-South African. But from which country, that is what we will establish later today.”

Mosikili says police are also gathering additional intelligence on the suspect to determine whether he could be linked to any of the other bodies recovered in the area.

She pointed out that two more bodies were discovered in the same vicinity after the first woman’s body was found.

“You will recall that when the first body was recovered, two more bodies were recovered in the same area.”

Police say further investigations will be key to establishing whether there is a connection between the cases and whether the suspect may be linked to any additional murders.

World.title: 'We will push back', says Lesufi as ninth woman's body found in Ekurhuleni
World.content:
JOHANNESBURG - Gauteng Premier Panyaza Lesufi has vowed that authorities will fight back after the body of a ninth woman was discovered in Ekurhuleni on Thursday.

The 30-year-old woman was found half-naked and wrapped in a sheet on the side of the road in Dawn Park.

Investigators are working to establish her identity and the circumstances surrounding her death.

Her death follows the discovery of the bodies of eight other women across Ekurhuleni over the past two months.

“Someone has declared war against us and we will push back,” Lesufi said.

“I have full confidence in the team. South Africans must know, someone has declared war against us, we will push back. We’re not going to surrender. They have declared war and we have to return it. The state has the capacity.”

Lesufi said the multidisciplinary task team investigating the deaths was working around the clock and had already gathered evidence.

“The groundwork has been done. No one must have doubts that we’re picking up bodies and there is no work being done. The team is working around the clock, and they are briefing us hourly and indicating the evidence they have,” he said.

The Premier said he was confident that investigators would solve the case soon.

“They have cracked many big cases before, and I have no doubt that they will break this case. But we must give them space to gather evidence. I have full, full confidence in them,” he said.

Meanwhile, Gauteng acting police commissioner Fred Kekana said police had received a large amount of information that could assist with the investigation.

“The teams are busy following up each and every piece of information provided,” Kekana said.

He also appealed to the public to stop sharing old pictures of bodies on social media, saying the practice was causing unnecessary panic.

World.title: Uber drivers stranded as Cape Town airport waiting area remains closed
World.content:
CAPE TOWN - The Western Cape E-Hailing Association is calling on the Transport Department to urgently intervene over what it describes as inhumane working conditions for Uber drivers.

This comes after Uber shut down its waiting area at Cape Town International Airport amid tensions between local and foreign national drivers.

Operators say the closure has forced them to wait for ride requests in high-crime areas, including Bishop Lavis.

Operators accuse Uber of failing to properly vet undocumented users on its platform.

They also say drivers are expected to contribute financially towards the upkeep of a facility they are currently unable to use.

The majority of Uber drivers at the site declined to speak on camera, saying they feared being blocked from the app.

Some operators have turned to alternative e-hailing platforms, which continue to accept ride requests at the site.

The Airports Company South Africa has referred eNCA to Uber, clarifying that the site is leased directly to the e-hailing company.

Uber says the waiting area was temporarily closed due to safety concerns.

The company adds that it is engaging with stakeholders to find a viable, long-term solution.

World.title: Indonesia cash-for-photos scheme turns animal hunters into protectors
World.content:
JAKARTA - Indonesian villager Octavius wades through the forest in rubber boots and tattered joggers, ears pricked, eyes peeled, a telephoto lens on his phone primed to capture orangutans, monkeys or birds.

The daily photo hunt earns Octavius and hundreds of others in Borneo cash as part of a conservation programme seeking to make animals worth more alive than dead.

Locals on the island have long made money from hunting wild songbirds and selling them, mainly to domestic customers.

The KehatiKu project aims to break that cycle by paying individuals in nine participating villages in West Kalimantan province for photos or recordings of animals instead.

Payments range from 5,000 rupiah (about $0.30) for observing a common bird, to 130,000 rupiah for an endangered orangutan -- the top prize.

World.title: Travis Kelce among investors bilked in Ponzi scheme
World.content:
LOS ANGELES - Kansas City Chiefs tight end Travis Kelce, husband of singer Taylor Swift, was among investors defrauded out of millions of dollars by a financial adviser who is going to prison.

Kelce was named in court by prosecutors among the victims in a Ponzi scheme, according to St. Louis TV station KMOV, that saw Siddharth Jawahar sentenced Tuesday to 11 years in prison and ordered to pay $31.35 million to Kelce and other investors, the US Attorney's Office for the Eastern District of Missouri said.

Jawahar, 38, was a co-founder and managing partner of Texas-based Swiftarc Capital, whose investors included Kelce.

Judge Zachary M. Bluestone said the duration of the fraud, stemming from 2016, and "enormous" losses involved plus Jawahar's failure to start repaying victims were key factors in the sentence.

Almost all of the funds were consolidated into Philip Morris Pakistan (PMP), and when PMP's value declined, Jawahar instead told investors it was profitable and falsely told clients their money had been made in specific investments when he never made such investments.

The court said Jawahar took more than $35 million from Swiftarc but invested only about $10 million from July 2016 through December 2023, with money spent on private jets, lavish hotels, luxury apartments in Texas and New York, fancy clothes and meals and memberships in private clubs.

Jawahar pleaded guilty in January to three counts of wire fraud.

According to court documents, Jawahar is from India and was illegally in the United States since 2005.

KMOV reported that Sam Graves, a US House of Representatives member from Missouri, had sent a letter asking a federal judge for leniency in Jawahar's sentencing.

World.title: Fitzpatrick 'not comfortable' over Dubai golf finale
World.content:
DUBAI - Former US Open champion Matt Fitzpatrick has expressed reservations about heading to Dubai for the season-ending DP World (European) Tour Championship due to the ongoing war in the Middle East.

The Englishman is the defending champion but concerns over his safety and a change in family circumstances have made him reluctant to travel to the United Arab Emirates for the November tournament.

Tour officials are currently reviewing safety protocols for the lucrative climax of the play-off series and the Abu Dhabi Championship which precedes it.

Fitzpatrick, the world number four, said Wednesday: "Being completely honest as things stand right now, I would say I'm not that comfortable.

"A few things have obviously changed for me (in terms of) perspective and stuff. I've had a child in August and that obviously changes things.

"I think for me, as things right now, it would feel a little bit weird given what I'm reading elsewhere. Things can change overnight, I'm sure, and I think it seems to be going down that path of things are getting better."

He added: "I know they changed (the advice) from essential travel only to one step better than that. I know the Tour has been on this for a long time.

"I think if the tour do go, I'm sure they have had the best advice possible but, as things stand right now, I wouldn't necessarily be too keen on going."

Fitzpatrick was speaking at Wentworth, where the PGA Championship, the European Tour's flagship event, gets underway on Thursday.

The 32-year-old is in a group that includes newly-crowned Irish Open champion Shane Lowry and Tyrrell Hatton.

"I think it's arguably the best event on the Tour," said Fitzpatrick.

"To sort of etch your name in history with some of the winners of this event would be an amazing feeling."

World.title: Refugees divided over relocation offer after months on Durban streets
World.content:
DURBAN - Refugees and asylum seekers who spent nearly four months living on the streets of Durban are divided over the government’s relocation offer.

The Department of Home Affairs says 274 people have agreed to move to the Lindela Repatriation Centre in Krugersdorp, Gauteng.

However, others have chosen to remain at Stella Park in Glenwood, KwaZulu-Natal, saying the government has not communicated a clear long-term plan.

The group had been camping outside the department’s offices in the Durban CBD, calling for protection after claiming they were under threat in the communities where they had been living.

Home Affairs previously verified the individuals and confirmed that they were legally in the country.

The relocation process has been ongoing for several months, with authorities citing contraventions of municipal bylaws.

Five buses have now transported some of the refugees to the Lindela facility.

However, many were reluctant to leave, fearing that the relocation could result in their deportation.

The remaining group says it is still seeking clarity on its future and the government’s long-term plans.

World.title: Alleged West Gang member killed in shootout with KZN police
World.content:
DURBAN - An alleged member of the notorious West Gang, who was wanted in connection with a string of serious and violent crimes, was fatally wounded during a shootout with police in Inanda on Wednesday.

Police say they received information that the wanted suspect was at a house on Ndimande Road in the Mzomusha area of Newtown C, Inanda.

The man was wanted in connection with murder, attempted murder, kidnapping and house robberies.

Acting on the intelligence, police operationalised the information and proceeded to the identified address.

ALSO READ | Grade 10 learner shot dead on school premises in KZN

Upon arrival, officers found five men at the house and identified themselves as police officers. When officers requested to search the men, one of them allegedly ran into the house.

Police said shots were subsequently fired, resulting in an exchange of gunfire between the suspect and officers.

The suspect was shot during the exchange and sustained fatal injuries.

No police officers were injured in the incident.

Investigators are also looking into whether the man was among a group of young men seen firing firearms in a recent viral video reportedly recorded in KwaMashu.

World.title: DCI seeks to block title release in forgery case involving KCB official's sister
World.content:
The DCI has moved to the High Court to block the release of title deeds and electronic devices linked to an ongoing alleged land forgery investigation. [iStockphoto]

The Directorate of Criminal Investigations has moved to the High Court to block the release of title deeds and electronic devices at the centre of investigations involving Judy Koech-Oyamo, sister of late KCB executive Rosemary Chemutai Koech.

The DCI wants orders issued by a Milimani magistrate directing it to surrender the exhibits suspended and eventually overturned, warning that releasing them could jeopardise ongoing investigations into alleged forgery, conspiracy to defraud and related land fraud offences against Judy and co-suspects.

World.title: Five killed as bandits ambush police search team in Isiolo
World.content:
Audio By Vocalize

Five people, including two police officers killed by bandits at the troubled grazing field of Gotu in Isiolo County on Wednesday.

The victims are a senior police officer, a police constable who was the driver of the vehicle that was ambushed by bandits, a livestock farmer and two National Police Reservists (NPR). The police officers were attached to an Anti-Stock Theft Unit (ASTU) located near Gotu trading centre.

The victims were part of a search team that was looking for an elderly man who reportedly went missing within the Gotu area and was last seen around Madho Gurba Huka, a grazing area in Chari Ward in Merti sub-county.

Isiolo County Police Commander Isaac Sang said the mentally challenged man from Barambate sub-location, Kulamawe location was reported missing a day ago.

The Isiolo camel keeper, reported to be related to the man who went missing, had requested police to search for him.

The mission turned tragic when the group was ambushed by armed bandits, killing all five on the spot.

The incident took place near the junction of Lososia-Merti road and Gotu-Merti route.

Mr Sang said the bodies of the officers and other victims were removed to Isiolo County Teaching and Referral Hospital awaiting postmortem.

"A reinforcement (of security personnel) had been sent to the area which includes an armoured vehicle to pursue the attackers," said the police chief.

The police boss called for calm and cooperation from the residents while police pursue the suspects.

He said that investigation into the incident had commenced.

On Wednesday afternoon, a gunfight was reported between police reservists and the bandits on the western bank of the river.

"The reservists in the area pursued the attackers minutes after reports of the killings that led to an exchange of gunfire. We are told an unknown number of people have been injured," said a herdsman from Gotu who sought anonymity for security reasons.

A source from Isiolo County and Teaching and Referral Hospital revealed that two ambulances had been sent to Gotu to attend to the injured persons.

Gotu, along with Kom in Merti sub-county is a bandit hotspot in Isiolo that is attributed to competition over scarce pasture by rival herders from Isiolo, Samburu East and parts of Marsabit with local leaders calling for eviction of pastoralists from outside the County. Several people have been killed in the two locations since last year and hundreds of livestock stolen.

On August 1, two people were killed in the Garse Dabata area in Gotu and nearly 700 goats and sheep were stolen. Nearly all the stolen animals were recovered in operation undertaken by a multi-agency security team stationed in various locations along the Isiolo-Meru border.

Interior CS Kipchumba Murkomen on two occasions called for an operation in parts of Isiolo, Laikipia, Samburu and Meru Counties that had experienced frequent cases of banditry and rustling.

However, leaders fault the CS for failure to take decisive action on insecurity that keeps on recurring in parts of Isiolo and Meru Counties. The leaders including Governor Abdi Guyo want herders from outside Isiolo who are in Kom and Gotu areas to be evicted.

World.title: Muthaiga Golf Club restores access after KFS standoff
World.content:
Audio By Vocalize

Muthaiga Golf Club has restored access to a section of its course that was temporarily taken over by the Kenya Forest Service (KFS), hours after the agency moved into the area, claiming it forms part of Karura Forest.

The disruption affected the Front Nine, covering Holes Two to Nine, before the club’s board intervened to restore normal operations.

In a statement issued Tuesday, Muthaiga Golf Club Chairman Dennis Mwirigi said the board had taken the necessary steps to facilitate the resumption of activities after the temporary disruption.

“We are pleased to confirm that access to the affected part of the course has been restored and members may proceed with their scheduled activities as usual,” Mwirigi said.

He said the board remained committed to protecting the club’s interests, assets and members while addressing the matter through the appropriate channels.

The development follows an earlier communication to members informing them that KFS had taken over access to the affected section, claiming it was part of Karura Forest.

The club had initially said the Front Nine would not be accessible until further notice as it sought to resolve the matter. The driving range and parking areas were not affected.

The incident sparked criticism over the manner in which KFS handled the dispute, with Prof Karanja, Chairperson of Friends of Karura Forest, urging the agency to pursue dialogue and legal channels.

Prof Karanja said KFS should have first engaged the club’s management and clearly explained its claim over the disputed land instead of deploying dogs, guns and heavy security.

“If they don't agree that it was your land, go to court. The court will determine,” he said.

He questioned whether KFS had adequately demonstrated that the disputed section was forest land or explained how it was allegedly acquired by Muthaiga Golf Club.

“They should have come publicly and said, look, Muthaiga, that area and that area belong to the forest,” Prof Karanja said.

He said KFS should identify the specific portion of land it claims belongs to the forest and explain the basis of its claim before taking further action.

Prof Karanja argued that the dispute should be resolved through established legal procedures rather than force. “Trees are not protected by guns,” he said.

He described the deployment of armed personnel as the wrong way of resolving a land dispute and called for engagement between KFS and the golf club.

Prof Karanja also warned that actions by government agencies could have wider implications for the administration of President William Ruto, saying confrontational conduct could lead members of the public to associate such actions directly with the government.

“When government departments behave like this, everybody now starts thinking, oh, it's Ruto's whatever,” he said.

He further recalled a previous dispute involving Friends of Karura Forest, where he said armed personnel were deployed and the group removed from an area before senior government officials intervened.

According to Prof Karanja, officials from the Treasury and forestry departments eventually intervened and encouraged dialogue to resolve the matter.

He urged KFS to adopt a similar approach in the Muthaiga dispute, saying the agency and the club should present their respective claims and seek a court determination if they cannot agree.

For now, the restoration of access means members can resume their scheduled activities, while the underlying dispute over the contested section remains subject to further engagement between KFS and the club.

World.title: Juja couple's surprise blessing of five babies
World.content:
Mercy Kanini, 28, from Juja, Kiambu County, gave birth to five children at Thika Level Five Hospital. [Gitau Wanyoike, Standard]

A couple from Juja, Kiambu County, is celebrating the unexpected arrival of five babies after scans during pregnancy showed they were expecting quadruplets.

Mercy Kanini, 28, delivered four girls and a boy through normal delivery at Thika Level Five Hospital, in a rare case believed to be among only a handful of quintuplet births recorded in Kenya.

World.title: Police to restrict access to CBD during Linda Mwananchi Nairobi rally
World.content:
Audio By Vocalize

Linda Mwananchi officials during a rally. [Courtesy]

Organisers of the Linda Mwananchi rally and their supporters will not be allowed to access Nairobi’s Central Business District (CBD), Nairobi Regional Police Commander Issa Mohamud has warned.

According to Mohamud, police had received notification of the planned rally, which is scheduled to take place at Jacaranda Grounds on Sunday, through Embakasi East MP Babu Owino.

However, he warned that the CBD would remain off-limits, saying police would not allow Nairobi to become a battleground for political supremacy.

“The National Police Service respects the constitutional right of every Kenyan to assemble, demonstrate, express political views, and participate in public affairs, but that right must be exercised peacefully, lawfully, and with respect to the rights and safety of other Kenyans,” Mohamud stated.

According to Mohamud, they had received a tip that some individuals were planning to mobilise goons to disrupt the rally, prompting the directive to keep the CBD out of bounds.

“We have received some information, some credible information, that some individuals may seek to mobilise groups of unruly youths and goons to outnumber and intimidate and confront rival groups.”

“Therefore, I make a direct appeal to all political leaders, organisers or influencers to restrain their supporters and control their crowds. No political objective is worth the blood of a Kenyan,” he added.

Mohamud assured the organisers and those planning to attend the rally that police would provide security throughout the event and facilitate all lawful activities.

The Linda Mwananchi movement is set to hold its Nairobi rally on Sunday, September 13. The procession will start at All Saints Cathedral before proceeding to Jacaranda Grounds.

World.title: ODM vows not to interfere with Linda Mwananchi rally in Nairobi
World.content:
Audio By Vocalize

Linda Mwananchi leaders during a rally in Western Kenya. [Linda Mwananchi, X]

The Orange Democratic Movement (ODM) has said it will not disrupt the planned Linda Mwananchi rally scheduled for Sunday at Jacaranda Grounds.

In a statement on Friday, September 11, ODM Nairobi Chairman George Aladwa said the party had no business interfering with the rally, noting that Linda Mwananchi had a right to speak to Nairobi residents.

“I want to make it clear that nobody in ODM has any intention of disrupting or interfering with the Linda Mwananchi rally,” Aladwa stated.

He added: “We believe that political competition should be about ideas, policies and the ability to convince Kenyans, rather than confrontations between supporters of different political formations.”

Aladwa said ODM’s opponents had a right to tell Nairobi residents what they stood for and what they intended to offer Kenyans.

“The people are intelligent enough to listen to different political messages and make their own decisions,” Aladwa said.

At the same time, Aladwa said ODM was engaged in an extensive programme to market and strengthen the party across Nairobi as it prepared for activities to commemorate the anniversary of the death of its former party leader, the late Raila Amolo Odinga.

The chairman lauded Odinga for his contribution to Kenya’s democracy, the struggle for constitutional reforms and the political transformation of the country, saying his contribution could not be erased.

“His legacy remains an important part of ODM and Kenya’s political history. As we approach the 2027 General Election, our responsibility is to ensure that ODM remains strong, organised and firmly rooted across Nairobi,” the chairman stated.

“We will continue engaging residents in all constituencies and wards and explaining the party’s agenda to the people. I appeal to ODM supporters to remain calm and focused. Do not allow yourselves to be provoked into unnecessary political confrontations,” he added.

World.title: Pope Tawadros: Inauguration of “Kom Maria” project in Mallawi important addition to Minya
World.content:
Pope Tawadros II, Pope of Alexandria and Patriarch of the Coptic Orthodox Church, said that “Kom Maria” project had been a dream for the people of Mallawi and has now become a tangible reality.He stressed that the project represents an important addition to the governorate and contributes to reviving the Holy Family Trail, with its religious, historical and cultural significance.

He made the remarks while attending the inauguration of the first phase of the Kom Maria project in Mallawi, Minya, one of the sites along Egypt’s Holy Family Trail.

The ceremony was attended by Minya Governor Emad Kedwani and Bishop Demetrius, Bishop of the Diocese of Mallawi and Ansina.

Pope Tawadros expressed his sincere thanks and appreciation to President Abdel Fattah al-Sisi for providing an example in consolidating the values of citizenship and ensuring that he serves as a president for all Egyptians.

For his part, Kedwani praised the national and community role of the Egyptian Church, headed by Pope Tawadros II, describing it as an active partner in development efforts across various sectors, particularly healthcare.He noted the contribution of church-affiliated institutions to supporting the governorate’s healthcare system through three major hospitals including Misr Al-Mahabba Hospital in Beni Mazar, Al-Ragaa Hospital in Abu Qurqas, and Al-Raai Al-Saleh Hospital in Samalout. The three hospitals have been accredited in preparation for joining the Universal Health Insurance System.

World.title: GAFI: 3,366 Chinese firms operating in Egypt across multiple sectors
World.content:
The number of Chinese investing companies in Egypt has jumped to 3,366 firms, operating across multiple sectors, including textiles, ready-made garments, solar panels, chemical industries, automotive manufacturing, and logistics services, according to the General Authority for Investment and Free Zones (GAFI).

Speaking during her participation in the Investment Promotion Forum at the 26th China International Fair for Investment and Trade (CIFIT), held in Xiamen from Sept. 8 to 11, GAFI Deputy CEO Eman Mansour highlighted the growth of Egyptian-Chinese investment partnerships.

She described the “TEDA Egypt” project in the Suez Canal Economic Zone as a model for industrial cooperation, local manufacturing integration, and export-oriented production.Mansour said sustainability is a cornerstone of Egypt’s economic development plans, citing plans to raise green public investments to 60% of total public investments in FY2026/2027.

She also touched on promising investment opportunities in green hydrogen, renewable energy, electric vehicles, and advanced industries.On the margins of their participation in the global event, GAFI officials explored cooperation opportunities with international bodies and investment agencies from Saudi Arabia, Malaysia, and China, Mansour said.

Discussions covered bolstering cooperation in sustainable investment fields, enhancing private sector competitiveness and linking it to global value chains, as well as expertise-sharing and institutional cooperation, she pointed out.

World.title: Egypt, Senegal plan direct shipping route between Alexandria, Dakar
World.content:
Minister of Transport Kamel al-Wazir held talks with Senegalese Minister of Fisheries, Maritime Transport, Infrastructure and Ports Amy Mara Dièye on launching a commercial shipping route between Alexandria and Dakar to increase trade between Egypt and West Africa.

During the talks, Wazir said that the proposed route would provide a more direct maritime connection between the two countries, facilitate Egyptian exports to West African markets and improve access for Senegalese products to markets in the Middle East and Arab countries.

He affirmed that the Alexandria-Dakar route could serve as a starting point for broader maritime cooperation and stronger trade and investment ties.The two ministers also discussed cooperation in shipbuilding, fishing vessel production and maritime training.

The talks also addressed possible use of Egyptian shipyards to build fishing boats and vessels for Senegal, as well as training programs for Senegalese personnel through specialized Egyptian institutions.For her part, Dièye expressed Senegal’s interest in expanding cooperation with Egypt and benefiting from its experience in maritime transport and infrastructure.

At the end of the meeting, the two sides agreed to form a joint committee to finalize a maritime transport cooperation agreement between Egypt and Senegal ahead of its planned signing.

World.title: FM, Lebanese PM discuss bilateral relations, developments in Lebanon
World.content:
Minister of Foreign Affairs, International Cooperation and Expatriates Badr Abdelatty discussed the latest developments in Lebanon during a phone call with Lebanese Prime Minister Nawaf Salam as part of the ongoing consultations and coordination between the two countries and the exchange of views on regional developments and ways to strengthen bilateral relations.

The Ministry of Foreign Affairs said in a statement on Wednesday, September 16, 2026, that Abdelatty reiterated Egypt’s support for Lebanon’s sovereignty, unity and territorial integrity, stressing Egypt’s complete rejection of all Israeli violations and attacks against Lebanese sovereignty.

He also underscored the importance of Israel’s full withdrawal from the occupied Lebanese territories and the full and non-selective implementation of UN Security Council Resolution 1701.

He stressed Egypt’s support for Lebanon’s state institutions, particularly the Lebanese army.The call also addressed the broader, rapidly evolving regional developments and efforts to de-escalate tensions, as well as the repercussions of developments in the Red Sea on the security and safety of maritime navigation, freedom of international trade and energy supplies.

Abdelatty reviewed the Egyptian diplomatic efforts to prevent the escalation from spreading and to spare the region further tensions and instability.

World.title: Nobel laureate Narges Mohammadi’s memoir details abuse in Iranian prison. She’s prepared for the consequences
World.content:
During her incarceration at Tehran’s notorious Evin prison, Nobel peace laureate Narges Mohammadi would smuggle out fragments of writing with the help of her friends and fellow inmates.

The risks were enormous; Mohammadi, 54, has suffered violent beatings, fallen gravely ill and spent much of the last two decades in prison, away from her children, for her activism against the Iranian regime.

“One of my friends was trying to take out just three sheets of paper on a visiting day, but the prison security forces confiscated them from her,” Mohammadi told CNN’s Jomana Karadsheh Wednesday in one of her first interviews since being released from prison in May on temporary medical leave.

Another time, more than 20 of her notebooks were lost after she says she was badly beaten and exiled to another prison. But she kept writing, unafraid of the costs of speaking out, and has turned those fragments into a memoir “A Woman Never Stops Fighting,” which is being released this month in some European countries.

In the book, Mohammadi shares new details about the people responsible for her mistreatment in prison.

“In order to document these things, it is better to speak openly about their methods, to expose and reveal their torture,” she said, wearing a multi-colored dress with the word “peace” printed in different languages and sitting in front of a portrait of Mahsa Jhina Amini, who was killed after being held in custody by Iran’s morality police, sparking nationwide protests in the autumn of 2022.

Publishing a book like this is dangerous. “There may be consequences, but this is what life is like for us in this region and in this country,” she said.

She also acknowledged the risk of retribution for talking to CNN, but said she wasn’t worried and that it was her “duty” to speak out. To avoid putting her at further risk, CNN agreed to focus the interview on her new memoir and personal experiences rather than recent events in Iran.

“If I could go back to the moment when I began my struggle, to each and every moment when I was arrested, even knowing what would happen to me, I would certainly make the same choice to begin the struggle,” she said.

Narges Mohammadi spoke about her imprisonment in an interview with CNN. CNN

“But when I look at Ali and Kiana,” she added, referencing her now 19-year-old twins, “I find myself filled with doubt. Did I really have the right to deprive them of a very ordinary life, of having their mother with them? That is the difficult part of the question, and I cannot answer it with certainty.”

In total, Mohammadi, one of Iran’s most prominent human rights activists, has been sentenced to more than 44 years in prison as well as 154 lashes, according to her foundation. During her most recent stint behind bars between December and May, she endured beatings and “life-threatening mistreatment,” the Norwegian Nobel Committee said in February, citing “credible reports.”

Those reports said she was beaten repeatedly with wooden sticks and batons during her arrest in December and dragged across the ground by her hair, sustaining injuries that left open wounds on her head. She was also kicked repeatedly in the pelvis and genital area, leaving her in severe pain and unable to sit or function normally, Jørgen Watne Frydnes, chair of the Norwegian Nobel Committee, told CNN in February.

“I was held in solitary confinement for two months in that same condition, without being allowed to make phone calls or see my family or even my lawyers,” Mohammadi recalled.

Narges Mohammadi is pictured at home in Iran during a stint out of prison on medical furlough. Reihane Taravati

She suffered a suspected heart attack in March, lost 20 kilograms (44 pounds) of weight and her condition deteriorated so much that her life was “in imminent danger,” her foundation warned in April.

After months of neglect by authorities, she was hospitalized for 18 days, suffering from heart disease caused by chronic anxiety and stress, her foundation said. At the time, Tasnim, one of Iran’s semi-official state news agencies, rejected reports her condition had deteriorated. Eventually, Mohammadi was discharged and temporarily allowed to return home. She says she is still receiving medical treatment.

Keeping prisoners in solitary confinement is “one of the government’s tools,” to “destroy a person” rather than simply executing them, Mohammadi said. The aim is to “break them down psychologically, emotionally and physically; to strip them of their identity, to strip them of their humanity, and to distort and undermine their perceptions,” she said.

Denying prisoners timely access to medical treatment is “another method that seriously endangers their health and, in some cases, leads to their death,” she said. “These deaths are a form of silent execution.”

The Iranian government and official media have downplayed Mohammadi’s allegations of mistreatment, despite eyewitness accounts and international public outcry.

Despite the risks that come with opposing the regime, two large-scale protest movements have convulsed Iran in recent years – one in January and one in the autumn of 2022 that was prompted by the death of 22-year-old Amini. Both were met with violent crackdowns from authorities.

“If you look at the streets of Tehran, and even at cities across the country, you can see how courageously women are standing tall in the streets,” Mohammadi said.

Protests rocked Iran in the autumn of 2022, following the death of Mahsa Amini. AP

“Through the Woman, Life, Freedom movement, we were able to create the power of the protestor and present it to the world; that is, someone who had come out into the streets would be beaten, killed, imprisoned and executed, but they had a sense of power, a sense of legitimacy which forced the government to retreat.”

For Mohammadi, constantly straddling the dual identities of a mother and an activist, her book represents both a paean to those fighting for democracy as well as the “words of a mother who wrote this book in prison,” with her children living far way in exile in France.

“Ali and Kiana have always been the force that brought me back to life and kept me hopeful,” she said. “I hope to see them, embrace them, and see how much they have grown – to see whether I come up to their shoulders now, or they come up to mine – and to stand beside them again.”

World.title: British university reinstates Egyptian student who was suspended after pro-Palestinian protests
World.content:
A prestigious London university will re-enrol an Egyptian student who was suspended following his participation in pro-Palestinian protests, after senior leadership initially enforced disciplinary action that could have triggered his deportation from the UK.

Usama Ghanem, 22, will return to King’s College London (KCL) this fall, nearly 18 months after university officials indefinitely suspended him and moved to revoke his visa sponsorship, according to an email he received in late August. This followed three reviews over his alleged actions in student-led demonstrations calling for the liberation of Palestinian people from Israel’s bombing and siege in Gaza.

While the university said in the email it upheld its allegations of non-academic misconduct against Ghanem in relation to those actions, dating to 2024 and 2025, it has now informed him that there were “no breaches” of the terms of his exclusion.

“The conditions set have been met and there is no reason for your suspension or exclusion to remain in place,” the email said. “Accordingly, you will be invited to re-enrol for the 2026/27 academic year and will be permitted access to King’s College London.”

The university also confirmed to Ghanem that it would start the process of reviving his visa sponsorship, in a separate memo sent on September 1.

Ghanem’s case, which CNN covered in February, prompted public outcry from some academics, who warned against what they described as a crackdown by US and UK universities that they said disproportionately targeted Muslim students and students of color for lawful expressions of Palestinian solidarity and legitimate criticism of Israel.

Ghanem told CNN he “unequivocally” denied the allegations of misconduct.

He said the outcome of his review had set “a huge precedent,” adding that he would still press for “Palestinian rights, and the fight for divestment from all of weapons and from all complicit actors with the genocide in Gaza.”

In June, an independent United Nations commission found that Israel was continuing to commit genocide against Palestinians by deliberately targeting children in Gaza. The Israeli government has repeatedly denied committing genocide and dismissed the UN findings.

Pro-Palestinian students protest outside King’s College London on October 7. Justin Tallis/AFP/Getty Images

In a statement to CNN, a spokesperson for KCL said, “A review of Mr Ghanem’s suspension was always scheduled to take place one year after it was put in place, as it is standard process for non-academic misconduct cases to set a specific review date.”

“Following that review, a panel determined that he had met the conditions agreed for suspension, and that re-enrolment was now the appropriate outcome,” the statement added. “The reasons for Mr Ghanem’s original suspension were upheld by the panel and clearly communicated with him. We will always apply a fair approach to misconduct proceedings, and have a duty to act where behaviour breaches safeguarding and security regulations, or puts others at risk.”

Asked by CNN about KCL’s decision to start the process of reviving Ghanem’s visa sponsorship, the spokesperson said, “Decisions about visa sponsorship are not made by King’s but by UK Visas & Immigration, who we have a legal duty to notify of any change in student status.”

The Home Office, under which UK Visas & Immigration falls, has not yet responded to CNN’s request for comment.

Although Ghanem will be returning to KCL, a legal case he filed against the university is ongoing. It claims breaches of human rights, assault, personal injury, discrimination and harassment on the part of KCL.

In a statement provided to CNN in January, a university spokesperson told CNN that students at KCL “are not disciplined for lawful affiliations, including support for pro-Palestine views, nor for participating in lawful protests,” adding: “It is incorrect to suggest students with different perspectives are treated differently.”

The allegations of non-academic misconduct upheld by KCL involve “regulatory” and “procedural breaches,” “health and safety concerns,” “offensive or abusive behaviour” and “operational obstruction,” according to a letter sent by senior leadership.

Ghanem does not have lawful immigration status in a third country. After KCL initially moved to revoke his visa sponsorship, he said he feared for his safety if he returned to Egypt. He has remained in Britain since KCL initially moved to revoke his visa sponsorship last May.

Reflecting on the outcome of the review, Ghanem’s UK lawyer, Franck Magennis, praised “sustained legal and public efforts” by supporters.

World.title: Huthis release video claiming to show downed Saudi F-15 fighter as Iran-backed rebels press their lightning advance
World.content:
Huthi rebels on Wednesday released video of what they said was a Saudi F-15 fighter jet they shot down over Yemen as the recent lightning advance by the Iran-backed rebels piles further pressure on global energy supplies.

According to a Huthi statement, the sophisticated US-built jet “was downed using a locally manufactured surface-to-air missile” as it “conducted hostile operations” over Marib Governate in west-central Yemen.

Video released by the group shows an electronic image of a missile hitting what appears to be a fighter jet followed by Huthi fighters inspecting wreckage in a desert landscape. At one point, the men raise what appears to be a tailfin of an aircraft, which bears a Saudi flag insignia and the identification number 5539.

CNN has not been able to verify or geolocate the footage. And Saudi Arabia has not made any official comment on the Huthi claims. CNN has approached Saudi and US authorities for comment.

F-15SA fighter jets from the Royal Saudi Air Force escort Air Force One ferrying U.S. President Donald Trump as they prepare to land at King Khalid International Airport on May 13, 2025, in Riyadh, Saudi Arabia. Win McNamee/Getty Images

CNN military analyst Cedric Leighton, a retired US Air Force colonel, said the markings on the tail of the downed F-15SA in the video were “consistent” with Saudi Arabian F-15 aircraft.

The alleged downing coincides with a wider regional escalation of the war between Iran and the United States, including rapid recent developments in Yemen, which has been torn apart for years by civil war.

The Huthis have recently stepped up their fighting against Yemen’s Saudi-backed government and have expanded their area of control. Last week, they captured a Red Sea port city in Yemen and an island near an important waterway that has, for months, acted as a backup to the Strait of Hormuz, allowing for the export of Saudi oil and refined products.

The have also ramped up attacks on Saudi Arabia in recent weeks, which Riyadh has responded to with retaliatory strikes.

There are fears mounting that Saudi Arabia could be drawn into a wider conflict as the US-Iran war drags on.

If confirmed, the loss of the Saudi jet would mark only the second time one of the US-built aircraft has been shot down by hostile fire.

A US Air Force F-15 Strike Eagle was previously shot down by Iranian forces earlier in the war.

That shootdown led to a US rescue operation that eventually recovered the crew, but at the loss of several US aircraft that had to be destroyed at a desert landing site where they became stuck.

Three US F-15s were also shot down by Kuwaiti friendly fire in the early stages of the Iran war.

The Saudi F-15SA is one of the newest versions of the twin-engine jet that has been in the US Air Force inventory since 1976. The Saudi model is based upon the F-15E Strike Eagle, a mainstay of US air power since it made its combat debut during Operation Desert Storm in 1991.

Saudi Arabia received their last order of the Boeing jets in December 2020, according to a US Air Force press release.

CNN’s Eyad Kourdi and Teele Rebane contributed to this report.

World.title: Trump’s frustration hits a boiling point with loss after loss
World.content:
Donald Trump is boiling with frustration after a spate of political blows weakened his presumption of dominance in Washington and abroad.

It’s been one of those tough weeks that presidents sometimes suffer, when multiple priorities seem to unravel all at once.

The Supreme Court’s decision to block Trump’s plan to restrict mail-in voting ahead of the midterms left him fuming at his first-term appointees on the top bench, whom he slammed as “a shell” of their former selves.

A lower court again frustrated Trump’s bid to renovate the Kennedy Center. The drama over the arts citadel, which Trump now plans to shut down, is most damaging because it’s an unflattering character reveal. Everyone knows this is really about him trying to muscle his own name onto the living memorial to an assassinated president.

The president’s authority took another dent Tuesday when the GOP-led House voted to require him to end his war with Iran, as three more Republicans swelled the list of party heretics to seven.

Trump’s big midterm offer of a $5,000 check for every American if Republicans win in November, meanwhile, looks dead in the water after Capitol Hill GOPers distanced themselves from the idea. And Speaker Mike Johnson, a close Trump ally, chose to send House lawmakers home Wednesday — a day earlier than planned — to avoid a potentially embarrassing vote on whether to impeach Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth.

Wednesday brought another implied rebuke to Trump when the Federal Reserve, under Trump’s handpicked new Chair Kevin Warsh, raised interest rates for the first time since July 2023 in a sign of central bank independence. Trump has spent months demanding large cuts to the cost of borrowing, ignoring the specter of rising inflation that his trade and war policies exacerbated.

The president reacted to the Fed’s move with a new outburst of exasperation on Truth Social. He advanced his idiosyncratic economic assessment that the country is booming and therefore US rates should be at one percent, rather than the new benchmark in the range of 3.75 percent to four percent.

Federal Reserve Chair Kevin Warsh speaks at Federal Reserve headquarters on September 16 in Washington, DC. Andrew Harnik/Getty Images

Trump’s vision of unchallenged US power abroad is also being undermined.

In a stunning development, Canada, a third of the mighty North American trading bloc, was just offered associate membership in another group, the European Union, as it seeks new friends following Trump’s sovereignty threats and tariff attacks.

And Trump’s waffling over when the Iran war will end can’t cover up a worsening situation. Tehran-backed Houthi rebels just seized land in and around the Bab al-Mandeb Strait, potentially giving them leverage over another critical oil exporting route while the US is still struggling to fully reopen the Strait of Hormuz.

Big gambles going wrong

The president’s cascade of misfortunes this week collectively point to more than the typical political dings for second-term presidents.

Each arises from a big, risky Trump bet and an apparently over-optimistic assessment of his own personal and political power.

He bitterly rebuked Justices Brett Kavanaugh, Neil Gorsuch and Amy Coney Barrett for appearing to be part of the majority that blocked his bid to sow chaos over postal ballots ahead of the midterms. “These are not the people I interviewed to serve on the United States Supreme Court,” Trump wrote on Truth Social. His critique is revealing because it shows a belief that his appointees would adjudicate the law in a way that repaid a personal debt to the president.

Democrats gripe about a Supreme Court that has often shared Trump’s vision of expansive executive authority. But at times, these three justices have also reined in Trump’s power. These are turbulent times, but it shouldn’t be surprising when Supreme Court justices uphold the Constitution, which gives control of elections to the states. Their lifetime tenure also means they’ll be forging their own legacies long after Trump leaves office.

From left: Supreme Court Justices Amy Coney Barrett, Brett Kavanaugh and Neil Gorsuch, all of whom were appointed by President Donald Trump. Getty Images/Reuters

Trump’s disagreement with the Fed’s rate hike was not a surprise. But it is another sign that his authority is limited. After all, he’d spent months hounding Warsh’s predecessor Jerome Powell over his failure to slash rates. Now the man he picked as a replacement has overseen a rate increase.

Trump has perhaps done more than any other president to erode the constraints on executive power imposed by the Constitution and custom. He has found particular success, for instance, in his evisceration of parts of the federal government by acting with shock and awe to outpace initial court action.

But the Kennedy Center farce, the mail-in voting decision and Fed independence are important indicators. They show that even faced with a relentless president, some institutions of government are standing firm.

Trump has dominated the Republican Party for a decade. But his inability to maintain unanimous support over a constitutionally questionable war; his failure to browbeat the Senate into passing his voter registration bill; and lawmakers’ coolness to his $5,000 giveaway idea suggest cracks are emerging in his power base.

Defying a superpower

Canada’s overtures to the EU represent an extraordinary geopolitical shock. The second Trump administration made US hegemony over the Western Hemisphere an article of faith. But the country’s closet geographical and cultural ally is seeking a highly symbolic break with its “America First” neighbor, a sign it now feels more politically and morally aligned with Europe.

Trump said Wednesday that the US could put “heavy tariffs” on the European Union if it allowed Canada to become its first “associate member” and if he considers it a “hostile act.”

“If it’s a good intention, that’s fine. If it’s a bad intention, we’ll put very heavy tariffs on Europe, which is a possibility,” he told reporters.

It’s unclear what associate membership of the EU means and how it would alter Canada’s huge trade relationship with the US if the current tariff war ends. But it’s clear Trump’s “51st state” threats led Ottawa to conclude it cannot depend on Washington even when Trump leaves office. A weaker North American trade relationship and fractured alliance system will ultimately weaken Washington’s ability to project unified Western power.

Equally, the Iran conflict is chipping away at the administration’s conceit that the US is so powerful it can do exactly as it wants.

The president can’t say whether the war will end before or after the midterms. Iran’s armed forces might be crushed and its economy in free fall. But Tehran’s revolutionary regime is as entrenched as ever nearly eight months into a war in which it defied a superpower.

US President Donald Trump speaks to members of the media before boarding Air Force One to leave from Shannon Airport, western Ireland on September 13, after attending the final day of the Irish Open golf tournament in nearby Doonbeg. Brendan Smialowski/AFP/Getty Images

Dark midterm vibes

So how will Trump’s week of big reversals alter his political position, play into the midterms and set the tone for whatever new balance of Washington power emerges from election season?

One obvious takeaway is that political gravity may be reasserting itself. The Iran war defections show that Trump is not immune from the ritual of endangered lawmakers seeking distance from an unpopular president.

“Where we agree with the president, we’re going to fight with him. Where we disagree with the president on things like beef, on tariffs, on the current state of how operations are working in Iran, we’re going to call him out and have a conversation on that,” Iowa Rep. Zach Nunn, who voted for an end to the war Tuesday, told CNN’s Manu Raju.

This is a bad midterm omen. Nunn is obviously reacting to voter sentiment in a solid Trump state. His plight suggests the Republican foundation is weakening.

Trump’s susceptibility to ordinary political forces is significant because the vibe last year was that he was all but unstoppable; that he had obliterated every guardrail and could compel elite law firms, corporate executives and university presidents to genuflect.

This is not to say that Trump is an exhausted force. He’s long defied pundits predicting his political demise. He engineered the greatest comeback in American history less than two years ago.

And if Democrats win back the House or the Senate in the midterms, Trump could paradoxically find new political definition. Any Democratic overreach during a promised blizzard of probes into the White House or an ideological dive left would offer an opening to a political street fighter who is most effective with a foil.

But a week in which power has tangibly ebbed from a president with an approval rating in the 30s can’t be ignored.

Once an aura of invincibility fades, political authority can erode quickly.

This article and its headline have been updated to reflect new developments.

World.title: Liberia: 2 Billion Tons of Ore- Switches Back to AMR
World.content:
The Putu Timeline

Sept. 2010: Government ratifies 25-year Mineral Development Agreement with Severstal

2011–12: Severstal buys out partner Afferro Mining, takes 100% control via subsidiary Lybica Holdings

2014: Class A mining license granted; Ukraine-related sanctions begin isolating Severstal

Dec. 18, 2025: AMR wins competitive IMCC bidding process (88.6 pts vs. Planet One’s 55.6)

Dec. 2025: Government and AMR execute binding Memorandum of Agreement

March 12, 2026: Severstal tells ministry AMR is “least advanced” bidder; pushes for Planet One

April 22, 2026: Acting Minister Blay-Archibald grants consent for Severstal-to-Planet One transfer

Late April 2026: Putu Contact Group and communities’ protest; scoring disparity goes public

April 30, 2026: President Boakai halts the Planet One transfer, upholds AMR memorandum

May 2026: AMR secures OFAC sanctions clearance and AFC financing backing

Sept. 11, 2026: Severstal notifies government that AMR’s binding offer beats Planet One’s

By Rodney D. Sieh, [email protected]

Monrovia – For a decade and a half, the mountain has mostly kept its secrets. Putu, tucked into the forested hills of Grand Gedeh County, holds an estimated 2.37 billion tonnes of iron ore — enough, by some reckonings, to rank among West Africa’s largest untapped deposits. And for just as long, it has sat there: surveyed, licensed, argued over, and never mined.

That may be changing. In a letter dated September 11 and addressed to Mines and Energy Minister R. Matenokay Tingban, Severstal — the Russian steel giant that has held the Putu concession since 2010 — told the government something it had spent much of this year arguing against: that Africa Metallic Resources Inc. has come through with a binding offer, and that it beats the rival bid from Planet One Natural Resources Holdings on price and terms alike.

It is a small paragraph with a long backstory.

A mountain with a complicated past

Putu’s modern history begins in 2010, when the Liberian government signed a 25-year mineral development agreement handing Severstal control of the deposit. The timing was almost immediately unlucky. Feasibility studies dragged on. Then came 2014, and Russia’s annexation of Crimea, and the first wave of Western sanctions that would follow Moscow for the next decade. By the time the war in Ukraine escalated those sanctions further, Severstal was, in practical terms, a foreign operator that couldn’t easily raise financing, sell into Western markets, or move equipment through the usual channels. Putu never got past drilling and paperwork. Twenty thousand potential jobs sat, on paper, in a country that badly needed them.

So Severstal went looking for an exit. And that’s where the story most Liberians have been following since spring actually starts.

A contract, a reversal, and a lot of noise

In December 2025, following a competitive review by Liberia’s Inter-Ministerial Concessions Committee, AMR — a Liberian-led consortium built around Cherif Abdallah’s Conex Group, with the Africa Finance Corporation as a financing partner — was named preferred developer. It scored 88.6 out of 100 in the government’s own evaluation, well ahead of a company called JSW and far ahead of Planet One, which came in last at 55.6.

Then, in the space of a few months, the deal seemed to unravel. Severstal began telling the Ministry of Mines that AMR was moving too slowly — that it hadn’t produced proof of funds, hadn’t cleared U.S. sanctions review, and was, in the company’s words, the “least advanced” of the potential buyers. By March and April, Severstal was actively lobbying for Planet One instead, and on April 22, an acting minister granted consent for exactly that transfer.

“What about us, the affected communities? Are we going to be silenced like before?” — Putu Contact Group chairman Joseph Geebro

It didn’t sit well. The Putu Contact Group, representing communities that live in the shadow of the deposit and have watched outside companies come and go for fifteen years without a shovel touching ground, called foul — loudly. Their argument was simple: the government’s own scoring had ranked Planet One last, and yet Planet One was suddenly winning.

President Joseph Boakai stepped in and hit pause. Citing a binding December memorandum with AMR, he ordered the Planet One transfer halted and directed that the existing agreement be given every chance to work before any alternative was considered.

What actually changed Severstal’s mind

Here’s the part of the story that tends to get lost in the back-and-forth: Severstal’s objections to AMR were never really about who AMR was. They were about two specific, fixable problems — sanctions clearance and proof of funds. Over the summer, AMR appears to have solved both. By May, the company had secured clearance from the U.S. Office of Foreign Assets Control, removing the sanctions uncertainty that had been Severstal’s loudest complaint. Financing commitments through the Africa Finance Corporation, a strategic partner of the U.S. International Development Finance Corporation, filled in the rest.

“The company Severstal spent the spring calling the ‘least advanced’ bidder is now the one it’s endorsing.”

That is presumably why Severstal is now writing letters that read almost like an endorsement — telling the ministry that AMR’s terms are better than Planet One’s, and that both bidders offer roughly the same timeline to production. Whatever the company’s earlier reservations, the practical obstacles behind them have largely disappeared.

The Liberian company behind the letters

AMR’s public face has been John B.S. Davies III, who has described Putu less as a mining deal than a test case for a different kind of resource development in Liberia — one where ownership, procurement, and processing stay closer to home rather than following the familiar path of raw ore shipped out and profit following it. Above Davies sits Cherif Abdallah, the Conex Group chairman whose business footprint in Liberia already runs through energy, logistics, and real estate — he’s the same figure who bought out Total’s Liberia and Sierra Leone operations a few years back.
