World.title: Jews once lived lived here: When houses tell stories
World.content:
Time and again, residents tracing the history of their homes discover the lives of Jewish predecessors who fled or were deported amid stories of suffering and loss.

Over the years, many people have passed through this fourth-floor apartment in an old Berlin building. Here, at Rosenheimer Straße 40, they have sat on the sofa and gathered around the kitchen table. They have looked out the window and let their minds wander.

Marie Rolshoven has lived here with her family since 2007. "The feeling of crossing that threshold, the same one the former residents crossed for the last time, stays with you," she says. She knows that Jews once lived here, and none of them survived the Nazi era.

Driven from their homes

After the National Socialists seized power in January 1933, it quickly became clear that Jews were considered second-class citizens under Nazi rule. Even the right to remain in their homes could no longer be taken for granted.

"A racially conscious fellow citizen cannot be expected to share a household with a Jew," the Nazi party newspaper Völkischer Beobachter wrote on September 18, 1938, claiming that landlords were therefore entitled to terminate leases without notice. On April 30, 1939, the law took effect. Jewish tenants and property owners were forced to leave their homes and move into buildings designated by the authorities, referred to in Nazi jargon as "Judenhäuser"(Jewish houses).

Several people were forcibly housed in Henny and Carl Möller's apartment at Rosenheimer Straße 40. In the end, there were nine of them. In the fall of 1941, Nazi authorities began systematically deporting Jews to ghettos and camps in Eastern Europe.

Jews were deported not only from Germany, but from throughout Europe Image: Scherl/SZ Photo/picture alliance

Propaganda Minister Joseph Goebbels wrote in his diary: "The main thing is that the capital of the Reich be cleansed of Jews; and I will neither rest nor relent until this goal is fully achieved." The residents of Rosenheimer Straße were among those who were subsequently deported.

Remembering at the original site

Marie Rolshoven aims to honor the fate of these individuals. In 2016, she, along with her late mother and a friend, founded the initiative Denk Mal Am Ort (a wordplay meaning both "Think about it at the site" and "Memorial at the Site") inspired by the Amsterdam project Open Jewish Homes.

Marie Rolshoven (left) hosted the niece of a Jewish woman (right) who once lived in her apartment and was murdered by the Nazis Image: KUBIN e.V.

The idea is to invite people to the very location where everyday life once occurred. "You feel a strong connection to these individuals through the actual site," says Rolshoven. "It's different from visiting a memorial."

'My brother's bed used to be right here'

Two floors below, her neighbors had a similar experience. Denk Mal Am Ort found out that the Jewish Katzenellenbogen family had previously rented the apartment.

The family escaped Nazi Germany in 1939, just in time. "In 2018, 92-year-old Joel Ludwig Katzenellenbogen was invited back here, accompanied by his daughter, son-in-law, and grandson,” Rolshoven tells DW.

The Denk Mal Am Ort initiative discovered him through Facebook. Rolshoven recounts how touched the visitors were when the former resident walked in and remarked, "Yes, I remember it clearly. My brother's bed used to be right here. He was 10 when we had to leave the country."

In 2018, Joel Ludwig Katzenellenbogen (seated middle) visited the apartment where he'd spent his childhood Image: KUBIN e.V.

Soon there will be no eyewitnesses left

Joel Ludwig Katzenellenbogen has since passed away, along with many other eyewitnesses. This highlights the importance of intergenerational remembrance, according to Rolshoven. She has already welcomed a descendant of a former resident into her home.

Claudia Samter's mother managed to escape from Berlin to Argentina, but her aunt was not as fortunate. Seeking assistance in tracing her family's history, Claudia contacted Denk Mal Am Ort. It turned out that her aunt had once been housed in Rolshoven's apartment.

Claudia Samter has already visited twice. "After all, there's no grave in a cemetery for her to visit," says Rolshoven. "We sat at the kitchen table to talk about life today and tomorrow, and we laughed a lot and cried, too. It felt good to give this space a new purpose once again."

Claudia Samter (standing right) tells 'Denk Mal Am Ort' visitors about her murdered aunt, who once lived in this apartment Image: KUBIN e.V.

Denk Mal Am Ort has so far organized 90 commemorative events in eight cities this year. Many young descendants attended, according to Rolshoven. "Knowing that they had stood in this stairwell and touched the same doorknob helped them."

Seeking traces of ancestors

19-year-old Adam Ethan Klein from Switzerland also wanted to learn more about his ancestors' history. "I always knew there was a story of escape, but it was never a significant topic at home,” he says.

"They'd say, ‘Yes, your great-grandparents left Germany in 1938, just in time. Luckily, otherwise you wouldn't be here today'."

Klein says his decision to dig deeper was prompted by the spread ofantisemitism, as well as the widespread slogan "Never again is now." (Editor's note: This slogan serves as a call to actively confront antisemitism, hatred, and threats to democracy today.)

The whole family was aware of a suitcase belonging to his maternal great-grandfather in the attic. However, no one ever looked inside until Adam finally opened the suitcase and discovered dozens of documents. He also found a letter from the Hanover District Court dated June 12, 1933, addressed to his great-grandfather, attorney Max Haas.

This suitcase in his grandmother's attic piqued Adam's curiosity Image: privat

The letter stated: "As of today, following the decree issued by the Minister of Justice, you have been removed from the list of licensed attorneys."

'They were above all one thing: Jews'

Klein was profoundly affected by the letter: "With this single sentence, it became unmistakably clear to the families that they were not quite what they had aspired to be for generations: an average German family. From that moment on, they were above all one thing: Jews."

For Klein, this was a troubling realization. So was the news that someone had stabbed an ultra-Orthodox Jew to death in Zurich while shouting antisemitic slogans. The attack occurred not far from the synagogue where he had shortly before celebrated a cousin's bar mitzvah. (Editor's note: In Judaism, a bar mitzvah is a ceremony that marks a young person's coming of age in religious matters.)

"For the first time in my life, I felt that unsettling sensation of not quite belonging. Yet Zurich is my home, the city where I've lived carefree as a Jewish Swiss from birth," Adam would later write.

"That was definitely new, uncharted territory for me. I had always thought that such things don't happen in Switzerland. Maybe that was a bit naive of me," he admits.

The subject would not let him go. Adam continued his research, determined to write his high school graduation thesis about his relatives. In the spring of 2024, he set off with his parents, sister, grandmother, uncles, aunts and several cousins to visit the places where their ancestors had lived.

A magical encounter

At some point during their journey, they found themselves in Stuttgart, standing in front of a five-story building at Hölderlinstraße 55, when a man on a bike emerged from the courtyard and approached them.

"So, are you taking a guided tour of the city, or are you planning to move here?" he asked jokingly. The man was Thomas Koch, who had spent time researching the former residents of his house. When he heard the answer, "No, we're just checking out where our ancestors lived," he was thrilled.

Adam Ethan Klein (right, light pants, blue sweater) and his relatives meet Thomas Koch (center, in reflector vest) Image: privat

Koch had already discovered that the former owners of the house, the Merzbacher brothers, sold it in 1936 for 75,000 Reichsmarks. From that amount, they had to pay 70,000 Reichsmarks in wealth taxes and the Reich Emigration Tax. The remaining sum was just enough to cover the ship fares to Brazil and the United States.

From 1937 to 1938, a family named Hirschheimer, who worked in the plywood trade, lived on the ground floor before they were forcibly relocated to a "Judenhaus." Their trail went cold in 1939, as Koch found no further records. So, he asked, "Are you the Hirschheimer family?" They were indeed.

Koch describes the encounter as magical. Adolf and Auguste Hirschheimer were Adam's great-great-grandparents, and their daughter, Ilse, was married to Max Haas.

Adam Klein and Thomas Koch have kept in touch since then. The next time Adam visited Stuttgart, he was invited over for coffee and cake.

Adolf and Auguste Hirschheimer lived with their daughter Ilse in the place where Thomas Koch now lives Image: privat

Adam was impressed by the beautiful apartment. "It was fascinating to imagine how my ancestors once lived there, and it probably wasn't that different. Back then, there was likely coffee and cake as well."

Adam showed Koch photos of his grandmother, Ilse, who had married at the synagogue in Stuttgart, standing in the living room in her wedding gown. "In front of the door that we still have," says Koch.

“It was really moving to discover new roommates in a historical context set in the past. And I think this experience — this process of putting myself in their shoes — is a deeply empathetic one that simply brings us together through this apartment.”

Shattered identities

Ilse and Max Haas found refuge in England, while the Hirschheimers emigrated to Switzerland in 1939. Adolf Hirschheimer died in 1940 from a heart condition, but Adam, his great-great-grandson, believes he "certainly also died of a broken heart."

Thomas Koch (right) and Adam Ethan Klein have presented their joint investigation to audiences on several occasions Image: privat

Auguste was brought to England by her son-in-law, Max, where the family felt homesick. "There, we were the Jews; here, we are the Germans. Try figuring that out," Ilse Haas wrote to a friend. Adam chose these lines as the title for his thesis.

Adam's great-grandparents could not find peace after being stripped of their homeland. From England, they eventually went to Israel and, at some point, returned to Europe — to Switzerland.

"At the end of their lives, my great-grandparents settled just a two-hour drive from their old homeland," Adam wrote. "When I look at their lives through the eyes of a great-grandson, it becomes clear that after breaking ties with Germany, they never managed to put down roots anywhere again."

"Remembering is important because, ultimately, we have to learn from history," says Adam. "And I think every single person has a responsibility— and the power — to actively keep memories alive. And hopefully, that can happen even without eyewitnesses.” For example, in his ancestors' former apartment.

This article was originally written in German.

World.title: Fiji declares HIV a national crisis, 1 in 60 adults carry it
World.content:
Fiji's government estimates that HIV prevalence has almost tripled in the last five years. It's expanding testing, prevention and treatment services. In 2025 the tiny island recorded 16 times more new cases than in 2019.

Fiji has declared HIV a national health crisis, pledging a "whole-of-government response to address the significant rise in HIV cases and protect communities across the country."

The Pacific island's government announced the move earlier this week, saying it had recorded 2,016 new HIV diagnoses in 2025 — 16 times the number recorded in 2019. The figures point to the virus spreading beyond high-risk groups like drug users and sex workers into the wider population.

Fiji said the known adult prevalence of the virus had almost tripled in five years in the country of a little more than 900,000 people.

The government is trying to boost free outreach and testing programs Image: AFP

What did Fiji's government say about HIV and its response?

"An estimated one in every 60 adults is now living with HIV, compared with one in 167 five years ago," the government said.

"Among pregnant women, two in every 100 are living with HIV, while 59 babies were born with HIV in 2025, with 18 dying before their first birthday," it warned.

However, the government also said that expanded testing was helping health services reach more people and identify cases that might have previously gone undetected, noting a period of slower surveillance starting around a decade ago.

Health Minister Ratu Atonio Lalabalavu and four other revlevant Cabinet ministers would form a sub-committe to "help remove barriers to rapid action."

The UN estimates that fewer than half of Fiji's HIV sufferers know their status, at least as of last year prior to the current efforts to boost screening services Image: AFP

The administration based in the capital and port city Suva said it was expanding access to free HIV testing, prevention services and treatment — including rapid testing, prevention medecine for people at high risk, harm-reduction measures for people who inject drugs and free treatment for diagnosed HIV sufferers.

"The response is focused on protecting lives, improving access to health services and reducing stigma," the government said. "Fiji is also receiving support from international partners, including Australia, New Zealand, India, the Global Fund and the United Nations."

It reminded people that testing was free and confidential across the country, saying "knowing your HIV status allows you to take informed steps to protect your health and others."

UNAIDS welcomes response, estimates less than half of Fiji's HIV sufferers know their status

UNAIDS in Geneva responded to the move on Wednesday, welcoming Fiji's decision to accelerate its response.

"Fiji has recognized the urgency of the moment and is stepping up its response," said UNAIDS Executive Director Winnie Byanyima. "It is also a stark reminder to the world that AIDS is not over. HIV epidemics can change quickly, and countries need health and community systems that are ready to respond urgently."

The UN organization said that among Fijian cases with a known mode of transmission, more than half were linked to sexual transmission and more than 42% to injecting drug use.

UNAIDS estimated that new infections increased 12-fold between 2010 and 2025 in Fiji. It also said that of an estimated 9,100 people living with the virus in 2025, "only 39% knew their HIV status and just 22% were accessing antiretroviral treatment."

However, giving medical advances in recent years and increased efficacy of treatments, it said that there was time to turn the tide.

"The national crisis declaration is a call for action, not fear. HIV is not transmitted through everyday contact, and people on effective treatment with an undetectable viral load do not sexually transmit HIV," said UNAIDS' Eamonn Murphy. "Fiji still has an opportunity to change the course of this epidemic."

The country director for Fiji at UNAIDS, Renata Ram, told the AFP news agency that transmission rates started rising around 2019 when a group of "very high-risk" injecting drug users emerged, primarily in the sex worker community.

Pacific islands like Fiji have become transit hubs for drugs from Latin America and Asia destined for the lucrative markets in Australia and New Zealand. This has also led to increased drug use on the islands themselves, often as a result of foreign crime syndicates paying their local associates with product.

World.title: Jürgen Klopp's first Germany squad includes 44 players
World.content:
Germany's new head coach Jürgen Klopp has named a huge squad for his first four games, splitting them into two groups. A host of new faces is included.

Jürgen Klopp's Germany era has begun as the new head coach announced his first squad on Thursday.

To manage the newly organized international break that sees the September and October pauses merged into one, Klopp selected 44 players splitting them into two squads across the four games. Klopp did add though, that Nico Schlotterbeck, Jamal Musiala and Serge Gnabry might stay for the whole two weeks. Goalkeeper Finn Dahmen is also in both squads as Klopp wants to take a closer look at him.

"I want to get to know as many players as possible," said Klopp at the press conference. There is no A or B team. The squads are put together in a way that makes sense on the pitch and in terms of character and experience.

"There are few names here that will surprise, but we wanted it to be a part of their development," he added.

"We didn't look at what we were missing but rather what we have and realized how much football talent we have."

There were a total of 11 new players included, with the biggest surprise being Hoffenheim's Bambase Conte, Stuttgart defender Finn Jeltsch, Celtic's Mika Baur, and Freiburg's Derry Scherhant. Younes Ebnoutalib, Frankfurt's breakout forward, was included, with Klopp saying he was a "huge talent" who was "hugely delighted" to be included.

Felix Keidel, the 23-year-old midfielder from Elversberg who has played just three Bundesliga games was another big surprise. Keidel can also play at right back, but has been predominately used as a holding midfielder since the small-town team won promotion to the top flight.

Younes Ebnoutalib scored a hat trick for Frankfurt in Berlin and was a member of Elversberg during their promotion push Image: O. Behrendt/Contrast/IMAGO

Politically, Klopp wants to win back the flag

Klopp spoke at length on many subjects, saying he wanted more from his players, that how the team played was more important than who played, and that his whole career had prepared him for this job. He also spoke on what it means to be German in the modern political and social climate.

"I hope that I don't have to talk about politics in future press conferences but from my sporting perspective, I would like to win back the flag," said Klopp. "I want us to always wave it in a way that makes no one think: 'What’s wrong with you?' But rather, that people simply get the feeling that you’re happy and understand how lucky you are to have been born, raised, or moved to this wonderful country."

"It’s more important that we have doctors. It’s more important that we have nurses. It's more important that we have a great, great many people in a wide variety of professions," said Klopp, before adding that football can "foster a sense of community that lets us truly feel the power of sports," he said, citing Zverev's recent success in tennis and the basketball World Cup.

ter Stegen one of many old faces who return to Germany squad

Marc-Andre ter Stegen returns to the Germany squad after a lengthy injury layoff, and Klopp called him the number one at the moment. The 33-year-old goalkeeper, who is now playing his club football at Ajax, last appeared for Germany in the Nations League Finals last summer.

"I've known Marc-Andre for a long time," Klopp said.

"He has the right amount of experience. He is a keeper that can play with the ball and he is also an excellent shot-stopper. Everything depends on performance."

Said El Mala was included. The Cologne youngster was a surprise inclusion in Germany's World Cup qualifying campaign in November 2025, but didn't make an appearance. He is widely expected to be one of the faces of this new Germany team under Klopp.

Notable absences in this first Germany squad under the new boss were Deniz Undav, Leroy Sane and Oliver Baumann.

Germany's international break starts in Amsterdam against the Netherlands on September 24, before a home game in Augsburg against Greece three days later. On October 1, Germany are to play Serbia in Munich before traveling to Thessaloniki to play Greece in the final game of the international break on October 4.

World.title: Australia to restrict student, backpacker visas in migration clampdown
World.content:
The Australian interior minister said reducing migration is needed to address housing pressures. The move comes amid a far-right surge in the polls.

Australia will cut migration by toughening visa rules for foreign students, backpackers, and working holiday-makers, the Home Affairs Minister Tony Burke said Thursday.

Under the new rules, foreign students will no longer be allowed to bring partners and children to join them while they study in Australia, while people who overstay their working holiday visas will face tougher enforcement.

The government is also cracking down on so-called "visa hopping," where foreign migrants who are already in Australia move from one type of temporary visa to another to extend their stay.

"If you want to come on a temporary basis to Australia, apply for a temporary visa. If you want ‌to ​come to Australia permanently, apply for a permanent visa. And if you no longer have a valid visa, you should leave Australia," Burke said.

What else did the Home Affairs Minister say about the migration reforms?

In remarks to the National Press Club in Canberra on Thursday, Burke insisted that immigration remains "fundamentally a strength" for Australia, but acknowledged that rules needed adjusting to ease pressure on housing.

"We need immigration to soften enough that housing has a chance to catch up," he said, while stressing the housing shortage was not caused by migrants.

Burke said it was "simply demonstrably wrong" that his ruling center-left Labor party was beefing up its visa rules as a response to a surge in the polls by the far-right One Nation.

This year, the group has become one of the country's most popular parties, campaigning on pledges to slash migration to the country as part of its "Australia First" approach, which has drawn similarities to US President Donald Trump.

The hard-right party said this week that it would cut the number of temporary migrants by 750,000 over the next three years to give Australians "breathing space."

The cost of living and immigration have ranked as some of voters' most pressing concerns in recent polls.

How this far-right outsider is winning in Australia To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video

What is the migration situation in Australia?

The changes are set to see net annual migration fall from the current 300,000 to around 225,000 by 2028. That would see numbers return to the levels before the Covid-19 pandemic.

Annual migration surged to its highest level of 538,000 in 2022, after borders reopened.

Data on Thursday showed that migration numbers had declined to 292,100 in the year to March, 47% below the peak following the pandemic, Burke said.

Students make up the biggest immigrant group: some 753,000 foreign students live in Australia, most of whom come from China and India.

The reforms will see Australia return to its policy of a decade earlier when those who overstayed were given two weeks to leave the country or face detention and deportation, the minister said.

People seeking to extend their working holiday visas in rural areas will enter a ballot for a second or third year.

Applicants with skills in construction and housing will be prioritized for visas, Burke said.

Relatives of visa holders wanting to visit the country will have "no further stay" conditions applied to their visas.

09/17/2026 September 17, 2026 Heat and drought set to wither Germany's 2026 potato harvest

Potatoes require a lot of water Image: Gottfried Czepluch/IMAGO

Extreme heat and drought this summer will lead to a weak potato harvest in northwestern Europe this year, according to an analysis released on Thursday by the UK-based Energy and Climate Intelligence Unit (ECIU).

In Germany, France, Belgium and the Netherlands, a combined shortage of 3,1 million tons compared to the five-year average harvest is expected.

The data shows the weak harvest will hit Germany particularly hard, with the country's share of the total expected potato harvest shortage coming in at 1,13 million tons.

These figures do not yet represent a final harvest report, but are an estimate.

"As fall begins, the effects of the record-breaking summer heat and drought on food and agriculture are becoming clear," said ECIU analyst Tom Lancaster.

Potatoes are among the crops in Europe that require the most water.

The analysis also reports a significant increase in prices. In Germany, spuds served at dinner are set to cost up to €280 per metric ton, compared to around €150 last year.

The expected 2026 harvest shortfall comes after oversupply in 2025 flooded the market.

World.title: India news: New Delhi denies claims world leaders fell ill after BRICS summit
World.content:
09/17/2026 September 17, 2026 India vows to protect trade and economic interests amid threat of US's Russia-linked tariffs

Beijing and New Delhi are expected to be the main targets of a new bill on Russian sanctions passed by the US Congress Image: Kevin Lamarque/REUTERS

India said Thursday it remains committed to securing energy supplies for its 1.4 billion people and will keep sourcing oil from diverse suppliers, hours after the US House of Representatives passed a bill authorizing tariffs of up to 100% on countries that continue buying Russian oil and gas, including India, along with new sanctions tied to Russia's war in Ukraine.

The bill now goes to President Donald Trump for signature.

India's Ministry of External Affairs issued a statement responding directly to the legislation: "India remains firmly committed to ensuring energy security for its 1.4 billion people. It will continue to do so through diversified sourcing and on the basis of evolving market dynamics."

The ministry said it had raised the issue with US officials in recent months, adding, "Its potential implications for not just the bilateral relationship but also the international energy market have been very clearly articulated by the Indian side."

"The Indian side has also made clear its determination to take all necessary measures to protect its trade and economic interests," the statement added, saying it would work with trade and industry bodies on the legislation's implications.

India is the world's third-largest oil importer, and Russia has become one of its largest suppliers as well as a longstanding strategic and military partner. New Delhi has consistently defended the relationship as necessary for its energy needs, resisting outside pressure to scale it back.

What do we know about the sanctions?

The package targets Russia's energy and defense sectors, President Vladimir Putin and other senior officials. It also targets Moscow's so-called shadow fleet, old tankers it uses to circumvent sanctions.

More controversially, the legislation allows Trump to impose secondary sanctions on countries that rely on Russian oil and gas, in the form of tariffs. Beijing and New Delhi are expected to be the main targets of such measures.

The bill would also extend sanctions on Iran.

World.title: Saint, sinner or feminist icon: How Mary Magdalene's image evolved through time
World.content:
From "Apostle of the Apostles" to prostitute, Mary Magdalene has been assigned a wide variety of roles, as a new exhibition shows.

Apostle, prostitute, penitent and confidante of Jesus — just a few of the roles assigned to Mary Magdalene since the early days of Christianity.

Artists from the Renaissance to the Baroque period, including Titian, El Greco and Georges de la Tour, depicted her in the 16th and 17th centuries as a repentant penitent; Rembrandt portrayed her as a witness to Christ's resurrection; and Max Beckmann, a representative of the New Objectivity movement, depicted her as a sinner in 1917.

Nearly a century later, she was portrayed by Lady Gaga in a music video.

"Mary Magdalene is probably the most multifaceted and enigmatic figure in the Bible, and also one of the most enigmatic in European cultural history," says Bastian Eclercy, curator of the exhibition "Mary Magdalene: Sin. Pray. Love" at the Städel Museum in Frankfurt. "She appears countless times in art history."

What do we know about Mary Magdalene?

Very little is known about Mary Magdalene from the Bible, yet she plays an important role in the New Testament.

The Gospels recount that Jesus delivered her from seven demons, and that she accompanied Jesus and witnessed his crucifixion and burial. On Easter morning, she discovered the empty tomb and became the first witness to the Resurrection. She then proclaimed the message of the risen Christ to Jesus' disciples: "She is then referred to as the Apostula Apostulorum, that is, the Apostle of the Apostles," explains Bastian Eclercy. "This gives her a very central role in the history of salvation."

But it didn't stop there.

Max Beckmann, 'Christ and the Sinner' (1917) Image: Bequest of Curt Valentin

Around 600 AD, Pope Gregory the Great permanently distorted the image of Mary Magdalene by merging her with two other women mentioned in the Bible: an unnamed woman, the "sinner" mentioned in the Gospel of Luke who washed Christ's feet, and Mary of Bethany (who also washed his feet). The Pope claimed that the seven demons cast out of Mary Magdalene by Jesus represented the seven deadly sins. His sermon played a decisive role in shaping Mary Magdalene's reputation as a repentant prostitute — something for which there is absolutely no evidence in the Bible.

Mary Magdalene's remains are in France — allegedly

In the High Middle Ages, a legend emerged to the effect that Mary Magdalene, together with Lazarus and a group of companions, had been cast adrift in a boat on the Mediterranean; with divine help, she is said to have reached the coast of Provence in France, where she first preached the Gospel and then lived in a cave for some 30 years, doing penance.

Even today, two French towns claim to hold her remains: Vezelay in Burgundy and Saint-Maximin-la-Sainte-Baume in Provence.

Flushed cheeks, parted lips, an ecstatic gaze: The depiction of Mary Magdalene as a penitent sinner often had an erotic element as well. Painting by Titian, 'The Penitent Mary Magdalene' (c. 1555–1565) Image: Heritage Images/picture alliance

In the 16th century, finally, the Reformation and Renaissance humanism brought about a change in thinking and opposition to the conflation of the three women into one.

However, it was not until the Second Vatican Council (1962 to 1965), which adopted far-reaching reforms to the Roman Catholic liturgy, that the identification of Mary Magdalene with the anonymous sinner was officially revoked.

"This very broad range of roles, which have been attributed to her throughout history and which are in a certain state of tension with one another, has evidently held a particular fascination for artists of all eras and genres time and again, whilst also presenting them with a challenge," explains Bastian Eclercy.

El Greco, 'The Penitent Mary Magdalene,' c. 1580–1585 Image: Worcester Art Museum/Bridgeman Images

A new image through the Gospel of Mary

With the rediscovery of the Gospel of Mary in modern times, the image of Mary Magdalene got something of a makeover.

This text, not included in the biblical canon, portrays her as a particularly close confidante of Jesus and has given fresh impetus to discussions about her role.

Today, she is regarded as one of the most influential women of early Christianity and a key figure in feminist theology. "In recent decades in particular, she has thus become a role model for women — that is, for female observers — but also, and especially, for contemporary female artists, who see in her the qualities of a woman who lives on her own terms," says Eclercy.

Lady Gaga portrayed Mary Magdalene in her 2011 video for "Judas" — "the most exciting artistic moment of my career," as she wrote on Twitter at the time.

The most recent portrait in the Frankfurt exhibition — which features more than 100 depictions of Mary Magdalene — is by the Spanish artist Nieves Gonzalez and was completed in 2025: "La Sfida" (The Challenge) deconstructs virtually all the traditional attributes ascribed to Mary Magdalene by artists of earlier centuries.

A confident Mary Magdalene in a flashy red coat: 'La sfida' (The Challenge) by Nieves Gonzalez, 2025 Image: Nieves González

Where she once gazed penitently towards the heavens, the painting depicts the female apostle looking down at the viewer with a self-assured gaze. Where her hair would otherwise have hung loose — alluding to the figure's sinful past — here it lies carefully brushed around her neck like a scarf. And where much bare skin would normally be visible, her body is now wrapped in a thick red down coat. In her hands, the disciple holds an equally (blood-) red skull — for centuries a symbol of transience — a gesture that clearly expresses her power.

Mary Magdalene has now also been officially recognized as an equal within the Catholic Church: In 2016, Pope Francis elevated her liturgical celebration on July 22 from a Memorial to a Feast, thereby aligning her legal and ritual status with that of male apostles within the faith. It's yet another chapter in the illustrious life story of Mary Magdalene, and unlikely to be the last.

The exhibition "Mary Magdalene: Sin. Pray. Love." runs at the Städel Museum in Frankfurt from September 17 through January 17, 2027.

This article was originally written in German.

World.title: Ayuso ignora los documentos que prueban la manipulación de las listas de espera del Ramón y Cajal e insiste en el “bulo”
World.content:
Isabel Díaz Ayuso ha ignorado los documentos publicados por EL PAÍS que prueban la manipulación de las listas en el hospital Ramón y Cajal y ha insistido en que se trata de “un bulo”. La presidenta de Madrid ha reducido todo el caso a “un señor que está manipulando las citas sanitarias”, en referencia al cirujano que denunció los hechos. “Entre otras muchas lindezas, se le conoce por reventarle el coche al jefe y por tener expedientes disciplinarios abiertos”, ha dicho este jueves en el pleno de la Asamblea de Madrid.

Sin embargo, el caso al que se refiere Ayuso cuenta con una sentencia absolutoria por falta de pruebas y un segundo proceso que acabó archivado al considerarse una causa ya juzgada, según documentación a la que ha tenido acceso este periódico. Ayuso exime de toda culpa a los dos jefes del hospital señalados y, al igual que hizo ayer su consejera de Sanidad, Fátima Matute, trata de desacreditar al cirujano, el único que ha dado la cara de los cuatro compañeros que sostienen lo mismo.

La acusación de que el cirujano Luis Alberto Martos fue quien manipuló las listas es desmentida por los correos y documentos del servicio de admisión del hospital que Martos compartió con EL PAÍS, según los cuales los responsables de los cambios son el jefe del servicio de Cirugía Ortopédica y Traumatología, Basilio de la Torre, y el director médico, Rafael Martínez. El cambio se produjo entre el 28 de febrero y el 14 de marzo de 2025 y supuso que 57 pacientes con dolencias que aconsejaban una operación prioritaria (que debe hacerse en menos de 90 días) fueron rebajados a la categoría de normal (menos de 180 días), doblando el tiempo de espera. El sentido de esta alteración pudo ser económico porque los jefes de servicio son premiados si cumplen metas de productividad, según se deduce de uno de los correos.

Madrid trata de señalar con el dedo al cirujano. Okdiario, el medio al que Ayuso le ha dado sus dos últimas entrevistas en exclusiva, publicó anoche el vídeo de la cámara de seguridad de un garaje en el que supuestamente se ve al médico acercarse y agacharse junto al coche de su jefe de servicio. Esas imágenes forman parte de la causa judicial que absolvió al cirujano. El médico apareció ayer en TVE, lo que le ha valido las críticas directas de la presidenta: “Ahora resulta que tiene que ir a la televisión del régimen sanchista y al resto de medios a darnos lecciones de listas de espera en esta comunidad”

Vox, el primer partido en tomar la palabra en la Asamblea, ha ignorado el tema del Ramón y Cajal y se ha centrado en la inmigración, como es habitual. Su portavoz, Isabel Pérez Moñino, le ha preguntado a Ayuso: “¿Qué piensa hacer para proteger los servicios públicos ante la presión que supone la inmigración ilegal? Antes de que me responda hablando de Pedro Sánchez le quiero decir que Pedro Sánchez no puede ser la respuesta a todos los problemas de Madrid”, le ha advertido Moñino, que ha agregado que Sánchez “controla la frontera”, pero una vez dentro de la región Ayuso es la responsable de los inmigrantes. “Del coladero de Barajas al centro de salud hay un coste que lo pagan los madrileños”, ha continuado. “El debate no va de abandonar a quien necesita una atención urgente, va de que los españoles que han pagado por nuestros servicios públicos sean atendidos”.

Ayuso le ha echado en cara que la ultraderecha nunca proponga nada y a Moñino se le ha devuelto la palabra, pero apenas ha dicho una frase y ha dejado la pelota en el campo de la presidenta, que entonces ha hablado de la supuesta manipulación demográfica del Gobierno central. “El desafío es crecer en equilibrio”, ha dicho, “no crecer masivamente”. “Primero ustedes ocultan todo lo que estamos haciendo en materia de vivienda, de transporte, de residencias o de planes como la maternidad, donde claro que es importante el arraigo”, le ha espetado. “Pero también le digo que yo prefiero atender y tratar como a uno más a un rumano, por muy rumano que sea, porque lleva años trabajando, contribuyendo y aportando en Madrid, pero un español delincuente, okupa y que no respeta a los demás para mí no es prioritario. Para mí todos son iguales en esta región, vengas de Rumania, vengas de Boadilla del Monte, pero que cumplas con la ley, con el orden y que aportes”, ha continuado.

Mar Espinar, la portavoz socialista, ha comenzado quejándose de que no se le permita llamar a comparecer al consejero delegado de Planifica Madrid, la empresa encargada de la compra del ático de Chamberí, y de que el Gobierno regional no dé explicaciones sobre el caso. Ayuso ha asegurado que delante solo tiene a “una portavoz que grita desesperadamente” y que no tiene nada que proponer ante las 100 medidas presentadas la semana pasada en el debate del estado de la región.

“La censura y la opacidad a la que están sometiendo esta Asamblea solo demuestra el grado de desesperación en el que están”, le ha respondido Espinar. Le ha echado en cara las explicaciones contradictorias que se han dado por la compra del ático, que siguen sin convencer a la oposición. “Tenemos a la Ayuso víctima de campañas imaginarias frente a la Ayuso depredadora de servicios públicos”, ha comenzado, para introducir inmediatamente el tema del día, las listas de espera del Hospital Ramón y Cajal, y compararlo con el reciente escándalo del Hospital de Torrejón que también reveló este diario: unos audios demostraban que la gerencia dio órdenes de aumentar las listas de espera y rechazar pacientes.

La denuncia por ese caso, ha recordado Ayuso, fue “archivada”, tal y como ha pasado “con sus centenares de denuncias en las residencias”. Y en ese momento ha sido cuando ha tildado de bulo el caso de las listas de espera y ha tratado de dibujar al cirujano Martos como un trabajador problemático que ha convertido este caso en algo personal. El PP tiene clara su estrategia y no se ha movido de ella ni un centímetro.

Más Madrid ha seguido la estela y Manuela Bergerot, su portavoz, ha asegurado que cambiar la gravedad de los pacientes para que salgan los números es un acto “criminal”. “Lo más inquietante del caso del Ramón y Cajal es que no es un caso aislado, es un patrón. Ustedes tienen a más de 360.000 personas pendientes a que les agenden una cita para que a ustedes les den bien los números. Tienen un plan perfectamente diseñado para que cada vez haya que esperar más en la pública y para que los frutos los recoja el Grupo Quirón”, ha añadido.

Ayuso, empeñada en que la oposición lleve propuestas al pleno, le ha preguntado que cuál es su “plan fiscal” para debatirlo. “Le cuento, señora Ayuso, todo empieza con que en Madrid hay dinero pero todo se lo lleva Quirón, se lo llevan los ricos”, le ha respondido Bergerot, que ha defendido una reforma fiscal para gravar a las rentas más altas. “Usted puede intentar convencernos de que usted merece una residencia oficial, pero yo sigo creyendo que lo que usted merece es un juicio por corrupta, porque vender el presupuesto de la sanidad madrileña a Quirón es corrupción, y comprarse un aticazo con el dinero de los madrileños frente a la casa de su madre, también”, ha concluido.

“Ustedes no tienen idea de nada”, ha dicho Ayuso de vuelta. “Ustedes siempre proponen y traen la miseria, porque necesitan que haya mucho pobre y poco rico al que culpar, esa es su política fiscal”. Y ha acusado a la “ultraizquierda” de querer “robarle” a los que más tienen. “Esta es la región en España que tiene menos impuestos y recauda más, y aporta más, al conjunto de los servicios públicos de todas las regiones. Pero con una diferencia, que los mejores servicios públicos se prestan aquí”, ha señalado Ayuso.

El portavoz del PP, Carlos Díaz-Pache, ha aprovechado su posterior intervención para asegurar que la izquierda “no deja de inventar casos que no le funcionan: las residencias, el ático, la Fórmula 1, las listas de espera”. “Todo es mentira, nada les sale bien porque no hacen nada más que mentir”, ha dicho para reafirmar la tesis de la presidenta madrileña de que el caso denunciado por el cirujano Martos es un bulo.

La presidenta de Madrid sorteó la semana pasada con cierta solvencia el debate del estado de la región, muy marcado por la polémica de la compra del ático. Ahora se le abre este nuevo flanco, que su Gobierno enmarca también dentro de su guerra con el Ministerio de Sanidad. Mónica García, la ministra y al tiempo la candidata de Más Madrid para disputarle la Presidencia el año que viene a Ayuso, se ha solidarizado con el cirujano y acusa a la presidenta de promover la sanidad privada con casos como este.

A media tarde le llegará el turno al tema del ático. El consejero de Presidencia, Miguel Ángel García Martín, comparece a petición propia para explicar todo lo relacionado con la vivienda de lujo que compró Planifica Madrid, una empresa pública. Ayuso y el PP no han dado una respuesta sólida de por qué se compró un inmueble que no puede utilizarse ni como oficina ni como residencia presidencial. No se sabe si García Martín revelará si hay algún comprador para esa vivienda, ya que hoy mismo se van a abrir las ofertas presentadas para adquirir este piso. Ni los partidos de la oposición ni la prensa han podido acceder a la memoria justificativa de la operación.

World.title: La estafa del falso empleado de banca
World.content:
Recibir un SMS que alerta sobre un movimiento sospechoso en nuestra cuenta bancaria puede evitar que seamos víctima de un robo, excepto si no ha sido el banco quien realmente lo ha emitido

En la estafa del falso empleado de banca el delincuente primero envía un mensaje con una alerta sobre un movimiento sospechoso en la cuenta y facilita un enlace o un número de teléfono al que llamar. Ya en la conversación, intenta convencer a la víctima de que su dinero está en peligro para que autorice operaciones que resultarán fraudulentas

En 2025, Instituto Nacional de Ciberseguridad (INCIBE) registró 25.133 casos de phishing. Durante los dos últimos años, tanto la Policía Nacional como la Guardia Civil y el Banco de España han emitido alertas sobre el aumento de las llamadas de falsos empleados bancarios.

TÉCNICAS DE MANIPULACIÓN

Autoridad Suplantan a profesionales pertenecientes a bancos a los que la víctima concede poder y confianza Urgencia Crean la sensación de que hay poco tiempo para actuar, lo que evita que la víctima reflexione o consulte con alguien Sobrecarga de información técnica Emplean jerga bancaria para intimidar y hacer creer que dominan una situación compleja Aumento gradual de las peticiones Incluye a la víctima en grupos de aplicaciones de mensajería para hacerle creer que mucha gente ya está ganando dinero

CIBEREXPERTO NOMBRE Jordi Sánchez CARGO Experto en fraude de CaixaBank “Durante la llamada, el estafador te hace creer que te está guiando para solucionar tu problema, pero en realidad, está intentando que tu hagas exactamente lo que necesita, emitir operaciones bancarias, descargar aplicaciones o facilitar información, como códigos o datos de tarjetas” Play / Pause CÓMO EVITAR LA ESTAFA DEL FALSO EMPLEADO DE BANCA 1 Sospechar de mensajes inesperados. No clicar en ningún enlace que aparezca en el mensaje ni llamar al número que ofrecen. Ante la duda, siempre se debe llamar a los números oficiales del banco 2 Desconfiar de la urgencia y de las amenazas.Mensajes como “Su cuenta será bloqueada” buscan que se actúe sin pensar 3 No compartir claves ni códigos de verificación. El banco nunca solicitará contraseñas u otros códigos de seguridad 4 No descargar archivos ni instalar aplicaciones. Los estafadores pueden pedir que se descarguen programas que en realidad les están dando acceso al teléfono de la víctima

Una estafa que ha evolucionado. Este fraude comenzó como un SMS y una llamada, pero hoy se dan variantes como la que busca robar información de las tarjetas bancarias mediante el uso de la tecnología NFC del teléfono móvil. Este sistema de comunicación inalámbrica permite compartir información entre otros, tarjetas y móviles, y realizar pagos sin contacto. Los estafadores solicitan a la víctima que se descargue una aplicación maliciosa y que acerque la tarjeta al smartphone. Así, sus datos son enviados a otro teléfono de los atacantes, donde crearán una tarjeta de forma virtual con la que intentar sacar dinero o comprar en comercios.

El teléfono puede parecer auténtico. Los estafadores pueden hacer que en la pantalla del móvil de la víctima figure el mismo número que utiliza el banco para atender a sus clientes o que el SMS aparezca en el mismo hilo que las comunicaciones legítimas mediante una técnica que se conoce como spoofing (que significa suplantación).

Conocen datos personales de su víctima. En muchos casos, disponen de información de su objetivo, como el banco del que es cliente, parte del DNI o la dirección de correo electrónico.

Si ya se ha caído en la estafa. Se debe poner en conocimiento del banco de inmediato para que se puedan adoptar las medidas operativas oportunas. También es muy importante guardar las evidencias, como capturas de pantalla, SMS, correos y registro de llamadas. Presentar una denuncia ante la Policía Nacional o la Guardia Civil.

OTROS CASOS DEL FALSO EMPLEADO DE BANCA

Cada semana aparecen noticias con nuevas maneras de embaucar a ciudadanos con una estafa de este tipo:

World.title: Mi hermano no quiere abandonar la vivienda que heredamos. ¿Puedo echarle y obligarle a venderla?
World.content:
Los lectores envían sus preguntas al consultorio de vivienda de EL PAÍS en colaboración con Legálitas

Pregunta. Mi hermano y yo heredamos un piso al 50% en Madrid valorado en unos 250.000 euros. Él se quedó viviendo en el inmueble, ya que carecía de ingresos. Ahora ha empezado a cobrar la jubilación con lo que ya no está en situación de vulnerabilidad. Yo quiero vender la casa, pero él está muy cómodo viviendo allí a coste cero y no quiere ni oír hablar del tema. Hace 15 años que no vivo allí. ¿Qué soluciones me ofrecen? R. Barrantes

Respuesta. Todos los coherederos tienen derecho a poseer los bienes de la herencia. Por ello, resulta incompatible con la ocupación exclusiva y excluyente de un inmueble que forma parte de una comunidad hereditaria aún no dividida. En tal situación, cualquiera de los coherederos puede exigir al ocupante que abandone la vivienda.

Además de solicitar el desalojo, si el ocupante se negara a abandonar el inmueble tras haber sido requerido para ello, también se pueden reclamar los daños y perjuicios que pudieran acreditarse como consecuencia de esa ocupación exclusiva, al privar al resto de coherederos de la posibilidad de obtener un rendimiento económico, por ejemplo, mediante su arrendamiento.

En el supuesto de que la herencia ya hubiera sido repartida y los dos hermanos se hubieran adjudicado la vivienda por mitades, nos encontraríamos ante una situación de copropiedad ordinaria.

El artículo 394 del Código Civil establece que “cada partícipe podrá servirse de las cosas comunes, siempre que disponga de ellas conforme a su destino y de manera que no perjudique el interés de la comunidad ni impida a los demás copartícipes utilizarlas según su derecho”.

Cuando existen varios propietarios, el ejercicio de acciones frente al comunero que disfruta del inmueble en exclusiva debe ser acordado por la mayoría de los copropietarios que representen la mayor parte de las cuotas de participación y ejercitarse siempre en beneficio de la comunidad. Sin embargo, cuando únicamente existen dos cotitulares con una cuota de propiedad del 50% cada uno, no existe un criterio unánime entre las Audiencias Provinciales.

Por un lado, algunas consideran que, aun tratándose de dos únicos propietarios, es posible acudir al procedimiento de desahucio por precario. Por otro, otras Audiencias entienden que no puede calificarse como precarista al copropietario que utiliza el inmueble en exclusiva, ya que dispone de un título que legitima su posesión. Según este criterio, el otro copropietario no podría ejercitar una acción de desahucio por precario al no contar con la mayoría necesaria, debiendo resolverse la controversia a través del correspondiente procedimiento declarativo.

En cuanto a una posible reclamación de indemnización por el uso exclusivo del inmueble, la jurisprudencia viene admitiendo que el copropietario privado de su uso pueda reclamar una compensación económica al que lo disfruta de forma exclusiva. Para ello, es imprescindible que el que reclama haya manifestado expresamente su oposición a ese uso exclusivo. Este requisito es esencial, ya que, de no existir oposición, se entiende que ha habido un consentimiento tácito.

A la hora de determinar la indemnización, suele tomarse como referencia la renta que podría obtener la vivienda si estuviera arrendada, siendo necesario acreditar dicho valor mediante el correspondiente informe pericial.

Si tiene dudas, sugerencias o simplemente quiere contarnos su caso, puede enviarnos un email a vivienda@elpais.es .

World.title: FvD refuses to remove racist podcast episode amid outcry
World.content:
An English language podcast broadcast aired by the far-right FvD party’s international arm, Forum & Friends, has sparked an outcry after guests described African people as “pack animals”, discussed racial IQ theories and described Black people as genetically inferior.

The podcast is a weekly show which, like other party operations, is funded through the interior ministry’s subsidy for political parties.

The August 26 episode was hosted by John Laughland, a British party staffer who has run FvD International since 2022 and is a mentor to party founder Thierry Baudet.

Laughland’s guest was British author Simon Elmer, who had posted a series of messages on X about Jason Arday, a Black Cambridge professor who took his own life earlier this year following plagiarism accusations.

Elmer went on to describe the “genetically determined culture and mentality of African people” and said their only use was “to destroy us and breed us out of existence”. He called people from 10 African countries “feeble-minded”. Laughland nodded along and said at the end that it was “hard to disagree” with the analysis.

“Outlandish”

FvD parliamentary leader Ralf Dekker told Volkskrant he had not heard the episode. The podcast gives a platform to voices that “provoke thought”, he said, “and then it can sometimes be outlandish. But if this was said literally, I do not agree with it.” He said there was no reason to remove it: “You should never take anything offline.”

Laughland and the FvD press office have not responded to questions from Volkskrant since Friday.

Léonie de Jonge, a political scientist who researches the far right, told the paper the English-language format was no accident: the podcast is aimed at international far-right networks, not Dutch voters. Anthropologist Amade M’charek said “feeble-minded” is a eugenics term used to justify mass sterilisation in the 20th century.

Earlier episodes have featured guests defending the “great replacement” conspiracy theory, and Laughland himself has spoken of a “horrible cabal” transferring wealth to a small elite, a phrase closely tied to antisemitic conspiracy theories, Volkskrant said.

Laughland, who taught Baudet at Oxford, worked from 2008 to 2015 for a Russian-funded think tank in Paris. Investigative platform Follow the Money reported last year that he spoke at four Russian government-linked conferences between June 2024 and May 2025, with his travel and accommodation paid by his Russian hosts, which the FvD confirmed. He has described Ukraine as “a fiction”.

World.title: Dutch asylum numbers a third lower than a year ago
World.content:
The number of people registering for asylum in the Netherlands has fallen below 600 a week for the first time this year, according to weekly figures from the asylum ministry.

The drop is heavy compared to last year, when for most of autumn 2025 the weekly total was around 1,000, Volkskrant reported on Thursday.

The drop in numbers is mostly down to a reduction in family reunification requests. The number of relatives arriving to join people who already have refugee status has dropped from around 300 a week before the summer to between 110 and 120 a week over the past fortnight.

Syrians

The Netherlands has recorded more than 40,000 asylum-related arrivals every year since 2022. New applications fell sharply after the collapse of the Assad regime in Syria in December 2024, but the total stayed roughly level because Syrians who already had refugee status were still bringing over their families.

A record 16,500 family members arrived in 2025, up 39% on the year before, and three-quarters of them were Syrian, according to statistics agency CBS.

Tighter EU rules on family reunification came into force in June under the European migration pact. The ministry has not yet said what is behind the drop.

Senate

The ministry has only published a breakdown of the weekly figures since late June. Until then its weekly press release was a single line giving one total for new applications, repeat applications, resettlement and family members combined.

Applications are reportedly falling across Europe. The EU asylum agency EUAA said last week that the 27 member states plus Norway and Switzerland received 332,000 applications in the first half of 2026, 17% fewer than a year earlier and the lowest first-half total since 2021.

The agency attributed much of the drop to fewer applications from Venezuelans and Syrians.

World.title: Nearly a quarter of children in NL have divorced parents
World.content:
Add as a favourite source on Google Add DutchNews as a favourite source on Google

See more DutchNews articles in your Google search results

See more DutchNews articles in your Google search results

New research shows that 24% of 15-year-olds have parents who are no longer together, just a slight increase from a decade ago, according to statistics bureau CBS.

In 2025, 3.3 million children were living in the Netherlands. Around 782,000 had parents who are separated.

Twenty years ago, around 13% of 15-year-olds had divorced parents. That number increased steadily, reaching 23% in 2016, when it plateaued.

Most children of separated parents lived with their mother, particularly the youngest: 93% of 4-year-olds, falling to 83% by the age of 17.

Since 1995, the number of children with same-sex parents has also increased. In 1995, around 1,000 children had two legal mothers. By 2025, that number was more than 12,000. There are far fewer children with two legal fathers, just 500 in 2025.

The number of parents who never marry has increased sharply in the last 30 years. In 1995, of 15-year-olds with two legal parents, 80% lived with their married legal parents. Only 1,500 children of that age lived with unmarried parents.

By 2025, that share had fallen to 54.7%.

World.title: Unemployment virtually unchanged in August
World.content:
The unemployment rate remained at 4% in August, the same as July, with around 408,000 people out of work, according to new figures from Dutch statistics bureau CBS.

While the total number of unemployed people in the Netherlands has risen, on average, by around 3,000 per month since June, the number of people leaving the labour force has also increased.

During the same time period, the number of people outside the labour force decreased by an average of 4,000 per month. Retirees and those who are unable to work due to disability or illness make up the majority of the non-labour force.

Since 2023, the number of unemployed people in the Netherlands has been slowly rising. In April, 343,000 were unemployed.

The Dutch unemployment agency UWV registered around 195,000 people on unemployment benefits. That was slightly higher, around 1.4%, than it was in July.

World.title: Netherlands slips again in global gender equality ranking
World.content:

See more DutchNews articles in your Google search results

See more DutchNews articles in your Google search results

The Netherlands has fallen three places to 46th out of 145 countries in the World Economic Forum’s Global Gender Gap Index, a year after dropping 15 places to 43rd.

The annual index measures the gap between men and women on economic participation, education, health and political influence.

The Netherlands has closed 75% of its gap, down 0.6 percentage points on last year, according to the University of Amsterdam team that compiled the Dutch data.

There is no longer a gap in education or health and the economic score has risen slightly, but neighbouring countries are moving faster, Henk Volberda, the UvA professor who led the research, told broadcaster NOS.

The main drag is politics: the share of women in parliament rose slightly but the number of women ministers fell, and the country has never had a female prime minister.

“I thought we had hit rock bottom last year,” Volberda said. He argued that nobody in government feels responsible for the issue, which sits with the education ministry, and wants quotas for senior public and corporate posts along with Scandinavian-style free childcare and longer maternity leave.

Iceland tops the ranking, followed by Finland, Norway, Namibia and the UK. Germany is ninth. The Netherlands was in the top 15 almost every year between 2006 and 2016.

World.title: Opposition urge cabinet to pick a route as budget debate begins
World.content:
The left-wing opposition party Pro is willing to talk to the coalition parties about reducing healthcare costs, but only if the cabinet abandons its €6.5 billion cuts to welfare spending, party leader Jesse Klaver said on the first day of the Dutch budget debate.

Klaver said it would be a “scandal” if the government fell over its first budget, but he also pressed Rob Jetten’s administration to make up its mind whether to seek support from left or right.

As the first speaker in the two-day debate on finance minister Eelco Heinen’s budget, Klaver said his party wanted to break the deadlock that led to pre-budget talks breaking down.

“After so much political unrest in recent years, I think it is in all our interests that this cabinet succeeds,” he said. “Sometimes I think the opposition is keener to make it a success than the coalition parties themselves.”

Jan Paternotte, leader of the largest coalition party D66, called on parties on all sides to work on a budget with broad appeal and look beyond “the left-right discussion in The Hague”.

But his words found little support from the opposition, which accused the coalition of D66, CDA and VVD of lacking leadership. “What kind of road map does the cabinet see before it?” Mirjam Bikker, leader of the ChristenUnie, asked.

The three parties have 66 seats in the lower house, 10 short of a majority, while in the Senate they need to find 16 extra votes to pass their legislation.

No perfect match

Pro, with 20 seats in the lower house and 14 senators, provides the most straightforward route, but the right-wing VVD is reluctant to make too many concessions to the left and favours a deal with parties such as JA21 and the orthodox Protestant SGP.

Paternotte said the coalition wanted to continue talking to parties on all sides in the coming weeks. “The perfect political match doesn’t exist, only the will to come to an agreement. My invitation stands.”

Klaver himself came in for criticism from other opposition leaders who said the proposed budget deal had already made too many concessions to the left.

Joost Eerdmans, leader of the hardline conservative JA21, said the cabinet needed to “make the choice” between his party and Pro rather than trying to reach out to both.

In contrast to Pro, JA21 argues the cabinet should cut even more from the welfare bill to create room in the budget for tax cuts and measures to ease the cost of living.

Eerdmans also said plans to invest billions in climate change measures should be redirected to help working families. “The idea that we can change the world’s climate is unrealistic,” he said.

Two budgets

Eerdmans suggested to Paternotte that the cabinet should write two budgets, one for the left-wing parties and one for the right, and let MPs debate them both.

But Paternotte urged Eerdmans to “take off the rose-tinted glasses”. “How does that get you to a majority in the Senate?” he said. “Pro or JA21 on their own aren’t enough.”

Klaver’s pitch to the cabinet also prompted Socialist Party leader Jimmy Dijk to ask how far Pro was willing to compromise on healthcare spending.

Pro would not “work to break things down”, Klaver replied, but he saw potential to make savings by tackling “all kinds of treatments that aren’t necessary” and “taking the market out of youth care”.

Draft published

Paternotte also said D66 was willing to discuss surrogate parenthood with the SGP, which wants the cabinet to block any moves to legalise the practice as a condition for its support.

MPs also voted to ask the cabinet to publish the original draft budget by finance minister Eelco Heinen which was rejected by his coalition partners, prompting an extra weekend of negotiations.

NRC reported that the original version preserved most of the plans to cut welfare spending, despite Pro pressing for them to be taken off the table. In both the draft and the final version Heinen proposed delaying around half the cuts by a year.

World.title: Unpublished princess Diana memorial books stolen in NL
World.content:
Copies of an unpublished book about Diana, princess of Wales, written by her brother Earl Spencer, have been stolen from a truck in the Netherlands.

Four copies of the book, which was en route from a printing plant to a warehouse, were taken while the truck driver was sleeping in his cab in a car park, according to the BBC. Dutch publisher Overamstel has the rights to the book in the Netherlands.

The book, titled Swan Song: Diana, My Sister is highly anticipated as it is said to contain details about her personal life and unhappy marriage to then prince Charles, now the king. It also describes the crisis in the royal family that followed her death.

A source told British paper the Daily Mail that the theft was highly suspicious. “Nothing like this has ever happened before. This is probably the biggest book of the year and the security surrounding it has been incredibly tight.”

“Every possible precaution has been taken to prevent it from being leaked ahead of its serialisation. Therefore this unprecedented incident is being taken extremely seriously.”

The Dutch police are reportedly investigating the theft.

World.title: Seven men arrested as police step up illegal fireworks crackdown
World.content:
Seven men have been arrested after police intercepted several consignments of illegal fireworks from Germany over the weekend.

The suspects, aged between 31 and 60, were stopped while transporting 2,600kg of explosives to Arnhem, Heijen and Urk on Saturday.

Police said the fireworks were in the most restricted category, F4, intended for professional use only, which were already illegal before a wider ban on importing and possessing fireworks came into force on August 1.

Only the lightest category, which includes sparklers and Roman candles, will be allowed from this year, following years of campaigning by doctors and emergency services.

Police have said they will adopt a zero tolerance approach to illegal explosives in the run-up to New Year, including monitoring border crossings and checking vehicles that have been used in the past to import fireworks.

Last month a 22-year-old man from Oss was arrested after police seized a consignment of 1,200kg of fireworks in Schaijk, Noord-Brabant, one of the first major hauls since the ban took effect.

World.title: Polish right-wing opposition MPs call for Independence Day march in Ukrainian city of Lviv

A group of MPs from Poland’s main right-wing and far-right opposition parties have jointly called on the government to organise a march on Polish Independence Day in the Ukrainian city of Lviv, which was historically part of Poland. The idea has been firmly rejected by figures from the ruling coalition, who have called it “gross stupidity” and “madness”. It is also unclear to what extent the leadership of the opposition parties support the proposal. Pomysł zorganizowania "polskiego Marszu Niepodległości ulicami Lwowa" połączył polityków całej prawicy: PiS, Konfederacji, Rozwoju Plus i Konfederacji Korony Polskiej. Odsłaniamy kulisy. Pisze @patrykmichalski, autor programu #NewsMichalskiego ⤵️ 🔵 https://t.co/9L0M5lN0zY pic.twitter.com/1W3YxHdXHT — TVN24+ (@tvn24plus) September 15, 2026 The suggestion was made in a so-called parliamentary interpellation – through which MPs can ask questions and make suggestions to the government – submitted this month and signed by a group of 21 opposition MPs. They called on the government to do more to support the ethnic Polish community that still lives in Lviv, arguing that neither the Polish nor the Ukrainian state does enough to help them preserve and celebrate their identity. By contrast, argued the signatories, Polish state entities provide funding for Ukrainian organisations and events in Poland, including celebrations of Ukrainian Independence Day on 24 August. As such, they called upon the government to “organise official celebrations of [Polish] Independence Day in Lviv, including a Polish Independence March through the streets of the city” on 11 November. This would be “a concrete sign of remembrance and solidarity with Poles living in Ukraine”. Among the 21 signatories, 14 are from the caucus of the national-conservative Law and Justice (PiS), Poland’s ruling party between 2015 and 2023 and now the largest opposition group. A further three are from Confederation (Konfederacja), a far-right opposition group. One is from Development Plus (Rozwój Plus), a group that broke away from PiS earlier this year; another is from Confederation of the Polish Crown (KKP), a radical-right, pro-Russian party led by Grzegorz Braun. The final two are an independent, Janusz Kowalski, who recently quit PiS; and Jarosław Sachajko, who was elected in 2023 on the PiS party list but is part of the small Direct Democracy (Demokracja Bezpośrednia) group associated with Paweł Kukiz, a right-wing, anti-establishment figure. Interpelacja do Prezesa Rady Ministrów w sprawie zorganizowania 11 listopada polskiego Marszu Niepodległości ulicami Lwowa 11 listopada Rzeczpospolita Polska obchodzi Narodowe Święto Niepodległości. Jest to święto wszystkich Polaków, również tych, którzy mieszkają poza granicami… pic.twitter.com/7m6yUg1iKZ — Dariusz Matecki (@DariuszMatecki) August 25, 2026 It remains unclear to what extent the MPs have the backing of their parties in calling for the government to organise an Independence Day march in Lviv. Indeed, when Krzysztof Bosak, one of the leaders of Confederation, was asked about the idea on Wednesday, he appeared to know very little about it. Speaking to broadcaster RMF, Bosak said that he had first heard about the proposal on Tuesday and that, after looking into it, he said it appeared to be a “stunt”, and one that he felt was “unnecessary”. “I think the point is to draw attention to the fact that Polish institutions are participating in the celebration of Ukraine’s Independence Day in Warsaw, and that there should be some symmetry,” said Bosak. However, he added that he felt many people would not understand this intention. “The appeal should be directed at Ukrainian institutions, not the Polish foreign ministry,” he said, adding that the MPs who came up with the idea should better explain it. “Frankly, I have more serious matters to attend to.” Czy przemarsz Polaków ulicami Lwowa z okazji Dnia Niepodległości to dobry pomysł? Zdaniem @krzysztofbosak niepotrzebny, a traktować go należy w kategorii happeningu. Ale jeśli się trzymać zasady wzajemności, to już lepiej organizować coś podobnego… w Kijowie. pic.twitter.com/PxdqNKBlCC — Ekonomat (@ekonomat_pl) September 16, 2026 Throughout much of history, Lviv (known in Polish as Lwów) was part of the Polish state, most recently during the period between the First and Second World Wars. However, amid postwar border movements, it became part of Ukraine along with some other former Polish territories. Many in Poland still feel a sense of attachment to the former Polish “borderlands” (kresy) that are now located in Ukraine, Lithuania and Belarus, and which are still home to at least hundreds of thousands of ethnic Poles (though the exact number is a matter of dispute). In Lviv itself, the most recent Ukrainian national census, taken in 2001, showed just under 10,000 people declaring Polish ethnicity in the city (around 1% of the population), though some estimates put the figure higher. Poland's culture minister has condemned Russia's attacks on the historic centre of Lviv in Ukraine, a UNESCO World Heritage site. She noted that Lviv, which was once part of Poland, represents the "shared history of Ukraine, Poland and all of Europe" https://t.co/qPhqXMAZ9r — Notes from Poland 🇵🇱 (@notesfrompoland) March 25, 2026 Last year, Confederation’s other main leader, Sławomir Mentzen, clashed with the mayor of Lviv, Andriy Sadovyi, after visiting the city and criticising a monument commemorating nationalist leader Stepan Bandera, a figure seen as a hero by many in Ukraine but regarded as a war criminal in Poland. Followers of Bandera were responsible for the so-called Volhynia massacres during World War Two, in which Ukrainian nationalists massacred around 100,000 ethnic Polish civilians. Poland regards the killings as a genocide but Ukraine rejects that label. The issue has caused renewed tension this year after President Volodymyr Zelensky named a Ukrainian military unit after the “heroes of the Ukrainian Insurgent Army”, which led the massacres. Any Polish attempt at a state-backed Independence Day march in Ukraine would likely stir further controversy. A leading candidate in Poland’s presidential election has clashed with a Ukrainian mayor after visiting his city and criticising the presence of a monument to Stepan Bandera, who is seen as a hero by many in Ukraine but regarded as a war criminal in Poland https://t.co/nA9JzMmBcg — Notes from Poland 🇵🇱 (@notesfrompoland) February 26, 2025 Although the Polish government has not yet officially responded to the opposition MPs’ interpellation, a number of figures from the ruling coalition – which ranges from left to centre right – criticised the idea on Wednesday. Deputy defence minister Cezary Tomczyk called it “gross stupidity” to think of organising such a march in Ukraine, especially at a time of war. He asked how Poles would feel if Germany tried to organise a similar march in Poland (some of whose current territory was part of Germany before World War Two). Both Dariusz Wieczorek, an MP from The Left (Lewica), and Marek Biernacki from the centre-right Polish People’s Party (PSL) told broadcaster TVN that the idea was “madness”. Próba zorganizowania we Lwowie prawicowej prowokacji z udziałem PiS-u, Rozwój Plus i Brauna to jednoznaczne działanie na rzecz Rosji i przeciwko polskiej racji stanu. — Witold Zembaczyński🇵🇱 (@WZembaczynski) September 16, 2026 Notes from Poland is run by a small editorial team and published by an independent, non-profit foundation that is funded through donations from our readers.
