World.title: European Parliament strips Polish far-right leader of immunity to face Holocaust denial charge
World.content: Keep our news free from ads and paywalls by making a donation to support our work! Notes from Poland is run by a small editorial team and is published by an independent, non-profit foundation that is funded through donations from our readers. We cannot do what we do without your support. The European Parliament has again stripped Polish far-right leader Grzegorz Braun of legal immunity to face charges in his homeland of denying Nazi crimes, an offence that carries a potential prison sentence of up to three years. The decision marks the sixth time that the European Parliament has lifted Braun’s immunity, and the second time for charges of Holocaust denial. Braun is already on trial in Poland for an attack on a Jewish religious celebration in parliament and is facing a number of other legal cases. Parlament Europejski w głosowaniu w Strasburgu uchylił immunitet europosła Grzegorza Brauna. Sprawa dotyczy negowania przez niego Holokaustu. Więcej: https://t.co/rB3UPUiS8o pic.twitter.com/icRLEqsWmF — Gazeta.pl (@gazetapl_news) September 15, 2026 In a vote on Tuesday, a majority of MEPs voted in favour of a request, submitted in February by Poland’s justice minister, Waldemar Żurek, to lift the immunity enjoyed by Braun as an MEP. He has sat in the European Parliament since being elected in 2024. In his request, Żurek said that Polish prosecutors wish to charge Braun in relation to “denial of genocide crimes committed by functionaries of the Third Reich in the Auschwitz-Birkenau concentration camp and the Lublin concentration camp (Majdanek)”. Poland’s Institute of National Remembrance (IPN), a state historical body that has prosecutorial power, also revealed that the accusation relates to the use of gas chambers at those two camps. Neither the IPN nor Żurek confirmed at the time what specific words Braun had said that prompted the planned charges against him. However, the IPN noted that they had come at a live event broadcast online on 27 September 2025. On that date, Braun took part in a discussion with Jan Żaryn, a right-wing historian and former senator for the national-conservative Law and Justice (PiS) party, titled “The Polish Underground State and the Jewish Issue”. A recording of the event is still available online. During his remarks, Braun referred to the “fake gas chambers of Majdanek and Auschwitz”, calling them “a dark, monstrous fantasy that has no satisfactory historical or academic support”. He suggested that the idea of the gas chambers had been invented as part of “propaganda and black PR operations conducted by the Soviet and Anglo-Saxon security services during World War Two”, and that the false claim continues to be exploited by Jews today. The European Parliament has again voted to strip Polish far-right leader Grzegorz Braun of immunity to face further charges for Holocaust denial as well as various antisemitic, anti-Ukrainian and anti-LGBT incidents during last year's presidential campaign https://t.co/4EHVEuSDnM — Notes from Poland 🇵🇱 (@notesfrompoland) March 26, 2026 In actual fact, historians estimate that around 900,000 people were killed in the gas chambers at Auschwitz. The vast majority were Jews, but victims also included Roma, Soviet prisoners of war, and ethnic Poles. Meanwhile, gas chambers at Majdanek were used to kill tens of thousands, again mainly Jews. Today, the ashes of the camp’s cremated victims are preserved in a memorial at the site of the former camp. Braun, who has a long history of promoting antisemitic conspiracy theories, has repeatedly sought to cast doubt on the veracity of Nazi crimes against Jews. Last month, he was charged with denying Nazi crimes in a separate case over earlier comments in which he called Auschwitz’s gas chambers “fake”. Polish far-right leader Grzegorz Braun has been charged with denying Nazi crimes, a criminal offence in Poland that carries a prison sentence of up to three years, for statements he made suggesting that the gas chambers at Auschwitz are "fake" https://t.co/PCssZt5eXD — Notes from Poland 🇵🇱 (@notesfrompoland) August 25, 2026 In December, Braun went on trial over a separate set of charges relating to four other incidents, including his attack on a celebration of the Jewish festival of Hanukkah in parliament in December 2023 and his disruption of a lecture by a Holocaust scholar. “I am standing before this court because I dared to defend myself against oppression and the ritual manifestation of Jewish supremacy,” declared Braun at the start of the trial, which remains ongoing. Braun is also facing various legal cases relating to his anti-Ukrainian and anti-LGBT actions. Last week, he posted a video of himself using a hammer to vandalise a monument in Poland dedicated to the Ukrainian Insurgent Army (UPA). Police are investigating that incident. Polish far-right leader Grzegorz Braun has published a video of himself using a hammer to attack a monument in Poland to soldiers from the Ukrainian Insurgent Army, a WWII group that fought against the Soviets but was also responsible for massacring Poles https://t.co/oCYRtNRO9N — Notes from Poland 🇵🇱 (@notesfrompoland) September 11, 2026 Braun’s high-profile stunts have seen his popularity surge among a section of the electorate. He finished a surprise fourth in last year’s Polish presidential election, with over 6% of the vote, and his Confederation of the Polish Crown (KKP) party is now polling around 8-9%. If it manages to secure that level of support at next year’s parliamentary elections, KKP could become a key player in deciding what kind of government can be formed after what looks likely to be a very close contest between the ruling coalition, which ranges from left to centre right, and the right-wing and far-right opposition. An MEP from the ruling coalition, Michał Kobosko, welcomed Tuesday’s decision to lift Braun’s immunity, saying that the far-right leader “deliberately and consciously…stokes hatred”. Kobosko said that such actions are particularly dangerous at a time when Russia is “actively waging hybrid and cognitive war against Poland”. He noted that Braun and his party have taken a sympathetic position towards Russia, including calling for Poland to “normalise” relations with Moscow. Figures from Polish far-right leader Grzegorz Braun's party celebrated Russia Day at the Russian embassy and presented a letter hailing Russia's development, blaming "globalists" for the Ukraine war and calling for normalisation of Polish-Russian relations https://t.co/SU3gEdVod0 — Notes from Poland 🇵🇱 (@notesfrompoland) June 13, 2026 Notes from Poland is run by a small editorial team and published by an independent, non-profit foundation that is funded through donations from our readers. World.title: China overtakes Germany as Poland’s biggest source of imports for first time
World.content: Keep our news free from ads and paywalls by making a donation to support our work! Notes from Poland is run by a small editorial team and is published by an independent, non-profit foundation that is funded through donations from our readers. We cannot do what we do without your support. China overtook Germany to become Poland’s biggest source of imports for the first time in July, according to new data from the central bank. It ends a period of around 35 years in which Germany had consistently held top spot. The shift came as imports of Chinese goods surged, driven in part by a sharp increase in Chinese cars, while imports from Germany declined. “In July 2026, China was the largest supplier of goods to Poland for the first time, overtaking Germany in that month,” wrote the National Bank of Poland (NBP) in an announcement on Monday. “A significant increase in imports of computer hardware, passenger cars and durable consumer goods influenced the shift in the geographical structure of imports,” added the bank. Znamy już pełne dane handlowe za lipiec 2026 – za miesiąc kiedy Chiny po raz pierwszy w historii stały się największym dostawcą towarów do Polski, przed Niemcami. W lipcu import ogółem z Chin wzrósł o 28,8% r/r, podczas gdy z Niemiec spadł o 1,8% r/r. Import pojazdów… pic.twitter.com/LfJ50nXzNM — PKO Research (@PKO_Research) September 15, 2026 In a comment on the new data, analysts at PKO, a Polish bank, said that the July shift was partly due to “one-time factors” and noted that Germany remains Poland’s largest supplier on a 12-month basis, although its lead has been steadily shrinking. In July, Polish imports from China rose 28.8% year-on-year, while imports from Germany fell 1.8%, according to PKO. Imports of motor vehicles from Germany fell 9.3% year-on-year, while imports from China rose 54.4%. Imports from China of computers, electronics and optical equipment rose 31.5% year-on-year in July, the strongest increase since 2022. More detailed data on trade with the two countries, published also on Tuesday by Statistics Poland (GUS), a state agency, provided further insight into the shift. According to GUS, Poland imported goods worth €36.7 billion from China in the first seven months of the year, giving China a 15.9% share of total Polish imports, up from 14.9% in the same period of 2025. Imports from Germany stood at €43.1 billion in that period, 18.6% of the total, down from 19.4% in 2025. Poland’s third-largest source of imports was the United States, with €12.7 worth of goods, a share of 5.5%, up from 4.9% in 2025. Poland has been NATO's biggest importer of arms over the last five years, according to new data from @SIPRIorg. Over 90% of Polish imports have come from South Korea and the United States https://t.co/jij0nfbhFc — Notes from Poland 🇵🇱 (@notesfrompoland) March 9, 2026 Germany has been Poland’s largest trading partner since the collapse of communism, leading both in imports and exports. It overtook the Soviet Union, which had dominated Poland’s foreign trade during the communist era. But China has steadily gained ground as a source of Polish imports since the 2010s, rising to second place behind Germany by the 2020s. In terms of exports in the first seven months of this year, Germany dominates, receiving goods worth €69.8 billion, or 26.3% of all Poland’s exports. It is followed by the Czech Republic (€14.3 billion), France (€14.0 billion), the United Kingdom (€11.6 billion) and the Netherlands (€10.9 billion). Prime Minister Donald Tusk says that Poland has been “disgraced in front of the entire world” by a new Financial Times report on how Polish state energy firm Orlen lost $230 million (856 million zloty) trying to buy Venezuelan oil through intermediaries, unsecured payments and cryptocurrency transfers. Tusk called the case a further example of “dirty deals” conducted under the former national-conservative Law and Justice (PiS) government, which was in power at the time. Orlen was then led by Daniel Obajtek, who is now a member of the European Parliament representing PiS. Obajtek himself today said that he wants the issue to be clarified in court and suggested that the current authorities are using the case to distract from current soaring fuel prices. How Poland lost $230mn trying to buy Venezuelan oil with crypto https://t.co/Xo07JkYy1t — Financial Times (@FT) September 15, 2026 In a report today, the FT provided new details on a case that has already drawn public attention in Poland. In April 2024, Orlen revealed that its Swiss oil trading subsidiary had lost around $400 million in prepayments for Venezuelan oil and petroleum products that were never delivered. Orlen, which was under new management after Obajtek had been fired earlier that year following the arrival of Tusk’s government, said that the losses included around $240 million paid to a Dubai-based intermediary run by a 25-year-old from Hong Kong. A week later, Polish prosecutors announced that they had launched an investigation into the case, focusing on Orlen Trading Switzerland (OTS), the subsidiary that oversaw the Venezuela deal. Polish prosecutors have launched an investigation into OTS, @GrupaORLEN's Swiss subsidiary which had lost $400 million on prepayments for oil that was never delivered. It also announced that the homes of Orlen's former senior management had been searchedhttps://t.co/QQ5QJMsHg4 — Notes from Poland 🇵🇱 (@notesfrompoland) May 1, 2024 The FT detailed how the then head of OTS, a Lebanese-born Polish citizen of Palestinian descent, who can be named only as Samer A. under Polish privacy law, had sought in 2023 to commission the import of Venezuelan oil through intermediaries, who were given a $230 million advance without any security or guarantees. Although the United States, under then-President Joe Biden, had temporarily suspended sanctions on Venezuelan oil, allowing companies such as Orlen to buy it, Venezuela’s state oil company, PDVSA, remained largely cut off from the global financial system. The FT detailed how the intermediaries therefore sought to use cryptocurrency to facilitate the deal. However, although oil tankers leased by Orlen to collect the oil sat waiting (accruing further large costs), the promised oil was not delivered, and Orlen’s advance payments were lost. The issue is now the subject of a criminal investigation in Poland and an ongoing arbitration case with the intermediary in Dubai, Hannon International. Speaking ahead of a meeting of his cabinet on Tuesday, Tusk said that the FT story is a “disgrace in front of the entire world”. He called the Venezuelan oil incident “the biggest scandal, or one of the biggest scandals, in our country’s history”. Turning his aim on the opposition, he said that the case includes “everything that has recently been associated with PiS”, including “dirty deals” and cryptocurrencies. That was a reference to an ongoing investigation into alleged links between a collapsed crypto firm, Zondacrypto, and figures associated with the opposition. Tusk also noted that opposition-aligned President Karol Nawrocki has recently blocked government bills intended to better regulate crypto markets and to levy a windfall tax on fuel firms. “We may be dealing with a network of dirty and highly dangerous dealings,” said the prime minister. 💬 Premier @donaldtusk: Cała Polska dzisiaj to komentuje. Wstyd na cały świat. Financial Times pisze o jednym z największych skandali w historii naszego kraju i cały świat dzisiaj o tym czyta. pic.twitter.com/Ej17Csi4DL — Kancelaria Premiera (@PremierRP) September 15, 2026 Later on Tuesday, the regional prosecutor’s office in Warsaw also responded to the FT article by issuing a statement providing an update on the investigation into the Venezuelan oil deal. They noted that the Polish authorities are continuing to seek the extradition of Samer A. from the United Arab Emirates, which last year rejected a request from Poland for him to be extradited. The prosecutors also reported today that, last month, they issued indictments against three former senior Orlen and OTS executives for failing to fulfil their duties to oversee the companies’ assets, resulting in losses of $378 million. Prosecutors have charged the former head of the charitable foundation of Polish state energy giant Orlen for allowing its funds to be used to support a political campaign of the former ruling PiS party in violation of the foundation's statute https://t.co/w1Xtmivn0I — Notes from Poland 🇵🇱 (@notesfrompoland) March 6, 2026 Obajtek himself responded to the FT’s story, writing on social media that the newspaper “describes an important part of the OTS case”. He then suggested that the new management of OTS had terminated the Venezuelan oil contract too quickly, saying that the oil could in fact have been delivered. “I hope this matter will be fully clarified, including before a Polish court!” wrote Obajtek. In a further post, he suggested that Orlen and the authorities are “trying to cover up current issues again, such as the most expensive fuel in history”. In response, Orlen’s press office wrote under one of Obajtek’s posts that they would “help [him] with English”. “The article is about how your team transferred hundreds of millions of dollars to a company owned by a 25-year-old from Dubai. He converted them into cryptocurrencies, which he copied onto USB drives. And then he handed them out in restaurants to people posing as oil traders…In this story, only Orlen’s money, which they lost, was real.” Panie Pośle, pomożemy z angielskim. Artykuł jest o tym, jak pana ekipa przelała setki milionów dolarów do firmy 25-latka z Dubaju. On zamienił je na kryptowaluty, które zgrał na pendrivy. A później rozdawał w restauracjach ludziom, podającym się za handlarzy ropą. To jak „kupić”… — Biuro Prasowe ORLEN (@b_prasoweORLEN) September 15, 2026 Obajtek rose rapidly under the former PiS government, which ruled Poland from 2015 to 2023. He went from being the mayor of Pcim, a rural commune of 11,000 people in southern Poland, to the CEO of Orlen, Poland’s biggest company, in the space of three years. Under Obajtek’s leadership, Orlen expanded rapidly, swallowing up other state energy firms and expanding into new areas of activity. By 2023, it was ranked among Europe’s 50 biggest companies. However, Obajtek was also accused of using the company’s considerable resources to support PiS politically, including through Orlen’s purchases of hundreds of local media outlets – many of whose editors were replaced with PiS-friendly figures – and lowering fuel prices ahead of the 2023 elections. Last year, at Poland’s request, the European Parliament stripped Obajtek of legal immunity to face charges for allegedly using Orlen’s funds to serve his own private interests. Polish prosecutors are also pursuing him for allegedly violating Poland’s press law and falsely reporting his income in a tax return. World.title: “Don’t be a creep”: Polish ice cream company launches campaign against sexual harassment of staff
World.content: Keep our news free from ads and paywalls by making a donation to support our work! Notes from Poland is run by a small editorial team and is published by an independent, non-profit foundation that is funded through donations from our readers. We cannot do what we do without your support. A Polish ice cream chain has launched a campaign to stamp out sexual harassment of staff by customers, including empowering employees to refuse to serve such clients. The campaign is based around the fact that the Polish word for ice cream, “lody”, also has an informal vulgar meaning, referring to oral sex. The company, Good Lood, which runs 37 outlets, says that its female staff regularly suffer lewd comments from male customers incorporating this double entendre. In response, in late August it launched a campaign titled “Nie bądź oblechem”, meaning “Don’t be a creep”, with information displayed prominently at its ice cream stands and on its social media platforms. The firm said it condemned “crude remarks, inappropriate jokes and verbal harassment directed at service workers” and promised to support its staff in dealing with them. “Everyone deserves respect, without exception!” Good Lood advised employees to respond to inappropriate comments with a short, firm retort such as “Great, that’s the 20th time I’ve heard that” or “Perhaps you could repeat that more loudly, so the rest of the queue can hear?” It also called on other customers to react if they witnessed such behaviour. In a follow-up social media post last week, the company confirmed that staff had its backing if they decided not to serve a customer. “If someone is a creep and makes inappropriate comments and verbally harasses them, our team have the right to refuse them service.” That post alone has so far garnered more than 50,000 likes or other positive responses on Facebook. Good Lood says that its messages posted as part of the campaign have already received over 10 million organic views on social media. Comments on the company’s posts show overwhelming support, with many commenters sharing their own experiences. “At last someone has spoken out about this!” wrote one, who said she worked in an ice cream parlour as a teenager. “I remember how outraged I felt when I heard comments like that from men who could have been my fathers, or even my grandfathers. I wonder what would happen if someone spoke to their daughters or granddaughters like that.” Good Lood says it want to start a broader conversation on the “global issue” of harassment and disrespect towards front-line staff in retail and hospitality. “Working in service or hospitality does not mean consenting to disrespect. The safety and wellbeing of our team will always come before profit. We are not afraid to lose a customer who cannot show basic human respect,” the company said in a press release. Founded 10 years ago in Kraków, Good Lood now has 37 outlets there as well as in the Warsaw area. It also sells its products throughout Poland at Biedronka, the country’s largest supermarket chain. A moose wandered onto the tracks at Warsaw Central Station on Sunday evening, disrupting rail services in the Polish capital for more than 80 minutes before it was safely removed. The animal first appeared on a platform before moving onto the tracks, forcing Polish Railway Lines (PLK), the company responsible for Poland’s rail infrastructure, to suspend, cancel and divert several train services. View this post on Instagram A post shared by TVP3 Warszawa (@tvp3warszawa) Videos and photographs shared online showed the moose lying on the tracks and running along the railway line at Warsaw Central, the capital’s busiest station, which is mainly underground and therefore not easy for such a large animal to access. Police do not know how the moose ended up at the station, reports broadcaster TVN24. Officers were first alerted at 7:10 pm on Sunday and cordoned off the platform where the animal was located. When emergency services arrived, the moose was tranquilised. It was then placed on a large sheet and carried out of the station by police officers and emergency workers before being loaded onto a specialist vehicle to be returned to a forested area. PLK, which named the moose Emil, later confirmed that the animal had been safely removed and that normal train services were being restored. The company added that the disruptions lasted just over 80 minutes, using a pun combining the Polish words for moose (łoś) and 80 (osiemdziesiąt) to produce the word “łosiemdziesiąt”. ❗Aktualizacja❗Zwierze zostało bezpiecznie zabrane z torów. Przywracana jest rozkładowa organizacja ruchu pociągów. Utrudnienia trwały przeszło łosiemdziesiąt minut. https://t.co/Xui2B6SxyU — PLK SA (@PKP_PLK_SA) September 13, 2026 The Eurasian moose (also known as the Eurasian elk) has long been native to Poland, but by the mid-20th century hunting and habitat loss had brought the species close to extinction in the country. Its population subsequently recovered, reaching an estimated 6,000 animals by the 1980s and around 30,000 by 2019, helped by a moratorium on moose hunting introduced in 2001. Several hundred live in the Kampinos national park on the northwestern outskirts of Warsaw. They are therefore relatively frequent visitors to the capital, according to the Interia news website, although venturing onto train lines in the centre is unusual. The growth in the moose population, combined with urban expansion and changes to its habitat, has led to other high-profile encounters in areas inhabited by humans. In 2022, a moose was spotted on the roof of a shopping centre in the northern Polish city of Elbląg. A moose was this morning spotted on the roof of a shopping centre in Poland. World.title: Two New Squares and a Tower Planned Around Holešovice Station
World.content:
The area around Prague’s Nádraží Holešovice station is set for a major redevelopment after the international architectural competition for the site was won by Czech studio Chybík + Krištof.

The winning proposal envisions turning the current transport hub and surrounding brownfield into a new urban district, with two public squares, improved connections between public transport services and a new high-rise building designed to become a landmark.



The redevelopment covers roughly eight hectares around the station. Its aim is not only to add new buildings, but also to reorganise one of Prague’s important transport nodes and connect it more closely with the surrounding neighbourhood.

The competition jury selected the proposal by Chybík + Krištof as the winning design.

From transport hub to urban district

Nádraží Holešovice is currently one of Prague’s major transport interchanges, but much of the surrounding area has traditionally been used primarily for transport and other infrastructure.

The redevelopment is intended to change that. Alongside new construction, the project places emphasis on making transfers between different modes of public transport easier and fully accessible.

The project forms part of the wider Nové Holešovice development, which brings together the Prague Public Transit Company and private investors.

CPI Property, EP Real Estate, Penta Real Estate and AKIPIA are among the companies involved. The City of Prague and Prague 7 municipal district are also participating in the project.

World.title: ČokoFest to Bring Three Days of Chocolate to Galerie Harfa
World.content:
Chocolate lovers will have plenty to discover in Prague this October as ČokoFest 2026 returns to Galerie Harfa for three days of tastings, workshops, competitions and sweet treats.

The festival will take place from October 16 to 18, 2026, at the shopping center in Prague 9. Admission is free.



Now in its 14th year, ČokoFest brings together Czech and international producers, including established chocolatiers and smaller makers.

Visitors will be able to sample and buy a wide selection of chocolates and confectionery, including handmade and bean-to-bar products, pralines, cakes, cookies and macarons.

The festival will also feature a range of less conventional chocolate and sweet specialties. Among the offerings will be a chocolate fountain, chocolate kebabs, chocolate-covered fruit, as well as chocolate-infused wine and beer. Other products on sale will include jams, liqueurs, syrups, dried fruits, honey products, coffee and tea.

Exhibitors from several European countries will join Czech producers, giving visitors the opportunity to discover different chocolate styles and specialties while shopping at international sales stalls.

ČokoFest will also feature a program of activities for both adults and children. Visitors can take part in tastings, competitions and creative workshops, while children can enjoy a dedicated zone and entertainment from performers dressed as popular children’s characters.

Cooking demonstrations will be another part of the program, with chefs from local restaurants sharing their experience and showing visitors how to prepare various sweet treats. Some workshops will also focus on chocolate-making techniques that can be tried at home.

The festival is designed as a family-friendly event, with activities taking place throughout the three days. In addition to tasting and shopping, visitors can watch pastry chefs at work, take part in competitions and learn more about the production and preparation of chocolate and other confectionery.

Opening hours:

Friday, October 16: 2:00–6:00 p.m.

Saturday, October 17: 10:00 a.m.–6:30 p.m.

Sunday, October 18: 10:00 a.m.–5:00 p.m.

World.title: Poznej Vltavu Festival Returns to Prague on September 28
World.content:
The second edition of the Poznej Vltavu (Get to Know the Vltava) festival will take place across Prague on September 28, 2026.

For one day, the banks of the Vltava will host a programme exploring the river from a variety of perspectives.

The festival will feature workshops, exhibitions, sports activities, boat trips, and tours of places that are not normally open to the public.



Prague’s riverfront embankments and other locations along the Vltava will offer activities for children, adults, and seniors.

The festival aims to highlight the Vltava as a natural part of Prague’s urban environment and an important ecological feature, while giving visitors the opportunity to spend a day exploring the river and its surroundings.

Experts from a range of fields will discuss the Vltava in its broader context and offer insights into lesser-known aspects of the river.

This year’s programme will involve organisations including the Prague Institute of Planning and Development, Prague City Tourism, the Prague City Gallery, the Vltava River Authority, Prague Waterworks and Sewerage Company, the Prague Water Management Company, ROPID, Prague City Forests, the Nature Conservation Agency of the Czech Republic, and many others.

The festival area will extend farther along the Vltava this year, reaching Žluté lázně and the new Dvorecký Bridge, which has quickly become a popular destination for Prague residents since opening.

Most events will be free to attend, although some activities will require advance registration due to limited capacity.

More information is available on the festival’s Facebook event.

World.title: Red Arrows to Fly Over Charles Bridge This Friday
World.content:
Prague will hear the roar of Royal Air Force jets on Friday, September 18, when the Red Arrows aerobatic team stages a flypast over the city.

Ten BAE Hawk T1 aircraft from the British RAF team are scheduled to pass over the Charles Bridge at around 2:00 PM. The jets will leave smoke trails in the colours of the Czech flag during the display.



The formation is expected to approach Prague from the north before reaching the area around Václav Havel Airport. The aircraft will then form an arrow-shaped formation and fly around the western and southern parts of the capital before turning north along the Vltava.

The jets are expected to fly at an altitude of roughly 300 metres above the ground. The engines will be clearly audible across parts of the city, although the flypast itself will last only a short time.

After passing through central Prague, the formation will turn northeast and continue toward Ostrava. The city is hosting NATO Days, one of the Czech Republic’s largest military and security events, this weekend.

The timetable and route could still change because of weather or other air traffic in the Prague area. A similar Red Arrows flypast was held in Prague last September, but poor weather delayed the aircraft by more than an hour.

The flypast is being held in connection with Czech Air Force Day, which is observed on September 15.

The Red Arrows are the official aerobatic display team of the Royal Air Force and regularly perform at air shows and military events in Britain and abroad.

World.title: Groovy Market Fest Returns to Riegrovy Sady on October 3
World.content:
Prague’s Groovy Market Fest will return to Riegrovy Sady on Saturday, October 3, bringing together food, independent brands, design and live music for its third edition.

The one-day event will take place at Energy Pub from noon until 10 p.m.

Following two editions held during the summer, the organizers are extending the concept into the autumn, with visitors able to browse local products, eat street food and listen to live music and DJs throughout the day.



The market is organised around three main areas. The Food Garden will focus on gastronomy and street food from local businesses, while Palm Street will feature bakeries, artisanal products and other local goods. The Design Zone will bring together fashion, design and products from independent Czech brands.

Live performances and DJ sets will run from the afternoon into the evening, providing the musical programme alongside the market stalls.

Marek Novák, founder of Groovy Market Fest, said the first two editions helped the team establish the format and identify what visitors respond to.

“After two editions, we know exactly what works at Groovy Market Fest: high-quality local brands, good food, and an atmosphere that keeps people coming back,” Novák said. “This third edition is an opportunity for us to show that Groovy isn’t just a summer event, but a festival that holds a firm place in Prague all year round.”

Visitors can buy tickets for either of the two five-hour sessions. The first runs from 12 p.m. to 5 p.m., followed by a second session from 5:30 p.m. to 10 p.m.

A ticket for one session costs 100 CZK, while an all-day ticket covering both sessions is available for 190 CZK. Tickets are sold through GoOut.

View this post on Instagram A post shared by Groovy Market Fest (@groovymarketfest)

From Barcelona street food to a Prague market

Groovy Market Fest was founded by Marek Novák and Veronika Kracíková, a couple with experience in Prague’s food scene and Barcelona’s street-food sector.

One of their main inspirations was Barcelona’s Palo Alto Market, an urban market known for combining food, design, music and independent creative businesses.

World.title: Prague Run Day to Bring Six Races to Riegrovy Sady on September 19
World.content:
On September 19, runners of all levels can take part in a new running event combining track and park races in one of Prague’s best-known green spaces.

There are six different races to choose from, so whether you’re looking for a serious challenge or just want to get out and run, there’s an option for you.



Six races to choose from

The programme includes six races, ranging from a short family run to a one-hour challenge.

The day will begin with the 800m Family Run, designed for young runners and their accompanying adults. There will also be an 800m race on the athletic track, offering participants the opportunity to compete over a short distance in a traditional track setting.

For those looking for a longer challenge, the 1 Mile race will take place on the athletic oval. The organisers describe it as a special opportunity to race over the classic distance, with participation limited to a maximum of 30 runners.

The 5km Solo Run will offer a more familiar challenge for runners of different experience levels. It is followed by the 4x3km Relay, a team race in which four runners each complete two 1.5km laps.

The final event of the day will be the Golden Hour Race, a one-hour running challenge taking place during the golden hour.

The event will be based at the Sokol Vinohrady athletic oval, which will serve as the main hub for the day.

Find all race distances, times and registration details at praguerunday.cz

World.title: Prague Is Turning a Historic Factory Chimney Into an Observation Deck
World.content:
A glass elevator will carry visitors through the preserved chimney of a former distillery before emerging above its rim to reveal views of the city.

Inside the developing Lihovar district in Smíchov, a historic factory chimney is being transformed into a viewing platform, with visitors set to travel through the structure in a panoramic glass elevator.



The chimney, which stands approximately 50 meters tall, is part of the former Zlíchov distillery. Rather than demolishing the industrial landmark, developers have incorporated it into the redevelopment of the site.

The project is being developed by Trigema, which is building the new Lihovar district on the former distillery grounds.

The elevator itself is one of the project’s most unusual features. Once it reaches the top of the chimney, the cabin will lift a special cap weighing approximately 500 kilograms, allowing it to rise above the chimney’s opening.

The glass cabin will then serve as an observation deck, offering a 360-degree view of Prague.

From industrial site to new Prague district

The Lihovar development is being built on the site of the former Zlíchov distillery in Prague 5. The redevelopment includes new buildings alongside the preservation of selected elements of the original industrial complex.

The factory chimney is among the structures being retained. Another is the historic former brewhouse, which is planned for cultural use.

The opening date for the observation deck has not been announced.

World.title: Riegrovy Sady to Host Goodbye Summer Party With Three Live Acts
World.content:
Summer may be drawing to a close, but the music season at Riegrovy Sady is not over yet.

On Thursday, 17 September, Energy Pub will host the Goodbye Summer Party, organised by Ploom in cooperation with Energy Pub.



The evening will feature a DJ set by Forgen, a performance by Jirka Drtil and a live concert by Renne Dang, following his sold-out show at Forum Karlín.

Tickets cost CZK 100 and the event is open exclusively to guests aged 18 and over.

The last long days and warm evenings of summer will get a musical send-off at Riegrovy Sady. The Goodbye Summer Party is designed for everyone who is not quite ready to say a final goodbye to summer and wants to enjoy one of the last outdoor evenings of the season.

The evening will kick off with a set by DJ Forgen, followed by a performance by musician Jirka Drtil. The main highlight of the evening will be a concert by Renne Dang, Ploom brand ambassador, whose current music blends elements of rap, pop and pop-punk.

His distinctive personal lyrics and energetic guitar-driven sound have already taken him to some of the country’s biggest stages. His recent achievements include a sold-out concert at Forum Karlín.

The Last Party of the Summer

Music will not be the only reason to head to Riegrovy Sady in September. The evening will also feature a dedicated Ploom zone, where adult guests can take a break during the programme and enjoy the atmosphere of one last summer party.

Every ticket holder will also receive a complimentary welcome drink. A food pop-up by Pavel Berky will be part of the event as well.

When: Thursday, 17 September 2026, doors open at 6:00 PM

Where: Energy Pub, Riegrovy Sady 28, Prague 2

Line-up: DJ Forgen, Jirka Drtil, Renne Dang

Tickets: CZK 100, including a welcome drink

Entry: 18+ only

Capacity: Limited

World.title: Rugby meets the boardroom: Top executives invited to unique leadership experience in Budapest
World.content:
Confindustria Ungheria, the British Chamber of Commerce Hungary (BCCH) and the French Chamber of Commerce and Industry in Hungary (CCI France Hongrie) are pleased to announce the “Executive Rugby Leadership Experience”, a joint initiative bringing the leadership principles of professional rugby to the business community in Hungary.

The event will take place on 24 September 2026 at the Novotel City & Budapest Congress Centre, and will host senior executives, CEOs and CFOs for an immersive leadership development programme built around the values and methodology of team sport. This is not a sports event: it is a structured learning experience exploring how the discipline, trust and resilience developed on the rugby field translate directly into business leadership.

Participants will be welcomed by the top management of Benetton Rugby, one of the most decorated clubs in Italian rugby, founded in 1932 in Treviso and competing in the United Rugby Championship, Europe’s premier cross-border league. The club’s delegation will include Antonio Pavanello, President and former captain of the Italian national team, Fabio Rigoletto, Marketing Manager, and coaches and former national team players Tommaso Benvenuti, Tommaso Iannone, Marco Lazzaroni and Ezio Galon.

Never miss a headline: join Daily News Hungary’s official Telegram channel!

The programme will open with registration and a networking lunch, followed by three leadership sessions dedicated respectively to leading from the front, supporting the team before the individual, and communicating clearly and effectively under pressure. Participants will then take part in an executive challenge, working in mixed teams on simple rugby-inspired activities requiring no prior relevant experience. The day will continue with a panel discussion moving “from the pitch to the boardroom”, a closing group reflection and photo, and will conclude with an executive networking dinner shared with the Benetton Rugby delegation.

Participation is limited to 50 executives, with a fee of 250 euro plus VAT. The event is supported by the Budapest Congress Centre as main sponsor, and by Flame Spray, Ilinox Hungary Kft and UniCredit Bank as supporting sponsors.

For further information and registration, interested companies may contact Confindustria Ungheria.

World.title: Girl taken to hospital with serious limb injury after Budapest bus runs over her leg
World.content:
A young girl has been taken to hospital with a serious limb injury after she was hit by a 144 bus while cycling in Budapest’s 14th district on Wednesday afternoon. Police are investigating the circumstances of the accident.

Girl injured in collision with turning bus

The accident happened at around 4 PM on Wednesday at the junction of Vezér Street and Fogarasi Road in Zugló, the Budapest Transport Company (BKV) told Telex. According to BKV, a 144 bus travelling towards Rákosszentmihály hit a child who was riding a bicycle. The girl was subsequently taken to hospital by ambulance.

The National Ambulance Service told Telex that it had received an emergency call about the accident and that its crews transported a child from the scene to hospital with a serious limb injury. The girl was in a stable condition at the time.

Police are investigating the circumstances of the accident, and BKV said it would provide further information once the investigation has been completed. Traffic changes were in place in the area until 5 PM on Wednesday because of the accident.

Have you heard? Police officers revived a man after he crashed while fleeing a traffic stop in Hungary

Reports say bus ran over girl’s leg

According to earlier reports by Telex and Ma.hu, the girl had been cycling with her mother and brother and was crossing Fogarasi Road when the collision occurred.

The reports said the mother crossed in front of the bus, but the girl, who was following her, collided with the side of the vehicle and fell to the ground. The bus’s rear wheel then reportedly ran over one of the girl’s legs.

Telex reported that the family had been cycling along Vezér Street from the direction of Füredi Road and intended to continue towards Mogyoródi Road. Although much of Vezér Street has a cycle path, it merges into the bus lane shortly before the junction.

According to information obtained by Telex, the mother crossed first when the traffic light was green, followed by her daughter and then her son. The 144 bus was travelling in the same direction but turned right onto Fogarasi Road. The mother passed in front of the bus, while the girl behind her was hit.

Junction has seen previous serious accidents

The junction of Vezér Street and Fogarasi Road has previously been the scene of serious traffic accidents. In 2012, a 79-year-old woman was hit by a 144 bus at the crossing. Another person was hit by the same bus at the junction in 2013, according to reports cited by Telex. In 2025, a 231 bus reportedly fatally struck a 30-year-old man at the same junction while turning.

The latest accident is being investigated by the Budapest Police Headquarters.

Featured image: illustration, BKK

World.title: Budapest to get a huge new riverside park with 36,000 sqm of green space! – photos
World.content:
A new 36,000-square-metre public park is planned along the Pest side of the Danube in Budapest’s popular 13th District, with residents now being asked what they would like to see there.

New park planned between Népfürdő Street and the Danube

A large new public park is set to transform a 3.6-hectare area of the Danube waterfront in Budapest’s 13th District. The development will be located in the Vizafogó area, stretching from south of the E.ON sports centre to Dráva Street, between Népfürdő Street and the river.

The district municipality is developing the park as its own investment, with the area set to become a major new recreational and green space for local residents, Építészfórum wrote based on the district’s statement. At 36,000 square metres, the park will be almost one and a half times the size of the 26,000-square-metre Millenáris Széllkapu Park on the Buda side of the city.

The development area of the new riverside park in Budapest. Photo: Facebook/XIII. kerület – Budapest

The development area consists of nine separate plots. These include three building plots owned by the district municipality, four plots already designated as public green spaces, a road owned by the Municipality of Budapest, and a roughly 14,000-square-metre area currently owned by E.ON.

Under a letter of intent, the E.ON-owned area is expected to come under the ownership and management of the district municipality.

Residents can help shape the park

The district has now launched the first round of public consultation, asking residents what facilities and functions they would like to see in the new park. The consultation began on 15 September. Based on the suggestions received, experts will prepare a concept plan for the area, which will then be submitted to residents for another round of feedback.

The municipality says the two-stage process is intended to ensure that the final development reflects local needs and includes features that have broad public support. The main objective is to create a substantial, connected green area by planting a large number of new trees and other vegetation.

The park is expected to be partially opened to the public by the end of 2028 or early 2029.

Part of a green development strategy

The project forms part of the 13th District’s longer-term urban development and greening strategy, including its Long-Term Development Concept, Integrated Urban Development Strategy and AngyalZöld 4.0 development strategy.

The district has already converted building plots into public parks and playgrounds at eight locations in recent years.

These projects include Vizafogó Park, which opened in 2022 and received the Budapest Architectural Award; Thurzó Park, opened in 2023 and later recognised with a Landscape Architecture Award; and Rokolya Park, which opened in 2025. A new playground on Szent László Street is also currently under construction.

World.title: Police officers revive man after he crashes while fleeing traffic stop in Hungary
World.content:
Police officers revived a man in Nagydorog, southern Hungary, after he failed to stop when signalled to do so and crashed while attempting to flee, the Tolna County Police Headquarters said on the police website on Wednesday.

According to the report, officers in Nagydorog spotted the driver during a routine check on Tuesday afternoon. He was not wearing a seat belt. When they attempted to stop him, the driver suddenly accelerated and drove off towards Pusztahencse.

The 36-year-old man was driving at high speed and violating traffic regulations, putting several other road users at risk. He narrowly avoided hitting a cyclist. At one bend, he lost control of the vehicle, which skidded off the road and eventually came to a stop on a grassy area.

The driver and his passenger were injured, so the officers called an ambulance. Before the ambulance arrived, however, the man suddenly collapsed, lost consciousness and stopped breathing.

The officers immediately began CPR

The officers immediately began resuscitation. Thanks to chest compressions, the man began breathing again within a short time.

When the injured man’s condition deteriorated, two police officers from Paks, who had arrived at the scene in the meantime, continued the life-saving intervention until the ambulance arrived. The man was taken to hospital by air ambulance in a stable condition and, according to police, his condition has since improved.

It later emerged that the driver was apparently under the influence of alcohol, had never held a driving licence, was not wearing a seat belt, and the vehicle’s registration had expired several months earlier.

The Paks Police Department has launched proceedings against the man over the traffic offences and criminal acts committed while he was fleeing, police said.

World.title: Fidesz: Von der Leyen has publicly confirmed the “Brussels-Tisza pact”
World.content:
Opposition Fidesz on Wednesday branded European Commission President Ursula von der Leyen’s annual State of the Union address as a public endorsement of what it called the “Brussels-Tisza pact”.

In a statement, Bertalan Havasi, the party’s communications director, said von der Leyen had “sent greetings from the Brussels centre to the Hungarian colony” and “publicly confirmed the Brussels-Tisza pact”.

He insisted that the EC president had spoken of Brussels using “financial blackmail” to help bring the Tisza government to power and keep it there, in exchange for the government “settling scores with patriotic politicians who oppose Brussels” and handing over the Hungarian economy “lock, stock, and barrel to foreign companies”.

Never miss a headline: join Daily News Hungary’s official Telegram channel!

In her address to the European Parliament in Strasbourg, von der Leyen said that on 12 April, the Hungarian people had taken their future into their own hands, choosing democracy and Europe, and returning Hungary to the heart of the European Union.

“The fight against corruption and state capture is speeding up. There is real progress on fundamental rights. On academic freedom. And now, billions of euros of investment in Hungary have been unlocked,” the EC president said.

World.title: Eight Slovak-Hungarian students left behind in France after school trip
World.content:
An English school trip ended in controversy for eight students from a Hungarian-language secondary school in Šahy, southern Slovakia, after they were left in France with a teacher while the rest of the group travelled home.

The six girls and two boys, aged between 15 and 17, were left behind in the town of Forbach, near the French-German border, after organisers accused some students of inappropriate behaviour and disturbing the peace at their accommodation. The incident was reported by Slovak media outlets Új Szó and tnlive.sk.

Students left behind in France after disturbance

The group had travelled to England on a school trip organised by the Hungarian-language secondary school in Šahy. On the final night of the trip, while the group was staying in Forbach, some students allegedly repeatedly disturbed other guests.

According to the trip organiser, the students were repeatedly banging on doors along the hotel corridor and disturbing other guests. Several guests reportedly opened their doors and threatened to call the police.

The organiser said the students had also laughed off a warning that their behaviour grade could be downgraded. As a result, the organiser decided that the eight students would not continue travelling with the rest of the group. A teacher stayed behind in France with them.

According to the organiser, parents had previously signed an agreement stating that a student could be excluded from the trip in the event of a serious breach of discipline, with the parents responsible for the cost of getting the student home.

Never miss a headline: join Daily News Hungary’s official Telegram channel!

Parents say the teenagers were shocked

The parents dispute the decision and say the students were effectively abandoned in France. Klaudia Uhor, the mother of one of the students, told tnlive.sk that the teenagers initially believed the bus was simply joking when it left without them.

After about half an hour, however, they realised that the group was not coming back for them, she said.

The parents were then forced to arrange and pay for their children’s journey home. The students first travelled to Frankfurt and then to Vienna, where a separate bus hired by their parents picked them up and took them back to Slovakia.

Uhor said the situation was particularly concerning because the students’ travel insurance was due to expire at midnight.

“We had to act quickly because anything could have happened to them,” she said, according to tnlive.sk.

The parents have filed a criminal complaint and are also working with lawyers over the incident.

Organiser says the rules were agreed in advance

The trip organiser maintains that the decision was made in accordance with the rules agreed with the parents before the trip. She also claimed that two of the eight students had not personally broken the rules but remained in France in solidarity with the other six.

“There was no alcohol, no drugs, nothing like that,” Richard Segeč, the father of one of the students, told tnlive.sk.

The organiser said she also had video recordings of the incidents.

Meanwhile, lawyer Miroslav Chromý, representing the parents, said it was too early to determine whether the incident constituted a criminal offence or another breach of duty. “The clarification of the facts and their legal assessment are fully in the hands of the relevant authorities dealing with the case,” he said.

The school’s management is also dealing with the incident. The exact circumstances and legal consequences of the decision have yet to be established.

World.title: Hungary tightens syphilis screening during pregnancy as congenital cases rise
World.content:
An increasing number of babies are being born with congenital syphilis in Hungary, prompting the National Public Health and Pharmacy Centre (NNGYK) to introduce new, nationwide procedures. The number of cases has risen significantly since 2021: 91 cases were recorded in 2025, while 100 were reported in the first eight months of 2026 alone.

New screening during the second half of pregnancy

According to the NNGYK, a coordinated response is needed because congenital syphilis can largely be prevented if the infection is detected and treated in time. One of the key changes under the new methodological guidance is that, from 1 September, pregnant women must undergo a second syphilis screening between the 24th and 28th weeks of pregnancy, in addition to the test carried out during the first trimester.

The requirement also applies to pregnancies where antenatal care began before 1 September. If the pregnancy has already progressed beyond the 24–28-week period, the screening must be carried out at the next antenatal care appointment. Women who have not received antenatal care, as well as those considered to be at high risk of syphilis infection, must undergo a rapid syphilis test when they give birth.

Never miss a headline: join Daily News Hungary’s Telegram channel!

Strict deadlines for treatment

The NNGYK aims to ensure that no positive screening result is left without appropriate follow-up. In confirmed cases of syphilis, specific penicillin treatment must be started within 72 hours of the diagnosis at the latest.

Treating sexual partners is also considered essential to prevent transmission and reinfection. Identification and notification of partners must begin immediately, and no later than 48 hours after a confirmed infection. If a test is positive, immediate steps must also be taken to ensure appropriate care for both the mother and the newborn.

Hungary more than twice the WHO target

The World Health Organisation (WHO) has set a target of no more than 50 cases of congenital syphilis per 100,000 live births. Based on data recorded in Hungary in 2025, the rate was 126 cases per 100,000 live births. The seriousness of the situation is also reflected in the reported deaths: 26 children died from the infection in Hungary in 2025, while a further 23 deaths had been recorded by August 2026.

The new nationwide procedure standardises the steps to be taken from screening and treatment through to the management of sexual partners and the follow-up care of newborns. The NNGYK stresses that congenital syphilis is largely preventable, but this requires the infection to be detected and treated in time.
