World.title: Special education gains popularity, but specialists remain scarce
World.content:
The special education field is attracting more university applicants, but schools across Estonia are still struggling to find the support specialists their students need.

Tallinn University (TLÜ) admits 55 students to its bachelor's program and 42 to its master's program in special education each year, and Tiiu Tammemäe, associate professor of inclusive and special education, said demand is steadily rising.

She said applications for full-time studies outnumbered available enrollment nearly nine times over, while session-based bachelor's studies drew more than 15 applications per spot, making special education one of the most competitive majors in the country.

The university trains as many special education specialists as funding from the Ministry of Education and Research allows.

"At the moment, we aren't looking to increase the size of these study groups either, although there may be public pressure to train more [specialists]," Tammemäe acknowledged.

Still hiring

Yet schools continue to struggle with staffing. Tallinn's Laagna Kindergarten-Basic School, which serves students with special educational needs (SENs), is required to have two speech therapists and two special education teachers, as well as a social pedagogue and school psychologist, said principal Andres Anton.

"There isn't the demand you'd expect among speech therapists, because the University of Tartu (TÜ) simply trains relatively few of them," he said.

His school is currently hiring a special education teacher, speech therapist and school psychologist, and Anton said they have been searching for the support specialists for at least a year already.

Visuals used in speech therapy. Source: ERR

"It's not uncommon for someone to apply to several places and then, as always, they go with the highest bidder," he said, adding that candidates will sometimes withdraw at the last minute as a result, sparking competition among schools over pay.

Tammemäe said demand is already reaching university students during their studies, with institutions requesting she share job openings, recruiting during internships and even getting hired before they graduate.

Unqualified staff hired under different roles

A master's degree is required to qualify as a special education teacher or pursue higher-level qualifications as a social pedagogue, speech therapist or school psychologist. Bachelor's graduates, meanwhile, can work as kindergarten teachers or school teaching assistants.

The Education Ministry estimates there are about 2,200 support specialists working in schools. However, 7–12 percent of positions, depending on the specialty, are filled by people who do not meet the formal qualification requirements, said Jürgen Rakaselg, head of the ministry's Inclusive Education Department.

Facing a shortage of specialists, he noted, some schools have formally placed under- or unqualified staff in other roles.

"We know some schools have never had a school psychologist at all, despite the law requiring them to provide that service," Rakaselg admitted.

Schools are best staffed in terms of social pedagogues and special education teachers, the ministry official said. School psychologists and speech therapists, meanwhile, are harder to find; the latter two are currently available at just over half of the country's schools.

World.title: New county bus contracts to deliver drivers hefty pay rise
World.content:
New regional bus contracts will require drivers to be paid Estonia's average wage, increasing the amount of state funding needed to subsidize bus services.

Regional bus routes have for years operated under a sector-wide collective agreement between employers and employees that sets bus drivers' pay rates.

In 2025, the Association of Estonian Road Carriers and the Transport Workers' Union agreed that bus drivers would in future have to be paid Estonia's average wage. Contracts for regional bus routes are awarded for eight years and this year public transport centers will begin conducting the first procurements under the new terms.

"Over the next five years, all of our contracts will be renewed. Some have already been renewed, so to speak, while some are still being processed. Next year there will be two contracts and after that two contracts a year through 2031. The requirement to pay the average wage is now fully included in the new contracts," said Andrus Nilisk, executive director of the North Estonia Public Transport Center.

The calculation would be based on the previous year's average wage, or around €2,100, while bus drivers working under existing contracts that still have several years to run are being paid €1,500 this year. Their wages are increased through indexation.

"With the old contracts, wages also rise by €100 each year, so they will eventually reach roughly the same level, but under the new contracts the increase is steep," Nilisk said.

However, the wage increase would mean raising the state's annual taxpayer-funded subsidy.

"Labor costs account for about half of the price per route kilometer, so naturally this will have an impact on the subsidy. During the transition period, it will require around €1.5 million a year in additional subsidies. For the past five years, every year when the state budget has been adopted, there has not been enough funding to last through the end of the year and then additional money has been found midway through the year," said Kersten Kattai, director of the Association of Estonian Road Carriers.

The minimum salary for teachers is €1,970 this year. Estonia's median wage has been €1,750 this year. Minister of Regional Affairs Hendrik Johannes Terras would now have to seek additional funding for subsidies in order to pay bus drivers €2,100.

"I know that this agreement has been reached. It may have an impact on the bids submitted in terms of the price per kilometer. But given that relatively few of our contracts will be renewed next year, I don't expect it to have an impact on the budget," Terras said.

World.title: EBRD boosts trade financing in Iraq
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – The European Bank for Reconstruction and Development (EBRD) is bolstering trade financing in Iraq by extending a credit ceiling of up to US$ 25 million (€21.3 million) to Bank of Baghdad, one of Iraq’s main private-sector banks.

The initiative is part of the EBRD’s Trade Facilitation Program (TFP) and aims to assist the Bank of Baghdad in enhancing its import and export transactions, as well as expanding its correspondent banking relationships.

The funding will assist in closing trade financing gaps in Iraq, improve access to trade finance for micro, small, and medium-sized enterprises (MSMEs) involved in cross-border trade, and boost commercial ties with regional and worldwide markets.

The technical cooperation funded by the EBRD will include advising help, specialized training, access to the EBRD Trade Finance e-Learning Program, and seminars on essential trade finance subjects.

The European Union will fund the creation of a dedicated training curriculum for the Bank of Baghdad, focusing on core and advanced banking competencies, improving staff skills, strengthening service delivery, and promoting the continued development of Iraq’s banking sector.

The initiative will also promote financial inclusion by providing a specific training module on increasing access to financial services for underrepresented populations, particularly women.

The Bank of Baghdad is one of Iraq’s top three private banks, with total assets of $2.2 billion by the end of 2025 and 35 branches around the nation.

In 1999, the EBRD launched the TFP initiative to enhance international commerce. The program provides guarantees and short-term loans to selected participating banks, which in turn support local exporters, importers, and distributors.

World.title: Iraq, Turkey finalize draft transport infrastructure agreement
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – The Iraqi Transport Ministry announced on Friday that Iraq and Turkey have finalized an agreement regarding the development of transport infrastructure.

The agreement paves the way for official government recognition and a formal signature.

The deal was reached after a memorandum of understanding was reached by Iraqi Transport Minister Wahab al-Hassani and Turkish Transport and Infrastructure Minister Abdulkadir Uraloglu in late July.

Officials from both sides completed the document after four days of intense discussions in Baghdad.

The agreement formulates a comprehensive institutional framework to regulate cooperation in developing infrastructure projects and modernizing transportation systems.

The draft framework includes a program to implement various phases of the Development Road, a strategic project proposed by Iraq to transport goods and energy from Basra to Turkey, in accordance with the approved technical priorities, timelines, and project completion requirements.

Given the economic and developmental importance of the Development Road project to Iraq and the region, this step serves as a critical foundation for consolidating Iraqi-Turkish cooperation and organizing joint working mechanisms.

The move is part of Iraq’s efforts to upgrade the transport sector and boost investment opportunities and economic integration, supporting strategic projects and strengthening Iraq’s position as a key hub for transport, trade, and regional and international supply chains.

World.title: Where the US-China tariff row stands ahead of White House summit
World.content:
Beijing – Trade frictions between the world’s top two economies are set to take centre stage next week when US President Donald Trump hosts Chinese counterpart Xi Jinping at the White House.

Although a shaky truce was reached last October that halted the frenzied escalating tariff battle launched by Trump, a comprehensive and permanent deal has remained elusive.

Here is where things stand ahead of the summit, which is expected to take place on September 24:

How high are current levies?

Tariffs have represented a major hurdle in the China-US trade relationship since 2018, during Trump’s first term.

In April 2025, the base US tariff rate on Chinese goods reached an eye-watering 145 percent — matched by China’s reciprocal levies of 125 percent — although both sides have since significantly reduced rates.

Tolls are now imposed by both sides in a complex patchwork of sector-specific policies.

The effective tariff rate for imports from China, which balances various duties paid across all items, was 22.8 percent as of July, the highest among all major US trading partners, according to research organisation the Penn Wharton Budget Model.

Among the highest effective tariff rates for Chinese goods heading to the United States are 40.5 percent on steel and aluminium, it said.

China still maintains a 10 percent levy on all US goods, with additional rates applicable in other specific sectors, such as 15 percent on liquid natural gas.

How much is still being traded?

Trade between the world’s two largest economies has continued despite the turbulence caused by the tariffs.

Total imports and exports hit $400.8 billion in January through August this year, Chinese customs data shows, a 5.4 percent rise from the same period in 2025.

But the balance is lopsided, with Chinese exports accounting for 75 percent of that.

Beijing’s soaring trade surplus has long ruffled feathers in Washington, while a similar asymmetry with the European Union is also exacerbating tensions with Brussels.

What is being discussed?

Trump told reporters on Sunday that he would be discussing “almost everything” with Xi at the summit.

Tariffs, however, are “the main issue on the agenda”, Dan Wang, a director on Eurasia Group’s China team, told AFP. “Xi wouldn’t go if there were no deliverables on tariffs or a trade truce,” she said.

Beijing and Washington are currently in consultation about a tariff reduction framework covering $30 billion worth of products on each side, China’s commerce ministry said last week.

That goal was agreed at Xi’s last meeting with Trump in Beijing in May, during which they also agreed to establish trade and investment councils intended to manage friction.

US Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent said Tuesday that he will meet his Chinese counterpart He Lifeng this weekend for talks expected to lay the groundwork for the White House summit.

What is China’s leverage?

Beijing successfully pressured Washington to back down from its sky-high tariffs last year after imposing stringent controls on exports of rare earths, the critical minerals used for various high-tech products whose processing is dominated by China.

“China still has the upper hand” going into next week’s talks, said Wang of Eurasia Group.

The country’s supply chains are “very flexible”, and its historic boom in exports has not been significantly dented by tariffs so far, she noted.

Xi’s diplomatic clout has also been on full display recently, having met this month with several leaders including Russian President Vladimir Putin and Indian Prime Minister Narendra Modi, traveling to Bishkek, Cairo and New Delhi.

What is Trump seeking?

With global oil prices spiking following renewed fighting in the US war with Iran, the Trump administration is looking to allay concerns about the economy ahead of crucial midterm elections in November.

Securing Chinese guarantees to purchase US agricultural goods, particularly soybeans, has been a recurring objective in trade talks with Beijing.

The meeting will also give Trump the chance to project statesmanship while hosting a high-stakes diplomatic engagement at the White House — Xi’s first visit to the US capital in 11 years.

What are other potential pitfalls?

Several other fraught issues threaten to derail any sweeping agreement.

Beijing’s economic and diplomatic support for Tehran is one major sticking point, with recent reports by the Wall Street Journal claiming that Chinese entities supplied Iran with satellite imagery of a military base housing US troops in Jordan.

Fierce technological competition is also ongoing, particularly in the closely watched artificial intelligence sector.

The US government last week accused Chinese AI labs of stealing the capabilities of US firms on an “industrial scale”.

World.title: Most stocks rise as Fed hikes and indicates drive to curb inflation
World.content:
Hong Kong – Most equities rose Thursday after the Federal Reserve hiked interest rates for the first time in three years and boss Kevin Warsh sounded a hawkish note that ramped up bets on another increase as officials fight surging inflation.

Investor sentiment was also given a lift by hopes for a pick-up in oil supplies from Saudi Arabia after the country moved to restore some capacity from a pipeline it closed at the weekend following drone attacks.

In a unanimous decision, the Fed lifted borrowing costs for the first time since 2023, defying President Donald Trump’s demand for cuts, as Warsh stressed the need to combat inflation that has been “too high” for “too long”.

“We removed a dose of accommodation so that financial and credit conditions would be more consistent with our ultimate objectives,” Warsh said after the announcement.

“Today’s action starts to show we’re serious about this, and we will deliver on the price stability objective.”

The decision was announced along with a graph showing the vast majority of Fed policymakers saw at least one more was likely necessary before the end of the year.

Traders now see an October hike as being a 50:50.

While Wall Street’s three main indexes ended Wednesday in the red, Asian traders took the 25-basis-point lift more positively, with analysts saying it shored up credibility in the central bank and provided some reassurance over officials’ determination to beat inflation.

Long-term government bond yields — which this week touched two-decade highs — fell as investors pared back their inflation expectations, which at 3.4 percent is currently well above the bank’s two percent target.

“Removing a dose of accommodation is not the language of a central bank that believes it has completed the job,” said Stephen Innes at Quintex Intel.

“It suggests policy was still providing support before Wednesday and may not yet be restrictive after it.

“The hike removed the immediate credibility question. The explanation created a new argument about how much tightening remains.”

And Christian Scherrmann at DWS added: “Overall, we believe the main motivation this time was credibility, given bond market pricing and recent developments in oil markets.”

Still, he added: “Despite his hawkish stance, Fed Chair Warsh’s optimistic outlook on the economy may be music to many ears.”

Equity markets across Asia were mostly higher in early trade.

Tokyo, Seoul, Singapore, Taipei, Wellington and Jakarta all advanced, though Hong Kong and Shanghai dipped.

However, Tai Hui, of JP Morgan Asset Management, warned: “We think the chance of U.S. policy rates returning to above five percent is still limited.

“Nonetheless, a catalyst to extend the equity bull market (lower interest rates) is looking unlikely in the foreseeable future.”

The news angered Trump, who called Warsh a “good man” who had “a hostile board”.

“They’re raising the rates to make Trump do as bad as they can possibly do… So they’re raising that only for political reasons, and that’s a raise against Trump,” he complained.

While the Middle East crisis continues to weigh heavily on sentiment and oil prices above $100 a barrel, investors took some cheer from reports that Saudi Arabia is looking to return about half the capacity of its cross-country oil pipeline within days.

The East-West conduit was shut last week after Yemen’s Iran-backed Houthis targeted it.

State-run Saudi Aramco said it was looking to get back up to full capacity in about six weeks, Bloomberg cited sources as saying.

The news sent crude prices tumbling around three percent Wednesday, and they extended the losses Thursday.

The Fed hike and Warsh’s remarks also pushed the dollar higher against its peers and held the gains in early trade.

Eyes are now on decisions by the central banks of Britain and Japan, with the latter also expected to hike as it looks to fend off a rise in inflation and a weaker yen.

World.title: US again denies Palestinian leader Abbas visa to attend UN assembly
World.content:
Washington – The United States has denied Palestinian President Mahmoud Abbas an entry visa to attend the UN General Assembly in New York next week, a source familiar with the case said Wednesday.

In a separate statement that did not mention Abbas by name, the State Department say it would deny visas to members of the Palestine Liberation Organization (PLO) and officials with the Palestinian Authority (PA), “as a consequence of their failure to reform, contrary to their commitments to the United States, and their ongoing activities that undermine the prospects for peace.”

A source familiar with the matter confirmed to AFP that the Palestinian Authority president, Abbas, was covered by the measure.

The Trump administration took the same step last year, forcing the Palestinian leader, a regular at the UN General Assembly, to address the body of global leadership by video.

In its statement Wednesday, the State Department said that the PLO and PA had “once again, failed to live up to their commitments.”

“This includes initiating and supporting actions at international organizations that undermine and contradict prior commitments,” the department also said.

Washington also accused the organizations of “taking actions to internationalize the Israeli-Palestinian Conflict including through the International Criminal Court (ICC) and International Court of Justice (ICJ), seeking to bypass negotiations through seeking unilateral recognition, and continuing to pay stipends to terrorists and to glorify acts of terrorism and terrorists in public pronouncements and school textbooks.”

The move puts the United States at odds with numerous countries, including France, that recognized a Palestinian state at the United Nations last year.

A total of 142 UN member states endorsed it following the conference on a two-state solution co-chaired by France and Saudi Arabia.

The decision comes as violence by Israeli settlers against Palestinians has escalated in recent months in the West Bank.

Israel has occupied the West Bank since 1967, and violence there has surged since the October 7, 2023 Hamas attack that triggered the war in the Gaza Strip.

According to an AFP tally based on Palestinian health ministry data, Israeli soldiers or settlers have killed at least 1,109 Palestinians in the West Bank — fighters and civilians — since October 7, 2023, when a Hamas-led attack killed more than 1,200 people.

The ensuing Israeli military campaign waged relentless strikes on Gaza that have killed more than 73,700 people, according to Gaza’s health ministry, which operates under Hamas authority and whose figures are considered reliable by the United Nations.

The international community has expressed concern over the violence, but the United States has remained largely quiet on the issue, saying only that the US government opposes any annexation of Palestinian territory.

World.title: AI looms large ahead of Xi, Trump summit
World.content:
Washington – Artificial intelligence is set to loom large when Chinese President Xi Jinping meets counterpart Donald Trump in Washington next week, but for all the urgency surrounding the technology, the rivals remain far from agreeing on anything substantial.

The United States and China are the two dominant powers in the AI race, and officials and analysts describe the technology’s future starkly, as a world shaped by one superpower’s AI or the other’s.

China, long seen as trailing the United States on frontier AI, has been closing that gap fast.

Chinese firms including DeepSeek and Moonshot AI have released open-weight models — which anyone can download, modify and run — that now rank just behind the top closed US systems from OpenAI and Anthropic, at a fraction of the cost.

Moonshot’s Kimi K3, released this summer, is seen by analysts as the clearest sign yet of that narrowing gap.

Washington has long tried to slow China’s progress with export controls on the advanced chips needed for cutting-edge AI, blocking access to top-end US semiconductors such as Nvidia’s.

The Trump administration has eased licensing rules for some chips even as it moves to restrict others, to the frustration of China hawks in Washington who want a harder line.

The AI question became more urgent after the recent Hugging Face incident, in which OpenAI models broke out of a test environment, triggering global alarm over the technology’s fast advancement — and calls for the industry to slow down or pause development.

– ‘Lose the race’ –

The AI debate in the US remains dominated by the idea that the country’s leading developers — OpenAI, Anthropic, Google and Meta — cannot afford to slow their pace of innovation, whatever the risks, for fear that China will pull ahead.

“If Congress just races in and does some sort of emergency session to try to regulate AI, we will lose the race to China, and that is a threat to every single American,” House Speaker Mike Johnson said this week.

Trump has taken a starker line, accusing AI safety advocates of bad faith and raising the specter of China dominating the field.

“There is a SICK conspiracy going on against AI and Data Centers, and the only one that is happy about it is China,” he wrote on his Truth Social platform.

Unease about AI’s danger to geopolitical standing is also alive in Beijing.

Minister of State Security Chen Yixin on Sunday described AI as “the main battleground” for global competition “and a new track for major power strategic rivalry.”

Despite the heated rhetoric, hope remains that the two global rivals can agree on something regarding the technology when the leaders meet in Washington.

But anything ambitious, like agreeing to slow development or craft global safeguards, is likely out of reach.

The US and China are stuck in “a prisoner’s dilemma at two levels,” said Aalok Mehta of the Center for Strategic and International Studies (CSIS), arguing that neither individual AI labs nor individual countries can afford to slow down unilaterally as long as they fear their rivals will not.

“What would it mean if the US were to slow its pace at a time China doesn’t?” asked Jennifer Huddleston of the Cato Institute, framing the dilemma facing US policymakers.

“What does that mean for our allies who are going to be looking to find technological solutions from someone” other than China, she added.

– ‘Close communication’ –

Others were skeptical that even modest cooperation was likely.

Jonathan Czin of the Brookings Institution said the dim prospects for cooperation reflect divisions on both sides.

“There’s not a consensus, by any means, that’s crystallized in the United States on what, if anything, to do about AI,” he said.

On the Chinese side, he said, there is “a deeply ingrained suspicion” that any dialogue on restraint is “just going to be a trap” designed to slow China down.

Any deal would likely be hammered out ahead of time by US Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent, who meets his Chinese counterpart He Lifeng this weekend to prepare the ground.

“As the number one and number two superpowers in AI by a lot, it behooves all of us to put up guardrails, to have close communication,” Bessent told reporters this month.

World.title: Trump to host Xi amid pomp, low expectations
World.content:
Washington – The US military honor guard has been rehearsing and the new White House helipad is ready. But will Xi Jinping and Donald Trump achieve lift-off at their summit next week?

Warnings of an AI apocalypse hang heavy over the Chinese president’s first talks at the White House with his US counterpart, with both countries racing for supremacy in this technology.

Trump’s Iran war casts a long shadow too, as China seeks to avoid US sanctions against countries dealing with Tehran, despite reports that Beijing supplied Tehran with intelligence for a strike on US troops.

A trade war is of even greater concern and the world’s two largest economies are still seeking to mitigate the fallout from Trump’s global tariffs. The threat of war over Taiwan looms large as well.

Behind it all is desire to manage tensions between a superpower keen to keep its place at the top and a rapidly rising rival determined to make the 21st century a Chinese one.

“I’ll be discussing almost everything with him,” Trump told reporters aboard Air Force One on Sunday, ahead of their meeting on September 24.

– ‘Don’t expect much’ –

But the two leaders are more likely to simply extend a relative truce rather than produce any concrete results, like when Xi hosted Trump in Beijing four months ago, experts said.

“I don’t expect much to come out of this,” Jonathan Czin of the Brookings Institution told AFP.

“In many ways, this is going to be a recapitulation of Trump’s visit to Beijing back in May, where the focus was really on the ostensible rapport between the two leaders.”

With fears about AI making global headlines, agreement to cooperate on regulation or a slowdown is expected to be a major topic of discussion between Trump and Xi.

But any major deals are “politically out of reach for now,” said Wang Dong, a professor at Peking University, as Beijing and Washington both fear losing out in the race for AI dominance.

Tensions over Iran will also come up. US Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent is due to meet his Chinese counterpart He Lifeng this weekend for pre-summit talks including on Iran sanctions.

Trump has, however, played down reports that Chinese entities supplied Iran with satellite imagery for an attack on a US military base in Jordan, saying Xi had “behaved reasonably well” and that “we spy on them, too.”

On trade, there is “room for progress on tariffs, agricultural purchases and selected export controls”, Yue Su of The Economist Intelligence Unit told AFP.

– ‘Spectacle’ –

Yet Trump has, as so often before, appeared more interested in the optics of his meeting with a powerful foreign leader than with the substance.

“This is less a summit and more a spectacle. This is designed for deep public consumption,” said Kurt Campbell, former US Deputy Secretary of State and now Chairman of The Asia Group.

Trump pushed for a new granite helicopter landing pad on the White House South Lawn to be open in time for Xi’s visit, which will include a grand state dinner.

Troops in flashy uniforms have been rehearsing on the White House driveway this week ahead of the welcome ceremony.

Trump’s only disappointment is that his under-construction $400 million ballroom won’t be ready — though he has said that when finished it will “top” Beijing’s Great Hall of the People, where Xi hosted him in May.

During the Beijing trip Trump showered praise on Xi, only for the Chinese leader to warn about possible “conflict” over Taiwan.

Fears of a possible Chinese invasion of the self-governing island and global semiconductor hub — which Beijing claims as its territory — remain the most sensitive topic between Washington and Beijing, said Peking University’s Wang.

One possible concrete deliverable is an announcement of further summits.

Trump and Xi are expected to meet in November at the Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation (APEC) forum in Shenzen, China. The Kremlin has suggested a three-way meeting with Russian President Vladimir Putin.

Trump is meanwhile expected to invite Xi to the G20 summit in December at his Doral resort in Miami.

World.title: Boehly and Walter sell Chelsea stake to Clearlake Capital
World.content:
London – Chelsea chairman Todd Boehly and director Mark Walter have sold their stakes in the Premier League side to majority owner Clearlake Capital, which has assumed full control, the club announced Wednesday.

American billionaires Boehly and Walter were two of the investors who partnered with Clearlake to buy Chelsea from Roman Abramovich for £2.5 billion ($3.3 billion) in May 2022.

“Chelsea Football Club today announced affiliates of Clearlake Capital Group, L.P. (‘Clearlake’) will acquire the ownership interest of Todd Boehly,” said a club statement.

“As part of the transition, Clearlake will also acquire Mark Walter’s ownership interest and therefore acquire full control of the Club,” it added.

Prior to Wednesday night’s announcement, private equity company Clearlake held 62 percent of Chelsea, with Boehly and Walter holding the remaining shares with fellow investor Hansjorg Wyss.

Wyss “will remain an important stakeholder and partner in the ownership group,” said the club statement.

No financial terms for the deal were disclosed. Boehly and Walter were reported to have valued the club at £5 billion.

The Financial Times reported that the pair were set to receive £950 million in cash, in a deal that values the club at about $5 billion including debt.

In the statement, Boehly said it had been “an honour to serve as Chairman of Chelsea Football Club.”

“I have valued my partnership with Clearlake and the wider ownership group, and the collective decisions and investment we have made to support the immediate and long-term success of the Club,” he said.

“I am confident that Chelsea is well positioned for continued success under Clearlake’s leadership.”

Chelsea finished a dismal 10th in the Premier League last season and hired Xabi Alonso as their new manager.

Boehly had reportedly been dissatisfied with the direction of Chelsea, notably regarding recruitment, managers and a potential new stadium plan.

There had been reports that Boehly and Clearlake had attempted to buy each other out of Chelsea several times over the last two years.

Boehly and Walter co-own the Los Angeles Dodgers baseball team, while Walter recently sold the Los Angeles Lakers basketball franchise for $12.5 billion.

Clearlake Capital co-founders Behdad Eghbali and Jose E. Feliciano thanked Boehly “for his time and contribution as Chairman.”

“There will be no changes to the day-to-day operations, leadership or strategy at the Club,” said the statement.

World.title: 'It can't be that Hindi will not be taught in Tamil Nadu', SC tells state during hearing on Navodaya schools
World.content:
âChennai shouldnât alienate Delhiâ: SC tells Tamil Nadu to reconsider opposition to Navodaya schools

Tamil Nadu raises language concerns

Court stresses cooperative federalism

State raises financial concerns

Supreme Court refuses to recall land direction

Join conversation View All Comments â Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful Â· TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: Supreme Court on Thursday directed the Tamil Nadu government to comply with its December 15, 2025 order to identify land in every district for establishing Jawahar Navodaya Vidyalayas, while urging the state and Centre to resolve their differences over the schools through dialogue.A bench of Justices BV Nagarathna and Augustine George Masih also questioned Tamil Nadu's opposition to the three-language policy followed by Navodaya schools and said the state should not view the establishment of the centrally funded institutions as a threat to its existing education system."You have to change your mindset, it canât be that Hindi will not be taught in the soil of Tamil Nadu," Justice Nagarathna observed during the hearing.The bench also said the people in Chennai should not alienate those in Delhi while stressing the need for cooperative federalism."We are saying in addition to all the good things youâre doing in your State, having something in addition will not bring down your standards. Coming from Delhi, will not lower the standards of Chennai. People in Chennai should not alienate Delhi and vice versa," the Court said.The court granted Tamil Nadu three more months to identify suitable land in each district and directed representatives of the state and Central governments to hold further discussions on the policy for establishing the schools.The matter has been posted for December 14.The case relates to Tamil Nadu's challenge to a Madras High Court direction to establish Navodaya Vidyalayas in every district.Navodaya schools are centrally funded, co-educational residential schools run by the Navodaya Vidyalaya Samiti under the Union Ministry of Education. Tamil Nadu has opposed their establishment, among other reasons, because the schools follow a three-language policy that includes Hindi, while the state follows a two-language policy.Senior Advocate Jaideep Gupta, appearing for Tamil Nadu, told the court that the state's objection was not to schools or the teaching of Hindi as such, but to the language policy associated with the Navodaya scheme."It is against the State policy. It supersedes Tamil. This kind of unification is not the purport of the Constitution. It is not a Central government school. It is a school run by a society. There is an adamancy that Hindi must predominate."Justice Nagarathna said the language issue could be discussed between the Centre and the state."If you want Tamil as a second language, it is a matter which can be considered," the Judge said, asking the state Secretary to speak to the corresponding Central government Secretary.Gupta said discussions had already taken place but the Centre had remained adamant about Hindi. He nevertheless agreed to another round of consultations.Tamil Nadu also argued that the judiciary could not compel a state to adopt an optional Central government policy through a mandamus.Gupta submitted that education is in the Concurrent List and that Tamil Nadu has constitutional authority to frame its own education policy. He also argued that the Navodaya scheme was not compulsory.Justice Nagarathna questioned the consequences of individual states refusing to accept Central policies."Education is in the Concurrent List. There has to be cooperative federalism. If each State says that I don't accept your policy, what will happen?" the Judge asked.The bench said Tamil Nadu could continue running its own institutions and following its own syllabus, while Navodaya schools would provide an additional educational option.The court also rejected the argument that the establishment of Navodaya schools would lower Tamil Nadu's educational standards."We are not alienating you and we are not alienating them. Some more type of schools come in your state also which will only enhance the high standard which we are aware of. This is not going to lower your standards. If Navodaya schools were going to lower the standard of education in Tamil Nadu we would have said that irrespective of what you would have said. That is not the case here. It will provide more opportunity," Justice Nagarathna told Gupta."Ultimately everybody must work together," Justice Nagarathna said.Tamil Nadu also raised financial concerns, submitting that the Centre had promised to release Rs 5,000 crore for education but had not done so.Gupta argued that the state could not take on additional financial liabilities when funds under existing schemes had allegedly not been released.Additional Solicitor General KM Nataraj, appearing for the Centre, submitted that the state's primary requirement under the scheme was to provide land, while construction and other expenses would be borne by the Central government.Nataraj said the scheme was at an early stage and construction would take several years, during which the language-related differences could be addressed through discussions.Gupta, however, said around 30 acres of land would be required in each district and that identifying land before deciding whether to accept the policy would create difficulties.The bench clarified that it was not directing the state to acquire land immediately, but only to identify suitable land in its government plan.The Supreme Court had in December 2025 directed Tamil Nadu to identify land required for establishing Navodaya Vidyalayas in every district within six weeks. The state subsequently sought recall of the order.On Thursday, the bench declined to recall the direction and instead granted the state three months to comply.In its order, the bench recorded that Tamil Nadu had cited the change in government and lack of material progress in discussions with the Centre as reasons for non-compliance."Be that as it may, we direct the petitioner to comply with our order of 15.12.2025 in so far as identification of the land necessary to establish the school in each district," the order stated.The bench also directed the Centre and Tamil Nadu to continue discussions on the policy while the state works on identifying the land.Advocates G Priyadarshini and Rahul Shyam Bhandari, appearing for Kumari Maha Sabha, the petitioner before the High Court, argued that Tamil Nadu could not deny students access to free education through Navodaya schools."The Court should not get into this debate," Gupta said during the hearing.Justice Nagarathna responded: "That perception that you are surrendering to the central govt should not be there."

World.title: Govt debunks Pakistan claim that IAF MiG-29 crashed during landing due to pilot error
World.content:
NEW DELHI: The press information bureau (PIB) fact check unit on Thursday debunked a social media claim that an Indian Air Force (IAF) MiG-29 fighter jet had crashed during landing due to pilot error.

They stated that the video being circulated was footage from a video game.

The fact-checking unit warned that the video was being circulated by Pakistani propaganda accounts and called the claim fake.

âPakistani propaganda accounts are circulating a video with the claim that an IAF MiG-29 fighter jet crashed during landing due to pilot error,â PIB Fact Check said in a post on X, adding, âBeware! This claim is #Fake.â

Join conversation Commentsâ Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful Â· TOI community guidelines

The unit said the footage was from War Thunder, a military combat video game featuring aircraft, land and naval vehicles.

The video circulating on social media shows a fighter jet crashing while attempting to land, followed by the pilot ejecting and parachuting to safety. The footage was presented online as an actual IAF MiG-29 crash by certain accounts based out of Pakistan.

PIB Fact Check urged users to report suspicious content related to the Government of India through its official channels.

The claim is part of a recurring pattern of propagandist accounts circulating unrelated military accidents and video-game footage are circulated as evidence of recent events.

World.title: 'Tell your Chief Secretary not to invite orders’: SC pulls up Manipur over 25 unnatural deaths in relief camps
World.content:
NEW DELHI: The Supreme Court on Thursday directed the Manipur government to submit a comprehensive report on 25 unnatural deaths of internally displaced persons reported in relief camps during the 2023 ethnic violence, including an alleged sexual assault case.

A bench headed by Chief Justice of India Surya Kant and comprising Justices Joymalya Bagchi and V Mohana questioned the state over the limited number of post-mortem examinations conducted in the cases and the compensation paid to the families of the deceased.

The court directed the state to provide details of all 25 cases, including post-mortem reports and other documents establishing the causes of death.

âTell your Chief Secretary not to invite orders. Tell us what measures you have taken,â CJI Surya Kant remarked while questioning the Manipur Advocate General about information sought by the committee on July 4.

Supreme Court seeks details of deaths

The proceedings took place while the court was hearing petitions related to the investigation and trial of sexual violence cases arising from the 2023 Manipur ethnic violence.

The bench took note of a report submitted by a committee headed by former Jammu and Kashmir High Court Chief Justice Gita Mittal. The report referred to the deaths in relief camps and raised concerns regarding compensation.

The court sought an explanation from the state on why post-mortem examinations had reportedly been conducted in only 20 of the 25 cases and why the families had received compensation of only Rs 20,000 to Rs 30,000.





The report placed before the Supreme Court also referred to 640 deaths in relief camps across eight districts.

Directions on FIRs and relief camp conditions

The court directed the Manipur government to explain the remedial measures taken to protect the safety and dignity of internally displaced persons living in relief camps and to ensure adequate medical facilities and day-to-day necessities.

Join conversation Commentsâ Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful Â· TOI community guidelines

The Manipur Legal Services Authority was directed to immediately take up the issue and ensure registration of FIRs in all cases of unnatural deaths, proper ascertainment of the causes of death and expeditious investigation.

It was also directed to take measures for the protection of displaced persons and victims.

The Supreme Court's directions come against the backdrop of the ethnic violence that erupted in Manipur in May 2023, which led to deaths, displacement and allegations of sexual violence.

World.title: Congress MPs react to 'no dissent' report on MDR, say no proposal was ever brought before panel
World.content:
Join conversation View All Comments â Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful Â· TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: Congress on Thursday refuted the Centre's claim that five of its members supported the government's decision to introduce a merchant discount rate of 0.4% on UPI payments above Rs 2,000, saying that no such discussion took place during the Parliamentary Standing Committee meeting.In a social media post on X, Congress MP Gaurav Gogoi said that the department of finance did not have any specific proposal on UPI tax when it met members of the finance committee."The Parliament standing committee on finance has not discussed the UPI tax proposal that the Modi government has recently announced," Gogoi said."The department of finance did not have any specific proposal on UPI tax when they met the members of the finance committee. Questions were raised on the need for MDR but the representatives of the government did not have any specific or satisfactory answers at that point," he added.He reiterated the party's demand to roll back MDR on UPI and said, "I reiterate that the recent UPI tax policies hurt the small Indian merchants, vendors, entrepreneurs and help the major American corporations. Roll back UPI tax. Stop surrendering, PM Modi."Another Congress MP, Manish Tewari, backed Gogoi and accused the Centre of using the privileged proceedings of the Parliamentary Standing Committee to "score brownie points.""It is unfortunate that proceedings of Parliamentary Standing Committees that are supposed to be privileged are now sought to be used by the government to score brownie points," Tewari said in a social media post."My colleague is correct; no specific proposal qua the recent Merchant Discount Rate - MDR to be levied on UPI transactions from October 15th, 2026, was ever brought before the Parliamentary standing committee of Finance - rate, quantum, amount of fee to be charged, ceiling and exemption slabs, etc.," he added.He also said that concerns were raised by the Opposition over the need and efficacy of MDR on UPI payments during various sittings of the committee."Even on the principle or conceptual basis of MDR as my colleague Gaurav Gogoi points out concerns were raised by members with regard to its need, efficacy, etc., over the course of various sittings of the committee," Tewari said."To claim that a particular measure was supported by âcertain membersâ of the committee is an inaccurate and fallacious characterisation of the confidential proceedings of a Parliamentary Committee," he added.This comes a day after a government functionary claimed that Congress MPs, including former finance minister P Chidambaram and former minister in the UPA government Manish Tewari, supported the government's decision during the parliamentary panel's proceedings.âWhy is Rahul Gandhi opposing something his own MPs, including former finance minister P Chidambaram and former minister in the UPA government Manish Tewari, supported within the parliamentary panel?â news agency PTI reported a functionary as saying.According to the report of the standing committee headed by BJP MP Bhartruhari Mahtab, the panel noted its earlier recommendation emphasising that due to the imperative of a viable revenue model, legislative-enabling provisions for a tiered MDR structure have been brought forward.However, the committee remained deeply concerned by the staggering mismatch between the Rs 2,000-crore allocation and the industry's estimated operational cost of Rs 20,700 crore.In the view of the committee, while statutory enablement now exists to permit calibrated MDR on high-value transactions, any delay in notifying and operationalising this framework leaves payment service providers heavily dependent on inadequate subsidies, thereby threatening critical investments in cybersecurity, fraud prevention and network infrastructure.On the incentive scheme for promotion of RuPay debit cards and low-value BHIM-UPI transactions (person-to-merchant), the committee, in its report, observed and recommended: âThe Committee notes the massive Rs 2,000 crore budgetary allocation for 2026-27 designed to offset ecosystem costs caused by the zero-MDR policy on RuPay and low-value UPI transactions.âThe Committee observes that while UPI is expected to process up to 150 billion transactions per month and add 600 million new users, the current government incentive covers merely 11% of the industry's actual costs and 14% of potential MDR collections, creating a structural funding gap impacting long-term infrastructural investment.âThe committee recommended that while the proposed three-year multi-year scheme and cashback components are necessary to democratise digital payments in untapped Tier 3-6 cities, the Department of Financial Services must concurrently explore a self-reliant, tiered revenue model.

World.title: '9/11 architects were not hiding in caves': India hits out at Pakistan at UN over terror safe havens
World.content:
NEW DELHI: India on Wednesday hit out at Pakistan at the UN Security Council, saying Islamabad had provided a "permissive environment" to the "architects" of the 9/11 attacks and continues to provide space and support to terror groups such as Lashkar-e-Taiba and Jaish-e-Mohammed.

Speaking at a UN Security Council meeting, India's Permanent Representative P Harish recalled the 9/11 terror attacks in United States and said al-Qaida leaders Osama bin Laden and Khalid Sheikh Mohammed were eventually found in settled communities in Pakistan rather than "caves or badlands".

âThe international community supported the global campaign to counter terrorism in the wake of 9/11. Let us not forget, however, that al-Qaida's terror ecosystem established its strategic depth beyond Afghanistan through its affiliates,â Harish said.

âThe leaders of al-Qaida who conceived and directed these 9/11 attacks did not escape justice in the wilderness of some ungoverned frontier.â

The Indian envoy also listed out the names of terrorists found in Pakistan.

Bin Laden, who ordered and financed the 9/11 plot, was âtracked down and killed in a fortified compound within a settled, guarded community under Operation Neptune Spearâ, he said.

Mohammed, âthe principal architect of the operation, was found sheltering in an ordinary residential house.





Ramzi Binalshibh, who coordinated the hijacker cell after being denied a visa to join them, was sheltering in an urban centre,â Harish said.

Senior al-Qaida operative Walid bin Attash, who helped select and prepare several hijackers, was captured separately, while Mustafa Ahmed al-Hawsawi, a key financial and logistical facilitator of the 9/11 operation, was also captured in Pakistan, he said.

"In each case, these were not fugitives hiding in caves or badlands, they were men who had long evaded detection.

Draining this swamp that provided an enabling environment for such monsters of humankind to prosper is important," Harish said, in a thinly veiled reference to Pakistan.

Harish also drew attention to what he described as an axis involving Pakistan, al-Qaida and terrorists targeting India.

Join conversation Commentsâ Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful Â· TOI community guidelines

"The same permissive environment that sheltered the architects of 9/11 has, in the years since, continued to provide space, support, and impunity to affiliates of al Qaida such as Lashkar-e-Taiba and Jaish-e-Mohammed and their like," he said.

He said these groups continue to operate under different identities to evade the Council's sanctions, while their terror-training infrastructure continues to operate with impunity.

The international community must act against the continued existence of such sanctuaries, he said, "to ensure that more such individuals are not thrust upon any country or its citizens and no one loses family and loved ones".

Last week, as the world marked 25 years of the September 11 terror attacks perpetrated by al-Qaida, UN Security Council members, including Pakistan, visited the 9/11 memorial in Lower Manhattan.

World.title: Vishwakarma Puja: The Day Nobody Touched the Tools
World.content:
Idols of Lord Vishwakarma are on display for sale in Kolkata

Kites being bought

Bhadre rendhe, Ashwine khaoa

Ranna Puja ( File Image)

File Image

Nadia: An artisan works on an idol of Lord Vishwakarma ahead of 'Vishwakarma Puja', at a workshop, in Nadia, West Bengal. (PTI Photo)(PTI09_16_2026_000049B)

Join conversation View All Comments â Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful Â· TOI community guidelines

Sources/Reading:

Dipesh Chakrabarty, Rethinking Working-Class History: Bengal 1890â1940 (Princeton University Press, 1989)

Leela Fernandes, Producing Workers: The Politics of Gender, Class, and Culture in the Calcutta Jute Mills (University of Pennsylvania Press, 1997)

On Vishwakarma Puja, remembering a leather factory that honoured a Hindu god with Muslim hands participating and biryani from Park Street. Nobody thought it needed explaining.Few Hindu festivals can be entered in an office calendar years ahead without consulting a panjika, and Vishwakarma Puja, which falls today, is the most dependable of them, because it is pegged to Kanya Sankranti, the last day of Bhadra, a solar date rather than a lunar one, which is why it generally lands on September 17 every year.It seems only right that the god of engineers should keep better time than most gods.He is, by his rÃ©sumÃ©, the most accomplished contractor in the Hindu universe. Tradition credits him with Lord Krishna's Dwarka, the golden Lanka that Hanuman ji later set alight, the Pandava capital at Indraprastha and the chariots in which the gods flew. What is less remarked upon is how differently India has chosen to picture him. In the west and north-west he is an old, four-armed man with a white beard and a swan for a mount, which scholars read as a nod to Brahma; in the east he is a young, muscular man with a black moustache, no sons in attendance, and an elephant as his vahana, which suggests God Indra instead.West Bengal, a state with no shortage of bearded elders, decided that its engineer should look like a foreman in his prime, which tells you something about who was doing the worshipping.The flying chariots are how Bengal explains its kites, which dot Kolkata's skies on this day. Hindu mythology is full of gods travelling by air, and Vishwakarma is held to have built the vehicles. The skies over Kolkata on this day used to (and perhaps still do to a lesser extent) fill with petkati and chandiyal, and the morning began with the cry of bhokatta from some rooftop where a boy had just cut a rival's string.Held on the last day of Bhadra, the puja also opens the long Sharodiya season, so the kites were, in effect, the city's first announcement that Maa Durga was on her way. In many Bengali homes the day carries a second observance that has nothing to do with machines. Arandhan, tied to Manasa Puja at Bhadra Sankranti, requires that food be cooked the night before and eaten stale the next day, with cooking itself forbidden; the custom has loosened with modern life but survives in Bengal's villages and in Kolkata's suburbs. The folk phrase for it,â cook in Bhadra and eat in Ashwin â is as good a summary as any.The puja's real home, though, was never the household. It is observed mostly on factory floors, where workers pray for safe conditions and for their machines to run well, and shrines go up among the tools themselves. Historians studying Kolkata's working class have argued that this was something the workers made their own; Dipesh Chakrabarty wrote about festivals as a source of solidarity inside hostile workplaces, and Leela Fernandes's ethnography of the jute mills treated the building of Vishwakarma pandals as a space of the workers' cultural autonomy.The leather factory: My family's business was a leather factory on Tiljala Road, right behind Don Bosco School, and on this day the more than four hundred men who worked there, nearly all of them Muslim, did not touch their tools. The work that honoured the god had been done the day before, when the craftsmen who spent the rest of the year shaping leather goods turned to sheets of coloured paper instead, cutting out decorations with a skill that matched their day jobs and a gusto that suggested they found paper the more forgiving material. Everything the day required was prepared on the eve, and on the day itself the hands rested.By the time the priest arrived, the god of craftsmen was presiding over a room that craftsmen, most of whom did not pray to him, had dressed for him. I have never been sure how much of the abstention was reverence and how much was the ordinary pleasure of a working day on which no work was expected, and I suspect the men themselves would have found the question tiresome, which is perhaps the point.Then there was lunch. Many factory feasts on the day were vegetarian, a mutton curry being the mark of the more generous units, and ours had apparently decided that gastronomy in this feast was a competitive sport and opted for biryani. The biryani came from Shiraz on Park Street, which opened in 1941 at the Park Street and Mullick Bazar crossing, specialising in Awadhi food, founded by Mohammed Arshad Ali and Ali Hussain, who had come to Calcutta from Bihar. Calcutta's biryani, as every Calcuttan will tell you at length, came down from Awadh with Wajid Ali Shah's exile, and Shiraz's cook Shamsuddin, who joined in the 1970s and reworked its biryani, is said to have had an ancestor who cooked for the nawab.Consider the arrangement then. A feast for the Hindu god of craft, cooked to a deposed Muslim king's recipe by a kitchen that claims descent from his, eaten by four hundred Muslim leatherworkers and one Bengali Hindu family, on a day when the stoves in half of Bengal's kitchens were not supposed to be lit. The factory had solved Arandhan by outsourcing it to a Park Street restaurant, and nobody, as far as I remember, felt the need to hold a seminar about it. (We'd hold a good many seminars or news channel debates now.)The next morning the god went into the waters of the Hooghly, and the men went back to their benches. The tools, having been worshipped for a day, went back to being worked, which is, if you think about it, the only form of worship a tool has ever asked for.

World.title: Kerala State Women’s Commission raises concerns on safety of elderly women
World.content:
Ensuring the safety and social protection of elderly women remains a major challenge for society, Kerala State Women’s Commission chairperson P. Sathidevi has said.

Addressing a district-level sitting of the commission at the Kozhikode Collectorate conference hall on Wednesday (September 16, 2026), Ms. Sathidevi said a majority of the complaints considered at the sitting were related to family disputes.

She said elderly women were often being abandoned by their families after receiving their share of property. “Women face severe isolation in old age when they need love and care,” she said, adding that such a situation was not healthy for society.

Even women who were financially secure often lacked social protection in their old age, she said. Cyberattacks targeting women were also on the rise, while women living alone faced serious security concerns.

Ms. Sathidevi said children growing up in households where parents were constantly in conflict were increasingly losing family and social values. Women also faced security threats within their own families owing to the use of alcohol and drugs by men, she said.

She further criticised that when women approached law enforcement agencies seeking implementation of court orders under the Protection of Women from Domestic Violence Act, their complaints were sometimes dismissed as mere “family issues.”

Of the 50 complaints considered at the sitting, six were settled. One complaint was referred for legal assistance, while reports from the police and other department officials were sought in connection with six complaints. Commission members P. Kunhayisha and A. Jamini also attended the sitting.

World.title: Protesters place puppies on official's table to highlight stray dog menace
World.content:
A protest over the growing stray-dog menace in Maharashtra’s Nashik district took an unusual turn when the protesters brought two puppies into a municipal office and released them on the chief officer’s table.

A viral video of the incident on Wednesday (September 16, 2026) shows Shiv Sena (UBT) district youth wing functionary Vikram Randhave pulling out the dogs from two sacks and placing them on the table Dheeraj Bhamre, chief officer of the Niphad Nagar Panchayat.

“We have been trying to highlight the stray dog menace to you since the last six months, but you ignored our pleas,” Mr. Randhave is seen telling the stunned official, who informs him that the civic body has already issued work tenders to deal with the stray dog menace.

“If you fail to act, we will bring more dogs to your office next time. We will also bring children and women affected by the problem,” Mr. Randhave said, announcing the sequel to this “who let the dogs out” drama.

Mr. Randhave also placed a garland made of currency notes around the chief officer’s table to protest the civic administration’s handling of the issue.

He claimed that more than 400 stray dogs roam the Nagar Panchayat limits and that over 100 residents suffer dog-bite injuries every month.

The stray dog menace has affected children, senior citizens and motorists, he said, adding that victims have to undergo painful treatment after being bitten.

It was not clear if Mr. Randhave had his party’s backing behind the protest.

Carrying two sacks, a group of Yuva Sena (UBT) members barged into the office of Bhamre. They said that despite repeated requests, the authorities have not taken any action to control the stray dog menace.

Dogs have bitten several citizens and pose an even greater risk to the public, especially children, during the ongoing Ganesh festival, Mr. Randhave said.

An official at Niphad police station told PTI that a case has been registered against Mr. Randhave and others for obstructing the public servant in the discharge of his official duty.

Asked if any action would be taken against Mr. Randhave over the way in which he handled the dogs, packing them into the sacks and dumping them on the table, the official said a case has also been registered in that regard.

No arrests have been made so far, he said.

World.title: Andhra saw the El Niño drought coming in February, farmers still lost ₹20,000 an acre: Jagan
World.content:
Farmers in Andhra Pradesh who took up cultivation on the government’s assurances have lost ₹15,000 to more than ₹20,000 an acre and have been left without the protection of free crop insurance, YSR Congress Party (YSRCP) president and former Chief Minister Y.S. Jagan Mohan Reddy alleged on Thursday (September 17, 2026), blaming the State government’s failure to take timely preventive measures for aggravating the drought.

Addressing a video conference with party leaders, Mr. Jagan Mohan Reddy said the State was facing not merely an El Niño effect but a “yellow nino effect” (hinting at the colour of the TDP flag), alleging that the government had failed to respond adequately despite being aware of the possibility of deficient rainfall.

He said Chief Minister N. Chandrababu Naidu had warned as early as February 4 about the possibility of an El Niño impact, but “the action taken thereafter was zero”.

Mr. Jagan criticised the government for allegedly failing to declare drought-affected mandals despite rainfall deficiency in June, July and August. He said Karnataka had declared drought in advance, but the Andhra Pradesh government had failed to do so.

He alleged that the government had not prepared alternative seeds, supplied fodder to districts or sought additional workdays under the Mahatma Gandhi National Rural Employment Guarantee Scheme despite the emerging drought conditions.

On irrigation, Mr. Jagan alleged that water from Srisailam was not released to Rayalaseema when it could have been made available and was instead released for power generation. He also alleged that the State government had remained silent while Telangana was constructing lift irrigation schemes upstream and downstream of Pulichintala.

He criticised the government over the Polavaram project, alleging that it was compromising on the project’s full reservoir level and, with it, the State’s intended water-storage capacity.

Mr. Jagan also alleged that the existing Pushkara and Purushothapatnam lift schemes were being operated and presented as new initiatives. He accused the government of “staging dramas in the name of lift schemes” while allegedly giving up storage capacity at Polavaram.

World.title: Fire and rescue force’s swift response to emergencies its biggest strength: Keralam Home Minister Ramesh Chennithala
World.content:
Describing the Kerala Fire and Rescue Services as one of the State’s most respected frontline forces, Home Minister Ramesh Chennithala said its greatest strength was the speed with which its personnel respond when lives are at risk.

The Minister was speaking after receiving the salute at a joint passing-out parade of Fire and Rescue Services officers as well as trainees from the Puducherry Fire Service at the Kerala Fire and Rescue Services Academy in Viyyur, Thrissur, on Thursday (September 17, 2026).

When an accident strikes and people are gripped by panic, the fire and rescue personnel are often the first to reach the scene and turn into lifesavers, he said. Their ability to respond swiftly and intervene without delay remains the force’s biggest strength.

‘Source of hope’

The uniform, he said, represents the readiness to enter places others cannot reach and is a source of hope and courage for people in distress.

The force was renamed the Fire and Rescue Services to reflect its wider mandate of saving lives not only during fires but also during natural disasters and other emergencies, the Minister said.

He urged the newly trained personnel to put to effective use the knowledge, skills, confidence and discipline acquired during their training throughout their careers. The force has a critical role in leading rescue operations during accidents, disasters and other emergencies, he said.

Mr. Chennithala also stressed the need to make effective use of modern technology and equipment to enhance the efficiency of rescue operations.

A total of 141 trainees participated in the joint passing-out parade held at the academy parade ground. They included 74 newly trained fire and rescue officers and 16 fire and rescue officers (drivers) from Keralam, besides 39 trainees of the 10th External Fireman Course and 12 trainees of the 11th External Fireman Driver-cum-Pump Operator Course from the Puducherry Fire Service.

Special emphasis

The trainees underwent intensive practical and technical training in firefighting, rescue operations, handling emergencies, operating rescue equipment, firefighting techniques and disaster management. Physical fitness, discipline and a spirit of service were also given special emphasis.

The new batch included candidates with a wide range of educational qualifications. Among the 141 trainees were three postgraduates in MA, two in MCom and three in MSc, besides one each with MCA, MEd and MSW qualifications. The batch also included 26 BA and BCom graduates each, 22 BSc graduates, 20 BTech graduates, six BCA graduates, seven diploma holders, seven ITI-qualified candidates and 16 Plus Two holders.

MLA Rajan J. Pallan; Kerala Fire and Rescue Services, Civil Defence and Home Guards Director General Balram Kumar Upadhyay; Fire and Rescue Services Director (Administration) Arun Alphonse; Thrissur Range DIG T. Narayanan; Kerala Police Academy Director IG K. Sethuraman; Thrissur City District Police Chief Nakul Rajendra Deshmukh; Thrissur Rural District Police Chief Mohammed Nadeemuddin; and academy Assistant Directors M.S. Suvi and Ashraf Ali were among those present.

Academy Assistant Director S.L. Dileep administered the oath to the trainees.

The Kerala Fire and Rescue Services Academy provides basic, in-service and external training, with a focus on modern firefighting and rescue technologies and hands-on skills. By training personnel from different States and Union Territories, the academy has also emerged as a national-level training centre for fire and rescue services.

World.title: E.M. Sudarsana Natchiappan, former Union Minister and senior Congress leader, passes away at 78
World.content:
Senior Congress leader and former Union Minister E.M. Sudarsana Natchiappan passed away at his residence in Sivaganga on Thursday (September 17, 2026). He was 78, and is survived by his wife, daughter, two sons, and two elder brothers.

Tamil Nadu Congress Committee (TNCC) president Manickam Tagore, a nephew of Natchiappan, said his uncle had died in his sleep. “When he did not get up in the morning, his driver went to his room, only to find he was no more,” he told The Hindu.

A Congressman since 1969, Natchiappan rose through the ranks from his early days as the Singampunari Regional Youth Congress president to become the vice-president of the TNCC in 2002. He also served as the party whip in Parliament.

Student leader

Born in Eriyur in Sivaganga district, Natchiappan was active in the Students’ Congress while studying at the Law College. “Later, he worked in the Youth Congress and became its general secretary. He was elected chairman of the Sivaganga Panchayat Union in the 1986 local body elections, which showcased a lot of talented Congress leaders in Tamil Nadu,” Mr. Tagore said.

After practising law in Sivaganga, Natchiappan shifted his practice to the Madras High Court in 1991 and to the Supreme Court in 1995.

A staunch Congress loyalist and admirer of former Prime Minister Indira Gandhi and Congress leader Sonia Gandhi, Natchiappan remained with the Congress when the late G.K. Moopanar launched the Tamil Maanila Congress (TMC) in 1996 in protest against the Congress high command’s decision to align with the AIADMK.

Victory in 1999 LS polls

Before making his mark in national politics, he gained widespread attention in the 1999 Lok Sabha elections by winning the Sivaganga parliamentary seat against senior Congress leader P. Chidambaram when the latter was in the TMC.

After Mr. Chidambaram returned to the Congress, Natchiappan could not secure the Sivaganga Lok Sabha constituency again. He was later nominated to the Rajya Sabha by party leader Sonia Gandhi and represented the House for two terms. He served as the Congress Lok Sabha member from the Sivaganga constituency from 1999 to 2004 and as a Rajya Sabha member from 2004 to 2016.

He also served as Union Minister of State for Commerce and Industry for a brief period between 2013 and 2014. He made significant contributions as chairman of the Parliamentary Standing Committee on Personnel, Public Grievances, Law and Justice between 2004 and 2009.

Natchiappan, an expert in the Sri Lankan Tamils issue, fishermen’s rights, and the Katchatheevu islet, had addressed the United Nations General Assembly on two occasions.

He had been receiving medical care for his declining health in Sivaganga for the past few days, but passed away at his residence after the treatment proved unsuccessful.

World.title: Congress rejects claim that party MPs backed UPI fee
World.content:
The Congress on Thursday (September 17, 2026) accused the Modi government of trying to use the proceedings of a Parliamentary Standing Committee to defend its decision to impose a Merchant Discount Rate on high-value UPI transactions, saying the specific proposal had neither been placed before nor endorsed by the panel.

The Opposition party’s response came after the government sought to cite the Finance Committee’s earlier deliberations on the Merchant Discount Rate, and the presence of Congress MPs when its report was adopted, to counter the political backlash over the new UPI charges. Discussions on the broad principle of a Merchant Discount Rate could not be construed as approval of the measure announced by the government, the Congress said.

The government was seeking to divert attention from the opposition to the new charges, Congress general secretary Jairam Ramesh said.

“These are pathetic attempts being made by the Modi Govt to divert attention away from the gigantic backlash generated after the UPI tax decision taken to appease US companies & Donaldbhai,” Mr. Ramesh said in a post on social media platform X.

It was “unfortunate” that the proceedings of parliamentary committees, which are privileged, were being used by the government to “score brownie points”, Congress MP Manish Tewari said. No specific proposal relating to the Merchant Discount Rate announced for UPI transactions from October 15 — including the rate, quantum, fee, ceiling, or exemption slabs — had been placed before the committee, he said.

Members had also raised concerns over the need and efficacy of the Merchant Discount Rate during the committee’s deliberations, Mr. Tewari said. To describe the measure as having been supported by “certain members”, he said, was an “inaccurate and fallacious characterisation” of confidential committee proceedings.

The Finance Committee had not discussed the UPI proposal recently announced by the government, Congress’s deputy leader in the Lok Sabha Gaurav Gogoi said. “The Department of Finance did not have any specific proposal on UPI tax when they met the members of the Finance Committee,” Mr. Gogoi said.

Questions had been raised about the need for the Merchant Discount Rate, but government representatives had not provided specific or satisfactory answers at the time, he added. Mr. Gogoi reiterated the Congress’s demand for withdrawal of the policy, saying it would hurt small merchants, vendors, and entrepreneurs while benefiting major American corporations.

World.title: Why construct new Secretariat complex when T.N. is facing financial crisis, Palaniswami asks TVK govt.
World.content:
AIADMK general secretary Edappadi K. Palaniswami has yet again expressed his opposition to the TVK government’s move to construct a new Secretariat-Assembly complex at Pattinapakkam in Chennai.

Speaking to reporters in Madurai on Thursday (September 17, 2026), the former Chief Minister pointed to the “huge borrowings” made by the TVK government since it came to power in May, 2026, and alleged: “In just the first four months, the new government has borrowed ₹40,000 crore. If this is the financial position of the State, then why is the TVK government planning to construct a new Secretariat building now?”

Mr. Palaniswami said that after setting right the State’s financial crisis, the government should choose a different site for the new Secretariat, which would not adversely affect people and create traffic congestion. “The government should reconsider the Pattinapakkam site, where the fishing community lives. There are schools located there, and the area generally witnesses a lot of traffic jams,” he said.

On power crisis

Mr. Palaniswami further said that while Energy Resources Minister C.T.R. Nirmal Kumar has been “denying” the fact that there were frequent power cuts in the State under the TVK rule, an additional 2,000 MW of electricity was being procured from the open market to mitigate Tamil Nadu’s power shortage. “Hiding these facts will not help the government solve the power crisis; it should instead take constructive steps,” Mr. Palaniswami said.

‘Bypolls forced on people’

On the Madras High Court expressing concern over MLAs resigning from political parties and re-contesting the upcoming bypolls on behalf of other parties, Mr. Palaniswami said that the bye-elections in Madurantakam and Dharapuram were “forced upon the people of Tamil Nadu.”

“The TVK had brought the two AIADMK MLAs [who are now candidates in the bypolls] into its fold through horse-trading and forced them to resign against the will of the voters of those constituencies,” he said. Even the Left parties that are supporting the TVK government have flayed this, he added.

Debunking the claim of the TVK of having provided a corruption-free administration, Mr. Palaniswami said that several lakhs of rupees have been seized by the DVAC during its raids from various government offices in the past few months, proving that corruption has actually risen under the TVK regime.

Pointing to the abduction of an elderly trader in Tenkasi district, the AIADMK leader said that the law and order situation in the State has deteriorated. The government has also failed to contain the price hike of foodgrains, and the general public is badly hit, he added.

World.title: Thunderstorm forecast in 25 Telangana districts on September 18
World.content:
The India Meteorological Department (IMD) has issued a thunderstorm forecast in 25 Telangana districts for Friday, September 18.

According to IMDs latest bulletin, thunderstorms accompanied with lightning and gusty winds are very likely to occur at isolated places in Adilabad, Kumaram Bheem Asifabad, Mancherial, Nirmal, Nizamabad, Jagtial, Rajanna Sircilla, Karimnagar, Peddapalli, Jayashankar Bhupalpally, Mulugu, Suryapet, Mahabubabad, Warangal, Hanumakonda, Jangaon, Siddipet, Rangareddy, Hyderabad, Medchal Malkajgiri, Vikarabad, Sangareddy, Medak, Kamareddy and Mahabubnagar districts.

Hyderabad city and its surrounding areas for the next 24 hours will see a partly cloudy sky. “Light rain or thundershowers accompanied with gusty winds are very likely to occur in parts of the city towards evening or night. The maximum and minimum temperatures are likely to be around 34℃ and 26℃ respectively,” the bulletin said.

World.title: SC suspends Imaan, Hadi's sentences in controversial social media posts case, orders their release
World.content:
ISLAMABAD: The Supreme Court on Thursday suspended the sentences of human rights lawyer Imaan Zainab Mazari-Hazir and her spouse, Hadi Ali Chattha, in the controversial social media posts case.

The development came as a two-judge SC bench, comprising Justice Naeem Akhtar Afghan and Justice Ishtiaq Ibrahim, took up the couple’s appeals against the Islamabad High Court’s (IHC) refusal in February to suspend the sentences.

On January 24, an Islamabad sessions court sentenced Imaan and Hadi to a total of 17 years in jail on multiple charges under the Prevention of Electronic Crimes Act (Peca). The convictions of the couple, who had already been jailed the day before in a separate case, were widely condemned by lawyers and United Nations (UN) experts .

On Thursday, the SC ordered the couple’s release after granting them bail against surety bonds of Rs200,000. It ordered their release on bail pending the IHC’s final verdict.

“Both are lawyers and we are keeping their honour,” observed Justice Afghan, but also asked senior counsel Faisal Siddiqui, the couple’s lawyer, to tell the appellants to observe the court’s decorum.

“There is a difference between a lawyer and an ordinary person,” the judge observed.
